title: Hybrid Aerospace Solar Photovoltaic-Thermoelectric Architecture with Advanced Thermal Regulation
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Project Title: Hybrid Aerospace Solar Photovoltaic-Thermoelectric Architecture with Advanced Thermal Regulation Creator / Author: Ahmad Wildan Wasim bin Ahmad Firdaus Project Overview & Problem Statement: Standard solar cells operating in a
content: Project Title: Hybrid Aerospace Solar Photovoltaic-Thermoelectric Architecture with Advanced Thermal Regulation Creator / Author: Ahmad Wildan Wasim bin Ahmad Firdaus Project Overview & Problem Statement: Standard solar cells operating in aerospace environments face a severe performance bottleneck: increased thermal absorption causes panel temperatures to rise, which drastically degrades electrical efficiency. Real-world baseline performance typically operates at an efficiency of ~20%, with un-harvested high-energy Blue and UV wavelengths contributing to a thermal waste load of >50%, and surface reflection accounting for a 5–10% energy loss. Furthermore, conventional single-junction silicon cells are mathematically capped by the Shockley-Queisser limit at roughly 33.7% efficiency. To overcome these fundamental limits, this architecture introduces a novel hybrid tandem system engineered exclusively for aerospace and deep-space missions. It is explicitly designated as not for standard terrestrial use on Earth and must operate in the vacuum/darkness environment of space to leverage proper radiative cooling. By stacking a high-bandgap Perovskite cell over a low-bandgap Monocrystalline CIGS cell, the architecture strategically bypasses the single-junction limit. The design is further enhanced to harvest unused solar wavelengths (such as high-energy Blue/UV light and sub-bandgap Infrared (IR) light) and channel that accumulated thermal waste downward into a continuously packed thermoelectric layer, converting a steep thermal gradient directly into extra Open-Circuit Voltage (Voc). Complete Core Architecture & Layer Stack (From Top to Bottom) 1. Optical Optimization & Concentrator Array Anti-Reflective Coating: A top Magnesium Fluoride (MgF2) layer to minimize photon reflection and maximize transmission. Concentration Optics: Micro-lenses or Fresnel lens arrays configured for a 500x geometric concentration ratio to maximize photon flux and deliver a massive boost to the Open-Circuit Voltage (Voc). 2. Advanced Tandem Photovoltaic Core Full Multi-Junction Chemical Stack Configuration: The core PV engine is structurally synthesized as an integrated monolithic tandem device following the precise chemical interface sequence: (Cs0.05(MA0.17FA0.83)0.95Pb(I0.83Br0.17)3 / Cu(In,Ga)Se2 / Ge) Top Absorber Layer: A high-stability, triple-cation Perovskite layer with the chemical formula: Cs0.05(MA0.17FA0.83)0.95Pb(I0.83Br0.17)3. (Design Note: For extreme thermal environments under 500x concentration, substitution with fully inorganic alternatives like CsPbI3 may be implemented to prevent organic outgassing). Charge Transport Infrastructure & Quantum Sheet: Optimized Electron Transport Layers (ETL) and Hole Transport Layers (HTL). The ETL incorporates an n-µc-SiGe:H (hydrogenated microcrystalline silicon-germanium) layer to reduce interface resistance, and transitions into a specialized Schottky junction configured as a 1–2V High Field Sheet utilizing Dirac Material

title: Applications of Radioactive Isotopes in Nuclear Medicine: Diagnosis and Cancer Treatment
source: Journal of Sustainable Smart Systems in Education & Environment
summary: The application of radioisotopes in nuclear medicine represents a modern technology that significantly impacts diagnosis and treatment, particularly in cancer care. In diagnosis, the use of radioisotopes for imaging organs and tumors involv
content: The application of radioisotopes in nuclear medicine represents a modern technology that significantly impacts diagnosis and treatment, particularly in cancer care. In diagnosis, the use of radioisotopes for imaging organs and tumors involves small quantities injected into the body to show regions of high biological activity, enabling one to accurately determine the positions of tumors. These include "iodine-131" and "technetium-99", which are commonly used for imaging the thyroid and heart, respectively. In this way, such images reveal to the doctor the functions of organs and allow him to assess the extent of tumor spread, thereby contributing to an accurate treatment plan. The therapeutic applications in treatment depend on the targeting of cancerous cells with specific dosages of radiation using selected radioactive isotopes. Radiation destroys either the cancer cells or shrinks tumors, while there is minimal injury to the healthy body tissue. Iodine-131 is applied in treatments for thyroid cancer, whereas lutetium-177 and radium-223 are other radioactive isotopes used in treatments for bone tumors and prostate cancer, respectively. These treatments allow radiation to be focused precisely at the diseased cells, which offers a greater efficacy in treatment with a lesser set of side effects that may arise from the use of more conventional forms of radiation therapy. Nuclear medicine can thereby create a bright future in improving the survival rates and lifestyles of patients. Simultaneously, it will contribute to offering avant-garde therapeutic solutions that also include consideration for individuality in treatment. With further development in this field, radio-isotope applications are envisaged to expand and bring up new frontiers for diagnosis and treatment in the future.

title: Interconnected pore networks as a unifying framework for transport in dense polymer membranes
source: Frontiers in Membrane Science and Technology
summary: Transport in many dense polymer membranes used for reverse osmosis, organic solvent nanofiltration, pervaporation, and gas separation has traditionally been interpreted through the solution–diffusion model, which treats the membrane as a de
content: Transport in many dense polymer membranes used for reverse osmosis, organic solvent nanofiltration, pervaporation, and gas separation has traditionally been interpreted through the solution–diffusion model, which treats the membrane as a dense, nonporous polymer phase where molecules dissolve and diffuse under concentration gradients. Although this framework has been useful for correlating membrane performance, its mechanistic foundation for water and solvent transport is contradicted by current experimental and molecular simulation evidence. Observations from positron annihilation lifetime spectroscopy, scattering methods, spectroscopic probes, and molecular dynamics simulations demonstrate that polymer membranes, long considered dense and nonporous, contain interconnected (sub)nanometer free-volume networks rather than isolated transient cavities. These molecular pathways provide a more physically grounded basis for interpreting transport across diverse membrane processes. Here, we synthesize recent experimental and molecular simulation evidence to establish interconnected pore networks as a unifying mechanistic framework for transport across major classes of dense polymer membranes. In pressure-driven liquid separations, solvent transport is governed by pressure-driven viscous flow through interconnected, solvent-filled pore networks. In pervaporation, liquid-like and vapor-like domains coexist within the membrane, indicating an internal phase transition rather than evaporation only at the downstream surface. In glassy gas-separation polymer membranes, permeability and selectivity are governed by pore connectivity, molecular sieving, and gas–wall interactions. Together, these insights shift membrane design from optimizing empirical solubility and diffusivity parameters toward engineering pore size, connectivity, tortuosity, and pore-wall chemistry.

title: Effects of Vermicompost on Sugarcane Productivity and Soil Carbon Accumulation
summary: Background and Objective: The application of vermicompost in sugarcane cultivation leads to an increase sugarcane yield by enhancing soil nutrient content, cane growth and boosting soil carbon accumulation as well as through enrichment of s
content: Background and Objective: The application of vermicompost in sugarcane cultivation leads to an increase sugarcane yield by enhancing soil nutrient content, cane growth and boosting soil carbon accumulation as well as through enrichment of soil fertility.This study investigates the impact of vermicompost application on sugarcane productivity and soil carbon accumulation.It aims to determine how vermicompost influences crop yield, soil fertility, and carbon sequestration, providing insights into sustainable sugarcane cultivation practices.Materials and Methods: The field experiment was conducted on over four cropping seasons.The soil of the area was silt loam and moderate fertility.The experiment followed a Randomized Complete Block Design (RCBD) with eight treatments combining different rates of vermicompost and chemical fertilizers.Results revealed that the highest sugarcane yield of 143.40 t/ha was found in T 4 treatment where vermicompost @ 5 t/ha along with N 180 P 40 K 90 S 45 Mg 10 Zn 4 kg/ha was applied.Soil organic carbon and carbon stock were also substantially improved by vermicompost application, with the highest carbon accumulation of 1.82 t/ha was observed in T 4 .Results: The trends of increased yield in sugarcane of 69%>62%>45%>34% in the cropping year of 2020-2021, 2019-2020, 2021-2022 and 2022-2023, respectively where the integrated use of vermicompost at 5 t/ha along with inorganic fertilizers of N 180 P 40 K 90 S 45 Mg 10 Zn 4 kg/ha.In 2022-2023 cropping season, the highest level of carbon storing or accumulation of 95% was occurred where incorporation of vermicompost at 5 t/ha along with in organic fertilizers of N 180 P 40 K 90 S 45 Mg 10 Zn 4 kg/ha were applied.Conclusion: The application of vermicompost with the recommended dose of fertilizer significantly increased tiller number, millable cane count, and overall yield across all cropping years but sugar quality measured by Brix percentage did not show any significant variation among treatments.Overall, the use of vermicompost in combination with chemical fertilizers enhanced sugarcane productivity that contributed to soil carbon accumulation, supporting its role in sustainable crop production.

title: Estimating Annual Wildfire-Related Potential Above-Ground Biomass Loss in Eastern Canadian Boreal Forests Using Multi-Source Remote Sensing and XGBoost
summary: Wildfire impact assessment requires information on both burned areas and the biomass exposed within burned landscapes. We developed a field-calibrated, multi-source remote-sensing framework to estimate above-ground biomass (AGB) and quantif
content: Wildfire impact assessment requires information on both burned areas and the biomass exposed within burned landscapes. We developed a field-calibrated, multi-source remote-sensing framework to estimate above-ground biomass (AGB) and quantify annual wildfire-related potential AGB exposure across the boreal forests of Quebec and Ontario, Canada, during 2018–2024. The dataset comprised 3725 plot-year AGB observations linked to optical, Sentinel-1 C-band, ALOS L-band synthetic aperture radar, environmental, and geographic predictors. Product-wise screening reduced the 91 candidate predictors to 28. An optimized extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model was evaluated using five-fold grouped cross-validation, with repeated observations from each plot assigned to a single fold. The model achieved an RMSE of 25.08 ± 0.36 t ha−1, an MAE of 20.89 ± 0.39 t ha−1, and an R2 of 0.53 ± 0.02. The full multi-source configuration outperformed all reduced-source and source-only configurations, while removing ALOS L-band SAR or environmental/geographic predictors produced among the largest performance declines. The model was applied to 9937 land-cover-stratified points within wildfire polygons using predictors from the year preceding each fire. Under the complete-loss assumption, cumulative potential AGB exposure was 269.20 Mt across 6.66 Mha of effective burned area, with a 95% bootstrap interval of 254.19–284.06 Mt reflecting finite-point sampling uncertainty and an area-weighted mean exposure intensity of 40.43 t ha−1. The 2023 fire season accounted for 206.44 Mt, representing 76.7% of cumulative exposure and 73.2% of effective burned area. Effective burned area and total potential exposure were strongly correlated (r = 0.99), whereas exposure intensity followed a distinct pattern and peaked in 2022 at 46.86 t ha−1. Thus, burned area was the primary correlate of regional potential biomass exposure, whereas exposure intensity reflected variation in pre-fire biomass among burned landscapes. These estimates represent potential exposure rather than measured combustion, mortality, or carbon emissions and demonstrate the value of integrating spatially explicit pre-fire AGB with wildfire perimeters.

title: Solar solutions to double dividends: Examining the impact of China's photovoltaic poverty alleviation pilot on pollution and carbon emissions from county-level cities
summary: Understanding whether renewable energy programs with social objectives can generate joint pollution and carbon benefits is important for assessing their broader environmental value. This study evaluates China's Photovoltaic Poverty Alleviat
content: Understanding whether renewable energy programs with social objectives can generate joint pollution and carbon benefits is important for assessing their broader environmental value. This study evaluates China's Photovoltaic Poverty Alleviation Pilot (PPAP) using panel data for 2594 counties from 2010 to 2023 and a multi-period difference-in-differences design, supplemented by heterogeneity-robust estimators. PPAP reduces county-level pollution and carbon intensity. County innovation capacity and household wealth accumulation may help unlock the environmental potential. The NEBP analysis finds more evident environmental gains in counties with favorable solar conditions and moderate slopes, as well as in poverty-stricken counties. Higher information and stronger local governance capacity are also associated with more pronounced environmental benefits. These findings support regionally differentiated policy expansion that aligns project deployment with local resource conditions and implementation capacity. More broadly, PPAP offers lessons for linking poverty alleviation with low-carbon rural development in less-developed areas.

title: Financial guarantees for humanitarian energy: examples, incentives and disincentives
summary: Key messages: • Access to and provision of energy in humanitarian settings requires complete transformation. Access is severely inadequate, and the limited sources available are carbon intensive. Most forcibly displaced people lack access t
content: Key messages: • Access to and provision of energy in humanitarian settings requires complete transformation. Access is severely inadequate, and the limited sources available are carbon intensive. Most forcibly displaced people lack access to modern and clean energy sources. Humanitarian operations rely heavily on diesel, creating high costs, emissions, and operational inefficiencies. • Though private-sector finance is essential for such transformation, investors are put off by high perceived risks in humanitarian settings. Refugee contexts are seen as impermanent, and refugees are viewed as having low-credit worthiness – despite the long-term nature of many refugee communities, clear and growing demand, and strong evidence of very high repayment rates. • Some evidence suggests that financial guarantees can work effectively for humanitarian organizations. However, the viability for refugee households and businesses remains a question because of a lack of studies. Financial sustainability is a challenge, and the full economy of guaranteed investments is still unclear. • Enhancing understanding the potential impacts of financial guarantees for humanitarian energy requires targeted research. Analysis should examine the commercial viability of such mechanisms and how the finance system for refugee energy may become self-sustaining. Most mechanisms remain donor dependent. Guarantees are typically packaged with subsidized fees and grant-financed technical assistance, so the full cost of market-building must be accounted for alongside the guarantee itself.

title: Metal oxide-based sensors for volatile organic compound detection: A systematic review
summary: Metal oxide-based sensors have gained popularity as a platform for volatile organic compound (VOC) detection because of their sensitive, simple, and miniaturised sensing system compatibility and use; however, the latest progress in material
content: Metal oxide-based sensors have gained popularity as a platform for volatile organic compound (VOC) detection because of their sensitive, simple, and miniaturised sensing system compatibility and use; however, the latest progress in materials engineering and sensor architectures has led to a fragmented and thematically diverse body of research, which needs to be systematically consolidated. This systematic literature review (SLR) attempts to critically discuss the recent state-of-the-art developments in metal oxide-based VOC sensors, with a special focus on material design strategies and advanced sensing platforms. The review was carried out following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) protocol, based on structured and advanced search strategies conducted on the Web of Science and Scopus databases. The keywords of the search were “metal oxide,” “sensor,” “volatile organic compound,” and “manufacturing,” and the inclusion criteria were peer-reviewed journal articles, limited to articles published between 2023 and 2025. Following the process of duplicate removal, screening, and eligibility assessment, a total of 39 primary studies were identified for in-depth qualitative synthesis. The literature analysed indicates that there are three prevailing research themes, namely: (i) defect engineering, phase control, and crystal structure modulation of metal oxide sensing materials, which are strongly involved in charge transport and gas–surface interactions; (ii) heterostructures and heterojunctions, and functionalised hybrid sensors, which enhance sensitivity, selectivity, and operational stability through interfacial engineering; and (iii) advanced device architectures, data-driven optimisation, and intelligent sensing, which enable improved reliability, real-time monitoring, and deployment in practice. If put together, all these themes demonstrate the fact that the trend has shifted towards more material-oriented optimisation of unified sensor systems with sophisticated data processing schemes. The present review can provide a clear thematic framework upon which one can comprehend the current direction of research, the emerging trends, as well as critical issues that will provide valuable detail on upcoming innovation and construction of advanced VOC sensing technology with the help of metal oxides.

title: Rapid change of limiting nutrient in the Gulf of Bothnia, northern Baltic Sea
summary: Historically, phosphorus has been considered the limiting nutrient for primary production in the northern Baltic Sea, whereas further south in the Baltic Proper nitrogen is the limiting nutrient. In this study, we investigated the nutrient
content: Historically, phosphorus has been considered the limiting nutrient for primary production in the northern Baltic Sea, whereas further south in the Baltic Proper nitrogen is the limiting nutrient. In this study, we investigated the nutrient distribution during the past 30 years using Swedish and Finnish monitoring data. The results show comprehensively for the first time that the entire Bothnian Sea has switched to nitrogen limitation and that the Bothnian Bay is rapidly heading towards similar conditions. This is due to increasing inorganic phosphorus concentrations, possibly resulting from phosphorus rich water inflowing from the Baltic Proper. Inorganic nitrogen concentrations decrease or are unchanged. The increase of phosphorus led to increased primary production and, in the Bothnian Sea, to increased occurrence of filamentous cyanobacteria. The resulting shift emphasizes the need to revise management strategies of these basins, where treating both basins for phosphorus and nitrogen is advisable.

title: Contractor practices in construction waste management towards the sustainability of construction projects
summary: The construction industry is one of the sectors that contributes significantly to the economy in Malaysia. However, this rapid development has brought in a large amount of construction waste, and the contractor needs knowledge on how to man
content: The construction industry is one of the sectors that contributes significantly to the economy in Malaysia. However, this rapid development has brought in a large amount of construction waste, and the contractor needs knowledge on how to manage the construction waste strategically while the sustainability of the construction project could be maintained. A survey design with a quantitative approach is adopted in this study. The questionnaire is employed as the main instrument, and all gathered data were analyzed descriptively and inferentially using the Statistical Package for Social Science (SPSS) version 29. A total of 357 contractors who were randomly selected from four districts in the state of Johor, which are Kluang, Batu Pahat, Muar and Johor Bahru have involved in this study. The findings showed that many respondents, who are contractors, ensure that construction waste is handled by a competent or licensed party that follows the Solid Waste Management and Cleaning Regulations. Whilst for the construction waste management methods, most of the contractors disposed of the construction waste only in gazetted areas. Furthermore, the majority of contractors believe that recycling construction trash can enhance cost-effective advantages to a project, and that there is a strong correlation between knowledge, the sustainability of construction projects, and construction waste management techniques. Consequently, there is a difference between construction waste management practices and the sustainability of construction projects based on the G1, G4, and G7 contractor classes. Therefore, this study is important in assisting Johor State contractors in managing construction waste more effectively and consistently in the future, so that the sustainability element can be applied in construction projects in Malaysia.

title: National digital village pilot construction alleviates the economic gap between counties in China
summary: This paper exploits panel data on 1,564 Chinese counties from 2015 to 2023 and applies a difference-in-differences approach to evaluate the impact of digital village pilot on inter-county economic disparities. The results show that the pilo
content: This paper exploits panel data on 1,564 Chinese counties from 2015 to 2023 and applies a difference-in-differences approach to evaluate the impact of digital village pilot on inter-county economic disparities. The results show that the pilots significantly narrow county-level economic gaps, a finding that remains robust across multiple tests. Mechanism analysis suggests that digital village initiatives enhance endogenous county development by promoting technological innovation and rural entrepreneurship, with industrial upgrading playing a moderating role. It has a stronger impact on regions with a lower degree of reliance on agriculture, regions with greater financial support, and the central and western regions. Policy implications include the steady expansion of digital village pilots, strengthening of innovation and entrepreneurship, guidance for industrial upgrading, and improved supportive policies to foster coordinated regional development.

title: Transición energética: comparación prospectiva de los costos de generación de las energías solar y eólicaeólica
source: Revista Interdisciplinaria de Ingeniería Sustentable y Desarrollo Social
summary: La transición energética requiere tecnologías capaces de reducir las emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero sin comprometer la viabilidad económica de los sistemas eléctricos. El objetivo de este artículo es comparar prospectivamente la e
content: La transición energética requiere tecnologías capaces de reducir las emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero sin comprometer la viabilidad económica de los sistemas eléctricos. El objetivo de este artículo es comparar prospectivamente la evolución de los costos de generación de las energías solar fotovoltaica y eólica hasta el año 2050. Para ello, se utilizaron datos históricos internacionales del costo total nivelado de generación correspondientes al periodo 2005-2020. La metodología se basó en simulaciones de Monte Carlo mediante un movimiento geométrico browniano, generando diez mil escenarios para proyectar la evolución de los costos. Los resultados muestran una reducción sostenida en ambas tecnologías, siendo la energía solar fotovoltaica la que presenta la disminución más pronunciada, al pasar de 89 USD/MWh en 2020 a 11 USD/MWh en 2050. Por su parte, la energía eólica reduce sus costos de 69 USD/MWh a 25 USD/MWh en el mismo periodo. Se concluye que la energía solar fotovoltaica presenta el mayor potencial de reducción de costos hacia 2050; sin embargo, la complementariedad entre la energía solar y la eólica constituye un elemento estratégico para fortalecer la transición energética sustentable, mejorar la seguridad energética y contribuir a los procesos de descarbonización a largo plazo.

title: Judicial Enforcements of Environmental Justice in Nigeria: Comparative Insights from India and South Africa
source: JOURNAL OF LAW AND GLOBAL POLICY
summary: The judicial enforcement of environmental justice in Nigeria faces significant challenges which includes jurisdictional conflicts, non-compliance by transnational corporations (TNCs) with court judgments, and systemic delays. While State Hi
content: The judicial enforcement of environmental justice in Nigeria faces significant challenges which includes jurisdictional conflicts, non-compliance by transnational corporations (TNCs) with court judgments, and systemic delays. While State High Courts have historically adjudicated environmental disputes, issues of jurisdiction exemplified in Shell v. Isaiah, Iwherekan v. Shell, and Four Fishermen v. Shell have raised concerns about access to justice for pollution victims, especially following the Supreme Court’s interpretation of the relevant provisions of constitution which grants exclusive jurisdiction to the Federal High Court over oil-related environmental disputes. Multinational oil corporations frequently exploit procedural loopholes to evade accountability, while weak enforcement mechanisms have remained a formidable hinderance to effective remediation for victims of environmental damage. A comparative analysis with South Africa highlights the benefits of a constitutionalized approach to environmental rights which Nigeria must draw inspiration from. Unlike Nigeria, where environmental rights remain largely non-justiciable, South Africa’s Constitution explicitly guarantees the right to a healthy environment which ensures that a stronger legal enforcement and judicial oversight is in place. Similarly, India’s establishment of the National Green Tribunal (NGT) offers valuable lessons in terms of expediting environmental litigation and ensuring corporate accountability. The NGT’s role in enforcing environmental laws and reducing the burdens of litigation offers invaluable insight to Nigeria on the need for Nigeria to consider specialized tribunals for environmental disputes. This study commends the Supreme Court of Nigeria for addressing jurisdictional ambiguities and their interpretative roles but argues that a strengthened judicial mechanisms and institutional reforms must be adopted to enhance environmental justice. Drawing insights from South Africa’s constitutional approach and India’s specialized environmental tribunal system, this paper recommends the constitutionalization of environmental rights and the establishment of an environmental court to improve access to justice for victims of environmental hazards in Nigeria.

title: Hybrid Dual-Stage Solar Thermal Integration into the Cement Kiln Pre-Heater for Industrial Decarbonization: A Case Study in Jordan
summary: Cement production generates approximately 7% of global CO2 emissions; Jordan’s kilns run on petroleum coke, coal, and olive residue with no demonstrated solar thermal integration for pre-heating. This paper addresses that gap and presents t
content: Cement production generates approximately 7% of global CO2 emissions; Jordan’s kilns run on petroleum coke, coal, and olive residue with no demonstrated solar thermal integration for pre-heating. This paper addresses that gap and presents the first plant-data-backed techno-economic and environmental assessment of a hybrid dual-stage concentrating solar thermal system integrated into the pre-heater tower of a cement plant in Ma’an, Jordan (30.2° N, direct normal irradiance (DNI) = 2749 kWh/m2/yr). The study objectives are to (i) characterize Stage 5 and Stage 6 thermal loads from real plant operating data; (ii) size and simulate a 6000 m2 parabolic trough collector (PTC) field with molten-salt thermal energy storage (TES) targeting Stage 5 (380 °C, 3200 kW) and an 8000 m2 Linear Fresnel Reflector (LFR) field with rock/PCM TES targeting Stage 6 (300 °C, 2200 kW); (iii) quantify the combined solar fraction, fuel savings, and CO2 avoidance; (iv) conduct a Jordan-specific cost analysis benchmarked against NREL 2015 solar heat for industrial process (SHIP) data under three CAPEX scenarios; and (v) evaluate net present value (NPV) at two discount rates with and without carbon credits. The PTC field achieves a Stage 5 solar fraction of 35.5%, and the LFR field achieves 50.0% at Stage 6, yielding a combined annual solar fraction of 41.4% and displacing 59,384 GJ/yr (4163 t CO2/yr). Under Jordan base-case CAPEX of $3.89 M, 6% concessional finance, and a $50/t CO2 carbon credit, NPV reaches +$1.11 M with a breakeven carbon credit of $29/t CO2. These results confirm commercial viability under accessible green finance and carbon pricing, providing a replicable model for cement kiln pre-heater decarbonization in high-DNI Middle East and North Africa (MENA) countries.

title: ChatGPT-generated socioscientific issues in the context of systems thinking: affordances and limitations
source: Disciplinary and Interdisciplinary Science Education Research
summary: Abstract This study explores the potential of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), specifically ChatGPT, in supporting the design of socioscientific issues (SSI) unit plans that foster systems thinking in high school science educatio
content: Abstract This study explores the potential of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), specifically ChatGPT, in supporting the design of socioscientific issues (SSI) unit plans that foster systems thinking in high school science education. Employing document analysis, we systematically examined a series of outputs generated by ChatGPT 3.5 to produce an instructional unit focused on cross-state air pollution. Activities were coded using Stave and Hopper’s systems thinking taxonomy to assess the depth of student engagement with systems thinking. ChatGPT generated a structured SSI unit plan that provided opportunities for students to practice basic levels of systems thinking. However, GenAI outputs typically lacked specificity and contained inaccuracies. Iterative prompting led to incremental improvements but did not substantively elevate the complexity of systems thinking tasks. Teacher expertise and critical engagement remain essential for ensuring accuracy, depth, and pedagogical value.

title: Causal heuristics for predicting co-benefits from decarbonization and sufficiency: presenting a multi-staged methodology based on Theories-of-Change and causal diagrams
summary: Abstract Background Sufficiency is a critical but often overlooked decarbonization strategy. A significant challenge in promoting sufficiency is the difficulty in assessing its social co-benefits, such as improved health outcomes. This stud
content: Abstract Background Sufficiency is a critical but often overlooked decarbonization strategy. A significant challenge in promoting sufficiency is the difficulty in assessing its social co-benefits, such as improved health outcomes. This study presents a multistaged, iterative methodology designed to facilitate empirical investigations into the direct and indirect causal effects of sufficiency interventions. The primary purpose is to bridge the gap between an ex-ante impact hypothesis, potential impact models and evidence for plausible causal pathways. It helps to identify relevant variables and guides their statistical control. Results The methodology employs a four-step heuristic approach combining Inferences-to-the-Best-Explanation logic, Theory-of-Change models, Bayesian epistemology, and causal diagrams. Using the improvement of public transport systems as a case study, the methodology identifies two main pathways to health co-benefits: the reduction of pollutants leading to cleaner air and the increase in physical activity from walking or cycling to transit points. Bayesian credence assessments reveal that while the health benefits from reduced pollution and increased activity are highly credible, the initial “modal shift” from cars to public transport is not a trivial outcome. The results highlight that this shift is heavily moderated by the specific preferences and capabilities of car users. Causal diagrams further enable the distinction between direct and indirect effects, allowing researchers to identify which parameters must be controlled for in empirical studies to accurately predict health outcomes. Conclusions The proposed methodology provides a robust blueprint for establishing plausible impact relations in social impact assessments. It successfully closes the gap between qualitative case-oriented research and quantitative population-oriented evaluations. It follows a probabilistic epistemology and is thus open to different types of impact assessment methods, including both impact modelling and conventional statistics. By re-evaluation of pathways in light of evidence, the approach helps researchers avoid causal fallacies and biased expectations. Beyond transport, this iterative framework is adaptable to various sectors, including sustainable finance and scenario analysis, offering a versatile tool for designing more effective decarbonization policies and impact models.

title: The Sustainable Fashion Paradox: Understanding the Gap Between Gen Z’s Climate Commitment and Their Fashion Consumption Behavior
summary: Many Gen Z consumers claim to be concerned about climate change and supportive of sustainable consumption. Yet their actual fashion purchasing behavior is different as fast fashion remains their primary choice. This study explores this cont
content: Many Gen Z consumers claim to be concerned about climate change and supportive of sustainable consumption. Yet their actual fashion purchasing behavior is different as fast fashion remains their primary choice. This study explores this contradiction by asking to what extent Gen Z’s climate commitment influences their fashion purchasing behavior, and what key factors contribute to this value-action gap. To address this question, the study combines retail field observations in New York, USA and Beijing, China, semi-structured interviews with fashion industry professionals, and a survey of 200 Gen Z respondents across different regions. The findings show that this value-action gap is not simply a matter of personal hypocrisy among young consumers or misleading sustainability claims from brands. Instead, the gap comes from the fashion industry system and real consumption settings, including limited retail visibility, accessibility, affordability and aesthetic appeal. This study argues that for sustainable fashion to become part of Gen Z’s daily fashion consumption, the fashion industry needs to move beyond conveying sustainable branding narratives and make practical changes in price, style, store presentation, communication, social media influence, and community engagement.

title: Electron acceptor-dependent duality of nitrous oxide metabolism in Thiobacillus during sulfur autotrophic denitrification
summary: Sulfur-driven autotrophic denitrification (SADN) is a promising biotechnology for nitrogen removal from low-carbon wastewater; however, nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions remain a significant environmental concern. This study systematically in
content: Sulfur-driven autotrophic denitrification (SADN) is a promising biotechnology for nitrogen removal from low-carbon wastewater; however, nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions remain a significant environmental concern. This study systematically investigated the effects of different nitrogen oxide electron acceptors on denitrification performance, microbial community succession, distribution of the N 2 O reductase gene nosZ clade, and the ecological functions of Thiobacillus using sequential enrichment cultivation. Among the tested conditions, the nitrate ( NO 3 - )-fed system achieved the highest denitrification and sulfur oxidation rates, with the lowest net N 2 O accumulation, whereas the nitrite ( NO 2 - )-fed condition led to severe N 2 O accumulation due to an imbalance between N 2 O production and reduction. High-throughput sequencing and quantitative PCR analyses revealed that Thiobacillus became the primary sulfur-oxidizing denitrifier in the presence of NO 3 - , NO 2 - , and nitric oxide, accompanied by substantial enrichment of nirS and clade I nosZ genes. In contrast, N 2 O-fed conditions promoted a more functionally diverse community enriched with clade II nosZ bacteria, including Azonexus and Dechloromonas . Metagenomic analyses recovered three distinct Thiobacillus metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs 10, 11, and 25), each with distinct denitrification and sulfur oxidation capacities. MAG 10 contains genes for complete sulfur oxidation and denitrification, including clade I nosZ and nirS genes. Conversely, the nosZ gene was not detected in MAG 11, whereas the norB/norC genes were present, indicating their potential role as an N 2 O producer. MAG 25 exhibits N 2 O-responsive functional enrichment upon N 2 O feeding, reflecting a specialized ecological strategy centered on sulfur oxidation coupled with N 2 O reduction. Overall, these findings show that electron acceptors play a key role in shaping microbial succession, nosZ clade distribution, and the dual roles of Thiobacillus in N 2 O cycling depending on conditions. This study provides new insights into microbial ecology and offers potential strategies for mitigating N 2 O emissions in SADN processes.

title: Setting a vision for a meaningful low-carbon concrete quota
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This policy brief presents a scenario modelling study on setting a meaningful low-carbon concrete quota for EU public procurement under the Industrial Accelerator Act (IAA). It challenges the European Commission’s initially proposed 5% quot
content: This policy brief presents a scenario modelling study on setting a meaningful low-carbon concrete quota for EU public procurement under the Industrial Accelerator Act (IAA). It challenges the European Commission’s initially proposed 5% quota by demonstrating that the EU market can deliver substantially higher quotas, ranging between 32% and 79%, depending on the definition of low-carbon concrete applied. The study evaluates supply capacity, demand projections, and technology readiness to inform quota setting that supports both near-term deployment and long-term innovation in concrete decarbonisation.

title: Building State Capacity for the Clean Development Transition
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The clean energy and industrial transition represents a profound institutional challenge rather than a conventional market‑fixing exercise. As the document states, “The global clean energy and industrial transition is fundamentally an insti
content: The clean energy and industrial transition represents a profound institutional challenge rather than a conventional market‑fixing exercise. As the document states, “The global clean energy and industrial transition is fundamentally an institutional crisis of state capacity.” Market‑conforming incentives, carbon pricing, and fragmented regulatory signals cannot resolve the systemic coordination failures inherent in deep decarbonization. Clean technology systems—spanning energy, transport, metallurgy, and urban infrastructure—are interdependent and require synchronized, multi‑sectoral capital deployment that private actors cannot achieve under short‑term financial constraints. The monograph argues for a modernized Developmental State capable of orchestrating structural transformation through embedded bureaucratic autonomy, mission‑oriented delivery units, and sovereign strategic finance. As the text emphasizes, “Successfully deploying multi-gigawatt clean infrastructure networks… demands the resurrection and modernization of the Developmental State.” This institutional model integrates high‑capacity planning commissions, empowered national development banks, disciplined industrial subsidies, and reformed state‑owned utilities. Across twelve analytical chapters, the work outlines a comprehensive architecture for clean state capacity: Administrative coherence via super‑ministerial Clean Coordination Councils Bureaucratic autonomy to prevent fossil regulatory capture Strategic finance through recapitalized national development banks Industrial discipline using reciprocal performance conditionalities SOE restructuring to manage stranded fossil assets Domestic value addition through mineral downstreaming and technology licensing Digital statecraft for procurement transparency and telemetry‑verified infrastructure Regulatory acceleration via spatial planning and unified permitting Just transition compacts for labor protection and regional diversification Fiscal space expansion through green tax reform and multilateral debt restructuring The monograph culminates in a 2026–2050 strategic roadmap detailing a sequenced, three‑horizon institutional transformation toward a fully autonomous, mission‑oriented developmental state capable of delivering national decarbonization, technological sovereignty, and long‑run macroeconomic convergence.

title: Cross-Border Governance and Prim-Lex Nine-Dimensional Compliance: Global Carbon Markets, Green Supply Chains, and the Nine-Dimensional Certification System (Version 2.0)
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: On 1 January 2026, the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) officially entered its substantive implementation phase, becoming the world’s first systematically implemented carbon border adjustment instrument. The CBAM certificate pri
content: On 1 January 2026, the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) officially entered its substantive implementation phase, becoming the world’s first systematically implemented carbon border adjustment instrument. The CBAM certificate price was set at €75.36 per tonne of CO₂ equivalent in Q1 2026, adjusted slightly to €75.28 in Q2, with Q3 tracking toward the €79–86 range. Concurrently, on 10 July 2026, Russia formally requested the establishment of a WTO dispute settlement panel (DS639), making CBAM the first carbon border adjustment dispute to reach the panel-request stage, with review scheduled for the 25 September 2026 DSB meeting. The EU further plans to expand CBAM to approximately 180 steel- and aluminum-intensive downstream products by 2028, covering machinery, automotive parts, household appliances, and others, with an estimated 7,000 to 8,000 newly affected Chinese enterprises and approximately €18 billion of Chinese exports annually brought under coverage. Based on the complete nine-dimensional theoretical system of Prim-Lex Theory (Economic Climatology) — the Fivefold Prim-Fire, the Three-Tier GC⁴A Constraints, the Five-Element Dynamic Coupling Equations, the Eight-Dimensional Framework, and the Prim-Nexus Guidance — this paper systematically applies the five operational models — REMC (Fire), CLL (Metal), GCSOS (Water), RCE‑B/S (Wood), and G‑REMI (Earth) — to cross-border carbon compliance governance. It proposes a “Prim-Lex Green Compliance Label” three-color certification system based on nine-dimensional assessment. Using manufacturing in the Yangtze River Delta and Pearl River Delta as empirical cases, this paper demonstrates that through systematic nine-dimensional compliance optimization, enterprises can reduce CBAM certificate purchases by approximately 25%–40% and lower carbon tariff compliance costs by approximately 18%–35%. This paper provides a quantifiable, certifiable, and auditable governance operating system for global carbon markets, green supply chains, and cross-border carbon compliance, while offering a theoretical response from China’s independent knowledge system to the WTO legality debate surrounding CBAM in the context of DS639.

title: How Digitalization Can Accelerate the Global Clean Transition
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Digitalization has become the decisive institutional accelerator of the global clean‑energy transition. Although renewable technologies have achieved steep cost declines, their diffusion remains constrained by capital market frictions, veri
content: Digitalization has become the decisive institutional accelerator of the global clean‑energy transition. Although renewable technologies have achieved steep cost declines, their diffusion remains constrained by capital market frictions, verification opacity, fragmented supply chains, and high sovereign borrowing costs. As the monograph states, “High upfront capital hurdles, split incentives, opaque asset performance risks, and punitive commercial borrowing costs severely suppress clean technology diffusion…” Digital public infrastructure—built on IoT telemetry, algorithmic underwriting, and open data protocols—collapses these frictions by transforming physical asset performance into continuous, verifiable digital cash‑flow streams. This shift enables decentralized adoption at scale, particularly in emerging markets where traditional collateral‑based lending has failed. A second pillar of the argument is the transformative role of automated digital MRV. Legacy measurement, reporting, and verification systems are slow, manual, and expensive, often consuming up to 30% of project transaction budgets. Digital MRV replaces episodic audits with high‑resolution sensor telemetry and cryptographically signed data, reducing verification latency from months to sub‑second intervals and cutting certification costs by over 90%. By integrating ground‑level IoT data with satellite remote sensing, digital MRV establishes an incorruptible audit trail that dramatically increases investor confidence, enabling scalable climate finance, sovereign green‑bond compliance, and cross‑border environmental market linkages. The monograph further demonstrates how FinTech architectures—especially Pay‑as‑You‑Go (PayGo) micro‑leasing—democratize access to clean technologies for low‑income households and small enterprises. Mobile‑money rails, remote lockout firmware, and continuous repayment telemetry convert lumpy capital expenditure into affordable micro‑subscriptions. These digital rails generate alternative credit histories, compress default risk premiums, and allow distributed receivables to be securitized into institutional‑grade green assets. Combined with algorithmic underwriting engines that evaluate real‑time asset performance, digital finance platforms lower the weighted average cost of capital and unlock trillions in clean‑energy investment. Ultimately, the monograph argues that digitalization is not an auxiliary enhancement but the institutional backbone of the clean transition. Open interoperability standards, virtual power plant orchestration, digital product passports, and tokenized green‑finance instruments collectively enable clean‑energy systems that are transparent, programmable, and economically inclusive. By embedding digital public infrastructure into national energy and financial systems, countries can accelerate technology diffusion, strengthen macro‑resilience, and achieve structurally lower‑carbon growth trajectories. title: When Energy Risk Becomes Salient
summary: Replication data for “When Energy Risk Becomes Salient: Attention, Structural Exposure, and International Energy Equity Revaluation” This dataset contains the replication materials and empirical outputs supporting the manuscript When Energy
content: Replication data for “When Energy Risk Becomes Salient: Attention, Structural Exposure, and International Energy Equity Revaluation” This dataset contains the replication materials and empirical outputs supporting the manuscript When Energy Risk Becomes Salient: Attention, Structural Exposure, and International Energy Equity Revaluation. The study examines whether energy-related investor attention affects the relative valuation of national energy-sector equities, whether these effects vary across countries and information regimes, and whether persistent structural energy-system exposures become financially relevant when energy risk becomes salient. The archive contains the data, code, figures and test-level outputs corresponding to the final manuscript and supplementary appendix. It includes: Google Trends Web Search and News Search data for the 12 analytical markets and the Worldwide series; structural energy-system inputs including energy-import dependence, energy intensity, energy mix and carbon-pricing variables; macroeconomic, geopolitical-risk, oil-price and market-risk controls used in the analysis; processed structural-exposure datasets; complete monthly and daily empirical result tables; country-heterogeneity and slope-equality tests; structural attention-by-exposure interaction results; robustness, nonlinear, regime, falsification and influence tests; publication-timing and pseudo-real-time information-set tests; out-of-sample forecasting and economic-value results; publication-quality figures and the underlying source tables for Figures 1–10; analysis scripts for the monthly, daily and information-set pipelines; editable versions of the principal manuscript tables; the full supplementary-results appendix. The principal outcome is the Energy Revaluation Spread (ERS), defined as the local-currency return on a country's energy-sector equity index minus the return on its corresponding broad domestic equity market. Raw national energy-sector and broad-market index histories are not redistributed because the underlying source files remain subject to source licensing restrictions. To support reproducibility, the archive provides the exact benchmark definitions, raw source filenames, sample windows, file sizes and SHA-256 hashes of the market files used in the analysis. Researchers with legally obtained copies of the same series can therefore verify and reconstruct the financial-data inputs. Google Trends histories were downloaded in 2026 and may reflect Google's historical sampling and normalization procedures. Accordingly, the information-set exercises should be interpreted as publication-lag-adjusted or pseudo-real-time tests rather than true historical-vintage reconstructions.
