title: Biogenic volatile organic compound (BVOC) emissions from boreal forest floors during the first years after wildfire: effects of stand age and management
summary: Abstract. Boreal forests emit a wide range of biogenic volatile organic compounds (BVOCs) that influence atmospheric chemistry and climate through oxidation reactions and the formation of secondary organic aerosols. These emissions originat
content: Abstract. Boreal forests emit a wide range of biogenic volatile organic compounds (BVOCs) that influence atmospheric chemistry and climate through oxidation reactions and the formation of secondary organic aerosols. These emissions originate from plant metabolism, microbial activity, and storage pools such as litter, and vary in response to environmental conditions and disturbances. Wildfires, the dominant natural disturbance in boreal ecosystems, substantially alter ecosystem structure and carbon cycling, yet their effects on BVOC emissions during the early post-fire years remain poorly understood. Here, we quantified BVOC emissions during the first years after wildfire across gradients of stand age, fire severity, and post-fire management. BVOC emissions were strongly controlled by tree mortality and management practices. High-severity fire in young stands resulted in persistently low emission rates and a shift away from monoterpene dominance, likely reflecting limited biomass and substrate availability. In contrast, sites with surviving mature trees exhibited elevated emissions dominated by monoterpenes, driven by litter-derived storage pools. Salvage logging caused a transient increase in emissions in the first year after fire due to accumulated needle debris, followed by a rapid decline as litter inputs were depleted. Conversely, reforestation led to increasing emissions over time. These results demonstrate that early post-fire BVOC dynamics are regulated by the interaction between disturbance severity, stand age and management strategies, leading to distinct emission trajectories in the early recovery phase. Such shifts in BVOC emission magnitude and composition may have important implications for post-disturbance atmospheric chemistry and climate feedbacks. Our findings highlight the need to account for disturbance legacy effects and management practices when representing BVOC emissions in large-scale models.

title: From seaweed to safe digestate: integrating anaerobic digestion and genotoxicity assessment to evaluate digestate quality as an agricultural substrate
summary: Seaweed is a valuable feedstock for anaerobic digestion, yet integrated evaluation of methane production and digestate quality across multiple species remains limited in Morocco. This study presents the first assessment of biogas production
content: Seaweed is a valuable feedstock for anaerobic digestion, yet integrated evaluation of methane production and digestate quality across multiple species remains limited in Morocco. This study presents the first assessment of biogas production and the biostimulant potential of digestate derived from seaweed collected from the southern coast of Morocco. Anaerobic digestion was optimized at an organic loading rate of 8 g VS/L and substrate to inoculum ratio of 1:2, yielding a maximum biomethane potential of 171.18 ± 12.74 Nml CH 4 /g VS. Under these conditions, 11 seaweed species were used, with C. galeatum (116.85 ± 14.67 Nml CH 4 /g VS) exhibiting the highest methane yield followed by N. larix (102.09 ± 7.05 Nml CH 4 /g VS). Digestate bioassays showed that P. cartilagineum and S. muticum significantly enhanced seed germination index, while all digestates displayed low genotoxicity effects, making them safe for agricultural use. Overall, these findings indicate that seaweed can be effectively valorized for both methane and high value digestate production in Morocco.

title: Hydrology and Bloom Shapes Dissolved and Particulate Organic Carbon and DOC Fluxes in Danjiangkou Reservoir
summary: Reservoirs are increasingly recognized as active components of the global carbon cycle, acting as both sinks and sources of organic carbon while providing essential drinking-water services. Yet, the spatiotemporal behavior of organic carbon
content: Reservoirs are increasingly recognized as active components of the global carbon cycle, acting as both sinks and sources of organic carbon while providing essential drinking-water services. Yet, the spatiotemporal behavior of organic carbon fractions and their coupled controls by hydrological extremes, algal blooms, and reservoir operations remain poorly resolved in large, regulated water-supply reservoirs. Here, we quantified the distribution, drivers, and transport balance of organic carbon in Danjiangkou Reservoir (China) through monthly monitoring from March to December 2024 across the main reservoir, downstream reach, and major tributaries. Dissolved organic carbon (DOC), particulate organic carbon (POC), and total organic carbon (TOC) were measured together with key water-quality parameters and hydrological indicators to identify the dominant controls. Across the reservoir–tributary network, DOC, POC, and TOC ranged from 1.03 to 13.17 mg/L, 0.03 to 45.40 mg/L, and 1.34 to 48.57 mg/L, respectively, with tributaries generating the largest extremes. Reservoir waters exhibited substantially lower concentrations than tributaries and showed pronounced seasonal heterogeneity, with DOC generally higher in autumn than in summer and spring. Event-scale analyses revealed two distinct regimes: precipitation-driven runoff primarily intensified POC and TOC through terrestrial particle inputs, whereas bloom periods increased DOC and, under severe conditions, elevated TOC. POC and TOC were positively correlated with inflow, indicating that inflow dynamics govern the delivery of particulate carbon. The annual DOC transport flux was about 61 kt, with seasonal alternation between sink and source months, indicating net interception of upstream DOC under specific hydrological and operational conditions. These findings clarify how tributary forcing and reservoir regulation jointly govern carbon routing in large drinking-water reservoirs, with implications for carbon budgeting and protection of source water.

title: A Policy-Oriented Dataset of Urban Construction Carbon Emissions for 290 Chinese Cities, 2010–2024
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This dataset provides a policy-traceable, city-year panel of urban construction carbon emissions for 290 prefecture-level and higher cities in China, covering 2010–2024 (15 years). It accompanies the Data Descriptor "A Policy-Oriented Datas
content: This dataset provides a policy-traceable, city-year panel of urban construction carbon emissions for 290 prefecture-level and higher cities in China, covering 2010–2024 (15 years). It accompanies the Data Descriptor "A Policy-Oriented Dataset of Urban Construction Carbon Emissions for 290 Chinese Cities, 2010–2024" (submitted to Scientific Data; citation to be updated upon publication). What this dataset covers Unlike existing urban carbon inventories that disperse construction-related emissions across sectoral entries (industry, energy, waste) or cover only a single life-cycle stage (operation or stock), this dataset treats urban construction as a unified object spanning the full process — from building material production through construction, building operation, municipal services, and offsets/carbon sinks — within a single city-year framework. The 12 accounting indicators (E01–E12) are not defined by sector or physical process alone, but map one-to-one onto the quantitative targets found in China's low-carbon urban policy documents, making the dataset directly usable for year-by-year policy evaluation: E01 Construction Material Consumption E02 Construction Energy Consumption E03 Residential Building Operation E04 Public Building Operation E05 Rooftop Photovoltaic Offset E06 Urban Road Lighting E07 Municipal Solid Waste Treatment E08 Waste Incineration Power Offset E09 Urban Built-up-Area Vegetation Carbon Sink E10 Urban Water Supply E11 Urban Wastewater Treatment E12 Gas Supply Leakage (conditional boundary) Indicators are aggregated into Gross Emissions and Core Net Emissions through an explicit, documented summation identity. Files in this deposit City_Results.xlsx — city-level results (primary body of the dataset): a module-year long table (56,550 records), a 290-city summary, a 280-city core balanced panel, and a 137-city full-indicator panel. Provincial_Results.xlsx — annual results aggregated to China's 31 provincial-level units. National_Results.xlsx — annual national totals. Each workbook opens with an Overview sheet describing coverage, units, the aggregation formula, sheet-by-sheet contents, and guidance on which sample scope (290-city / 280-city / 137-city) is appropriate for which type of analysis. Data quality and uncertainty Every city-year record carries a data-quality grade (A–D) and completeness flags; missing values are retained as missing rather than zero-filled (with one documented exception, E05 in 2010–2012). Uncertainty is reported per module according to its statistical nature — Monte Carlo probabilistic intervals, preset scenario envelopes, or conditional physical boundaries — rather than as a single synthesized interval. Full grading criteria and technical validation against published inventories are provided in the associated Data Descriptor and its Supplementary Materials. Units and structure All emission values are reported in 10⁴ tCO₂e unless otherwise noted. Data are structured for direct use in R, Python, or GI

title: HOE Legacy 3 Particle Number Flux
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This dataset consists of measurements of particle flux taken during the SCOPE Hawaii Ocean Experiment - Legacy 3 (HOE Legacy 3) cruise in March 2016. The size spectrum of sinking particle flux was microscopically examined using Particle Int
content: This dataset consists of measurements of particle flux taken during the SCOPE Hawaii Ocean Experiment - Legacy 3 (HOE Legacy 3) cruise in March 2016. The size spectrum of sinking particle flux was microscopically examined using Particle Interceptor Traps (PITs) containing polyacrylamide gels (Ebersbach and Trull 2008, McDonnell and Buesseler 2012, McDonnell et al. 2015). Free-drifting sediment trap arrays containing 12 PITs (cross sectional area of 0.0039 m2) at each of 4 discrete depths (150, 300, 500, 750 m) were deployed. Two PITs at each depth were deployed with polyacrylamide gels mounted to the base of the traps; the remaining traps were used for subsequent analyses of particulate carbon and nitrogen (PC/PN) fluxes. Traps containing gels were prepared as described in Durkin et al. (2015) using custom-built 7.6 cm diameter polycarbonate cups as the base for each trap. A total of 100 mL of the gel solution was poured into each cup, yielding a solidified gel that was ~2.5 cm in height. Gel cups were covered and stored refrigerated until deployment. During deployment, cups containing the solidified gels were affixed to the bottom of the PITs, and traps were gently filled with a 0.5 m filtered brine-fixative seawater solution (50 g NaCl L-1 and 1% formalin final concentration). Duplicate gel cups were left in the refrigerator to serve as analytical blanks. Upon recovery, gel traps were placed in the dark and allowed to settle for 8 hours prior to processing. The brine-fixative solution was aspirated from each gel trap and cups were removed, stored in covered containers and refrigerated until laboratory analyses. Approximately 1 month after recovery, in the shore-based laboratory, gel-embedded particles were visualized and imaged using Nikon SMZ1500 stereomicroscope equipped with a Nikon DS Fi1 color camera and fiber optic light source. A grid (5 x 5 mm squares) was placed under each gel and the entire gel was photographed at 20x and 40x magnification. Vertical heterogeneity in the distribution of particles within the gels occasionally required capturing multiple images in each field of view from differing focal planes. The resulting images were analyzed using ImageJ software, and converted to binary images for subsequent particle sizing (Durkin et al. 2015). At the 40x magnification, particles <10 mm could not be accurately identified. We calculated the equivalent spherical diameter (ESD) based on the two-dimensional surface area calculated for each particle. Using the derived ESD, particles were classified into 10 logarithmically spaced size bins ranging from 10 μm to 1653 μm. The resulting particle size distribution was calculated from the number of particles in each size bin, normalized to the width of each size bin, and the duration of deployment. Particle counts from the duplicate gels deployed at each depth were averaged and analytical blanks were subtracted.

title: Paleogeographic controls on Phanerozoic weathering rates and implications for climate regulation
summary: Abstract Earth’s climate has remained habitable for billions of years, a stability usually attributed to a negative feedback from silicate weathering – the chemical breakdown of silicate rocks on land, which consumes atmospheric carbon diox
content: Abstract Earth’s climate has remained habitable for billions of years, a stability usually attributed to a negative feedback from silicate weathering – the chemical breakdown of silicate rocks on land, which consumes atmospheric carbon dioxide faster as climate warms. However, whether temperature or hydrology primarily drives this feedback remains uncertain. Here we show the two controls leave geographic fingerprints: in an ensemble of climate simulations with randomized continents, temperature-controlled weathering depends on tropical land fraction, whereas hydrology-controlled weathering depends on continental fragmentation. Stronger weathering removes more carbon dioxide, cooling the planet, so each regime predicts anti-correlation between temperature and its controlling geography. Reconstructed global temperatures spanning 480 million years are anti-correlated with tropical land fraction, except from roughly 295 to 200 million years ago – overlapping the supercontinent Pangea – when they anti-correlate with continental fragmentation. The mechanism stabilizing Earth’s climate may thus have evolved, with temperature control apparently dominant for most of this period.

title: Monodehydroascorbate reductases in plants: integrating ascorbate recycling, redox signaling, and stress adaptation
summary: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are central regulators of plant growth, development, and environmental adaptation, with hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) acting as a key signaling molecule. The ascorbate-glutathione cycle is the major antioxidant
content: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are central regulators of plant growth, development, and environmental adaptation, with hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) acting as a key signaling molecule. The ascorbate-glutathione cycle is the major antioxidant pathway that maintains H 2 O 2 homeostasis, and monodehydroascorbate reductase (MDHAR) plays a critical role by regenerating reduced ascorbate (ASC) from monodehydroascorbate (MDHA). Although traditionally viewed as an ASC-recycling enzyme, increasing evidence indicates that MDHAR has broader functions in redox regulation. Recent studies have revealed that MDHAR contributes to stress responses, developmental regulation, and ROS signaling through mechanisms that cannot be fully explained by ASC recycling alone. In this review, we summarize recent advances in the structural characteristics, regulation, subcellular specialization, and evolution of plant MDHARs. We also discuss emerging non-canonical functions of MDHAR, alternative pathways for MDHA reduction, and the mechanistic basis for the contrasting effects of MDHAR manipulation on ASC accumulation. Finally, we propose that MDHAR functions as an integrative hub linking ascorbate metabolism with cellular redox networks and highlight key challenges and future opportunities for exploiting MDHAR to improve crop stress tolerance, productivity, and nutritional quality.

title: Ultrafast charge and energy transfer dynamics in solids and at interfaces revealed by time-resolved x-ray absorption spectroscopy
summary: The excitation of solid materials with femtosecond optical pulses induces non-equilibrium states that are interesting for both fundamental and application-related reasons, as their properties can be quite different from those generated by e
content: The excitation of solid materials with femtosecond optical pulses induces non-equilibrium states that are interesting for both fundamental and application-related reasons, as their properties can be quite different from those generated by e.g. thermal excitation or chemical doping. However, once several degrees of freedom such as electronic and lattice excitations, or multiple components in a heterostructure, couple strongly, analyzing the resulting ultrafast dynamics on femto- to picoseconds requires element-sensitive spectroscopy on these timescales. This Topical Review discusses how new insights into ultrafast charge and energy transfer dynamics in solids and at interfaces can be gained from time-resolved soft x-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS). The state-of-the-art of the pump-probe XAS method at large scale facilities, namely synchrotron Femtoslicing sources and x-ray free electron lasers, is reviewed, with an emphasis on the opportunities and challenges of the respective facilities that motivate new methodological developments. For three selected material systems, it is then shown how x-ray absorption spectroscopy with femtosecond time resolution, in conjunction with theoretical calculations, is able to reveal and characterize non-equilibrium states by analyzing the transient electronic structure as well as lattice excitation via characteristic, time-dependent spectral features. Finally, future opportunities through the further development of laboratory-based soft x-ray sources and the combination of time-resolution with non-linear XAS are presented.

title: Response Letter to the Reviewer
summary: Abstract. Oceanic vertical velocity (w) is often neglected due to its small magnitude compared to horizontal currents. However, it plays a fundamental role in coupling the ocean surface with its interior, with major implications for a wide
content: Abstract. Oceanic vertical velocity (w) is often neglected due to its small magnitude compared to horizontal currents. However, it plays a fundamental role in coupling the ocean surface with its interior, with major implications for a wide range of physical and biogeochemical processes. In this study, four ADCPs were deployed on fixed Eulerian moorings and collected w measurements over slightly less than one year, covering the water column from 50 to 410 m depth. Using a combined approach based on Fourier spectral analysis and Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition, the variance distribution was characterized. The spectral analysis highlights the fundamental anisotropy of the flow, as vertical and horizontal velocities exhibit distinctly different spectral properties. While horizontal currents are mainly constrained by topography, vertical motions are primarily driven by internal gravity waves and intermittent small-scale processes. Furthermore, a persistent w signal at synoptic scales shows that the velocity is not purely geostrophic at all temporal scales. The results show that the variability of w time series is primarily dominated by short timescales, on the order of a few days or less. The data are also strongly influenced by biologically driven diel vertical migrations, which impose a pronounced periodic signal. The overall dynamics of the study area, strongly influenced by a canyon-incised slope topography, is characterized by a prevailing weak downwelling regime (3−4 mm s-1), intermittently disrupted by short-lived (few days) strong upwelling events (exceeding the 90th percentile of 1-day moving averaged w data). Finally, our results suggest that the canyons could act as an efficient tracer sink (e.g., carbon), with vertical velocities reaching several mm s-1.

title: Feedback of GHG in the Arctic Marine ecosystem
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This document and related data are presented in the fulfilment of Deliverable 5.2 of the GreenFeedBack Research and Innovation Action. The GreenFeedBack project is designed to advance scientific understanding of greenhouse gas (GHG) dynamic
content: This document and related data are presented in the fulfilment of Deliverable 5.2 of the GreenFeedBack Research and Innovation Action. The GreenFeedBack project is designed to advance scientific understanding of greenhouse gas (GHG) dynamics across terrestrial, freshwater, and marine ecosystems. The deliverable 5.2 assesses how climate change and local human pressures may alter greenhouse gas feedbacks in the Arctic marine ecosystem, focusing on the Arctic Ocean as a net atmospheric CO2 (carbon dioxide) sink and a net CH4 (methane) source. Drawing on literature, WP5 expert questionnaires, group discussion and fjord modelling, the report evaluates direct effects on air-sea CO2 uptake and CH4 release, while excluding indirect emissions from fossil-fuel use and life-cycle impacts. Most assessed human pressures are judged likely to weaken the Arctic Ocean CO2 sink and/or enhance CH4 emissions, notably fish farming, offshore oil and gas installations, coastal population growth, dredging and disposal of dredged material, agriculture, shallow sea mining, and major ports. Riverine inputs and atmospheric deposition of nutrients are assessed as strengthening both the Arctic Ocean CO₂ sink and its CH₄ source, with medium to high confidence. Exceptions include offshore oil and gas pipelines, which have no significant impact on CO2 uptake while increasing CH4 release, and fisheries and oil spills, which decrease CO2 uptake with no or no significant impact on CH4 release. Coastal wastewater treatment plants and hydroelectric reservoirs are also expected to decrease CO2 uptake, though no consensus was reached on their CH4 impact, while deep-sea mining is thought to have no significant impact on either flux. Some pressures, including land-based mining, land-based industries, shipping and offshore wind farms, remain difficult to assess because of limited evidence or lack of consensus. Climate-related pressures show similarly concerning tendencies: ocean acidification and ocean warming are expected to reduce CO2 uptake, while marine heat waves are expected to both reduce CO2 uptake and increase CH4 release. Both long-term increases in wind speed and storm-related wind events are expected to strengthen the CO2 sink and the CH4 source, with medium to high confidence. Sea-ice decline is also assessed as strengthening both the CO2 sink and the CH4 source, but with low confidence. Overall, the majority of anthropogenic pressures assessed are expected to act detrimentally on the Arctic Ocean's role as a CO2 sink or CH4 source, and the report emphasises that these biogeochemical outcomes must be considered alongside broader biodiversity and ecosystem impacts.

title: Data for:Low Burial Efficiency, High Carbon Sink Benefit: Paradoxical Role of Algal Organic Carbon in a Large Shallow Eutrophic Lake
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This deposit contains the data and code underlying the manuscript "Low burial efficiency, high carbon sink benefit: Paradoxical role of algal organic carbon in a large shallow eutrophic lake" (Zhu et al., submitted to Global Biogeochemical
content: This deposit contains the data and code underlying the manuscript "Low burial efficiency, high carbon sink benefit: Paradoxical role of algal organic carbon in a large shallow eutrophic lake" (Zhu et al., submitted to Global Biogeochemical Cycles), a source-resolved carbon budget of Lake Taihu, China, for 2001–2020. The dataset includes: (1) annual inputs of organic carbon (OC) from three sources — terrestrial, algal, and macrophyte — to Lake Taihu from 2001 to 2020; (2) source-specific OC mineralization and burial efficiencies; (3) the annual whole-lake carbon budget expressed as CO2-equivalents (CO2-eq), including CO2 and CH4 terms and the resulting net CO2-eq change; (4) sediment core profile measurements (δ¹³C and C/N ratios); (5) macrophyte biomass records compiled from the literature; (6) lake monitoring data (chlorophyll-a, water temperature, suspended solids concentration, and photosynthetically active radiation) from the Taihu Laboratory for Lake Ecosystem Research; (7) the annual inflow and outflow discharge of each water-resources zone of the Taihu watershed, together with the areas of these zones; and (8) all data underlying the figures. The MATLAB code includes the reactive transport model coupled with a gamma-distribution reactive continuum model used to analyze OC reactivity in sediments (rc_rtm_poc_calibration.m, with input file RC_RTM_POC.xlsx), and the Monte Carlo elasticity analysis of the sediment-to-water mineralization ratio (monte_carlo_elasticity_analysis.m).

title: Beyond millijoules: a six-dimensional tissue-dose model for fractional ablative carbon dioxide laser therapy
source: International Journal of Research in Dermatology
summary: Fractional ablative carbon dioxide (CO2) laser treatment is commonly documented with displayed parameters such as pulse energy, power, pulse duration, density level and number of passes. These settings are device-specific inputs, not a port
content: Fractional ablative carbon dioxide (CO2) laser treatment is commonly documented with displayed parameters such as pulse energy, power, pulse duration, density level and number of passes. These settings are device-specific inputs, not a portable description of the tissue dose. This perspective proposes a six-dimensional tissue-dose model that represents treatment as a state vector comprising ablation geometry, coagulation geometry, treated fraction, spatial distribution, heat accumulation and healing reserve. The framework was developed through a targeted narrative synthesis of foundational fractional photothermolysis studies, histologic and computational dosimetry work, wound-healing investigations, clinical consensus statements and complication literature. A targeted PubMed, Crossref, journal-archive and web search through 19 August 2026 did not identify a previously published framework integrating the same six dimensions. The model separates the delivered tissue insult from device settings and treats healing reserve as a biological and anatomical constraint on the acceptable exposure. It explains why equal millijoules, equal nominal density or equal total energy can produce different lesion geometry, local overlap, thermal burden and recovery. The framework is intended for treatment planning, cross-platform reporting, education and prospective data collection; it is not a validated dose calculator and does not support universal presets. Validation should combine expert content assessment, platform-specific histology or optical imaging, a common clinical data dictionary and prospective prediction of efficacy, delayed healing, postinflammatory hyperpigmentation and scarring. A shared six-dimensional vocabulary may improve reproducibility while preserving the site-and patient-specific judgment required for safe fractional ablative laser therapy.

title: The Capitalogenic Security Trilemma
summary: This article introduces the capitalogenic security trilemma, that is, a reconceptualization of the tension among social, trade, and national security in which ecological (in)security figures as a constitutive structural condition of the mod
content: This article introduces the capitalogenic security trilemma, that is, a reconceptualization of the tension among social, trade, and national security in which ecological (in)security figures as a constitutive structural condition of the modern world-system rather than a contextual backdrop. Drawing on Moore’s world-ecology, we locate the source of ecological (in)security in capitalism’s appropriation of unpaid natures, and we specify two transmission mechanisms through which this contradiction stratifies the trilemma across the core-periphery hierarchy: the balance of payments constraint—the monetary form through which peripheral states are disciplined into extractivism—and unequal ecological exchange—the biophysical form through which the material preconditions of security are transferred to the core. Core militarization is the coercive technology through which the frontiers of appropriation are held open. The contribution to the world-systems literature is a unified theoretical model in which the monetary and biophysical asymmetries of the world-system, hitherto theorized in parallel, are shown to be two forms of a single circuit of appropriation, such that core security and peripheral insecurity are jointly produced rather than separately determined, with direct implications for the (in)efficacy of reform.

title: The Filamin A Proteomic Switch: Solubility States and Cytoskeletal Dynamics Explain the Inverse Epidemiological Relationship Between Cancer and Alzheimer's Disease
summary: This manuscript unifies global registries with molecular kinetics to resolve the inverse comorbidity between cancer and Alzheimer's disease. We propose this inversion represents a binary, tissue-specific allocation of cell survival strategi
content: This manuscript unifies global registries with molecular kinetics to resolve the inverse comorbidity between cancer and Alzheimer's disease. We propose this inversion represents a binary, tissue-specific allocation of cell survival strategies dictated by the solubility of the Filamin A (FLNA) cytoskeletal scaffolding network under systemic cobalamin insufficiency. Chronic exposure to trace environmental nitrous oxide (N2O) pollution passivates cobalamin, arresting the cell-autonomous one-carbon cycle. In post-mitotic neural architectures, this bioenergetic arrest forces membrane potential collapse and excitotoxic decay, activating caspase-3 to cleave the FLNA matrix into a divergent fragment pool. Specific cytosolic domains bind alpha-7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (α7nAChRs) to anchor toxic amyloid signaling, driving Alzheimer's pathogenesis; concurrently, separate liberated 90-kDa C-terminal fragments (FLNA-90) translocate to the nucleus to execute a genomic tumor-suppressor checkpoint. Conversely, peripheral tissues with high metabolic plasticity escape collapse via malignant transformation. These cells keep caspase-3 checked and maintain the FLNA network intact, soluble, and phosphorylated at Serine 2152 (pS2152) to complex with cytoplasmic Cyclin D1/CDK4 networks. This reconfigures FLNA into an active motility engine driving invasive lamellipodia, but stalls proteolytic processing and forces an absolute loss of the nuclear FLNA-90 tumor-suppressor brake, unleashing c-Myc oncogenic transcription. Crucially, this malignant transformation functions as an active metabolic adaptation; by acting as a high-velocity metabolic sink that harvests coenzymes and consumes systemic excitotoxins, the peripheral tumor drives active metastatic seeding to locate uncompromised nutrient sources and export bioavailable cobalamin, rescuing central neural networks from homeostatic collapse. Filamin A thus serves as the definitive structural, conformational, and proteomic switch governing this inverse disease matrix.

title: Defiant hope - intercessory prayer as spiritual resistance to hopelessness in the climate crisis
summary: This paper examines the role of intercessory prayer in how Christian climate activists from the Global North engage with the existential challenges of the climate crisis. Based on a qualitative case study of the evangelical prayer network C
content: This paper examines the role of intercessory prayer in how Christian climate activists from the Global North engage with the existential challenges of the climate crisis. Based on a qualitative case study of the evangelical prayer network Climate Intercessors, the research draws on participant observation and interviews, exploring how prayer functions as a spiritual response to despair and uncertainty. The findings show that intercessory prayer fosters solidarity, helps to process climate anxiety and cultivates defiant hope. This is a stance that resists hopelessness while acknowledging human limitations. The research also shows how digital technologies are a tool that connects people from different churches and geographical contexts united by their awareness of the climate crisis. The study contextualizes these findings within lived theology, three empirical case studies by Nita, Hall and Schüler and engages with Jürgen Moltmann’s theology of hope.

title: Geschichte/n schreiben im Anthropozän
summary: Vierzehn Beiträge aus Literatur- und Geschichtswissenschaft zur interdisziplinären Reflexion und Analyse anthropozäner Sinnstiftung über Medien- und Gattungsgrenzen hinweg. Das Anthropozän mag als geologischer Begriff abgelehnt worden sein
content: Vierzehn Beiträge aus Literatur- und Geschichtswissenschaft zur interdisziplinären Reflexion und Analyse anthropozäner Sinnstiftung über Medien- und Gattungsgrenzen hinweg. Das Anthropozän mag als geologischer Begriff abgelehnt worden sein – als Gegenwartsdiagnose hat es jedoch seit einigen Jahren diskursprägenden Bestand, und das wird sich voraussichtlich nicht schnell ändern. Die literatur- und geschichtswissenschaftlichen Aufsätze in diesem Sammelband gehen nicht nur der Frage nach, wie die brenzlige Situation, in der wir uns befinden, in Form von Geschichte/n erzählt wird, sondern auch, welche innovativen Lesarten und Methoden dem Anthropozän und seiner nuancierten Analyse gerecht werden können. Sie zeigen, dass sich diese Auseinandersetzungen sehr bewusst in ästhetische und narrative Traditionen einschreiben und auch alte Texte und Fragestellungen in ein neues Tageslicht rücken. Wer ist denn dieser anthropos im Anthropozän? Welche Sinnstiftungen gibt es jenseits der Binarität Utopie – Dystopie? Und nicht zuletzt: Welche blinden Flecken im Anthropozändiskurs decken Literatur- und Geschichtswissenschaft gegenwärtig auf?

title: Melanin Suppresses Aβ Aggregation and Toxicity
summary: Abstract The aggregation of amyloid-β (Aβ) peptides into insoluble deposits is a characteristic hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and related neurodegenerative disorders. While AD is the most common cause of dementia, there are currently
content: Abstract The aggregation of amyloid-β (Aβ) peptides into insoluble deposits is a characteristic hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and related neurodegenerative disorders. While AD is the most common cause of dementia, there are currently no disease-modifying treatments which are both affordable and adverse-free. In this study, we report that melanin, a pigment which is commonly found in nature and is abundant in parts of the human brain, suppresses the aggregation of the 42-amino acid Aβ variant (Aβ42). Using biophysical and biochemical techniques, we show that melanin delays Aβ42 aggregation while also reducing the amount of Aβ42 that converts into aggregates. Using thioflavin T assays paired with chemical kinetics, we characterised the melanin-induced inhibition of Aβ42 aggregation in vitro. Using MALDI-MS, we elucidate the molecular basis of this effect by showing that melanin prevents Aβ42 dimerisation. We then demonstrate that melanin also reverts the aggregation process by dissolving pre-formed Aβ42 fibrils. Finally, we show that melanin reduces Aβ42 aggregation and rescues Aβ42 toxicity in an SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cell model. Our study shows that melanin disrupts the aggregation and cytotoxicity of Aβ42, and suggests that compounds derived from human metabolites may offer promising avenues to combat amyloid formation.

title: Aqueous-Phase Delivery of SLIC-SABRE Hyperpolarized [15N3]Metronidazole
summary: Abstract Metronidazole is an antiprotozoal antibiotic drug holding promise for tumor microenvironment analysis in hyperpolarized MRI due to its hypoxia-sensitive metabolism. Previous studies have explored the 15N hyperpolarization of metron
content: Abstract Metronidazole is an antiprotozoal antibiotic drug holding promise for tumor microenvironment analysis in hyperpolarized MRI due to its hypoxia-sensitive metabolism. Previous studies have explored the 15N hyperpolarization of metronidazole using dissolution dynamic nuclear polarization (d-DNP) and signal amplification by reversible exchange (SABRE). Here, we demonstrate that by using spin-lock-induced crossing (SLIC), 15N polarization levels up to 10–11% are achieved for 30 mM [15N3]metronidazole, improving polarization levels by a factor of 1.4 ± 0.1 compared to polarization levels achieved in conventional SABRE experiments under otherwise the same conditions. This polarization was harnessed to probe the purification of methanolic solutions of hyperpolarized [15N3]metronidazole, reducing the methanol concentration by 10-fold in the obtained aqueous solutions of 15N-hyperpolarized metronidazole, retaining up to 1/3 of initial polarization. This pilot study marks a substantial step toward the biomedical application of [15N3]metronidazole and is promising for the 15N-hyperpolarization of other substrates via SLIC and other SABRE strategies.

title: HvPHO1 Controls a Glucose 1‐Phosphate– SnRK1 Signalling Module That Coordinates Starch Accumulation in Barley Endosperm
summary: Developing barley grains must balance the use of imported sucrose between soluble sugars and storage starch, but how this balance is controlled remains unclear. Here we show that loss of the plastidial α-glucan phosphorylase HvPHO1 causes s
content: Developing barley grains must balance the use of imported sucrose between soluble sugars and storage starch, but how this balance is controlled remains unclear. Here we show that loss of the plastidial α-glucan phosphorylase HvPHO1 causes starch and soluble sugars to accumulate concurrently in barley grains. Developing pho1 grains showed sustained increases in glucose 1-phosphate (G1P) and adenosine diphosphate glucose (ADP-glucose), and exogenous G1P also promoted starch accumulation, supporting a stimulatory effect of elevated G1P on starch synthesis. G1P directly bound sucrose non-fermenting 1-related protein kinase 1 (HvSnRK1), suppressing its kinase activity and its phosphorylation of sucrose synthase 2 (HvSUSY2); the metabolic phenotypes of snrk1 and susy2 mutants supported a role for this phosphorylation module in sucrose utilization and soluble-sugar homeostasis. HvPHO1 also interacted with the starch-granule initiation factor starch synthase 4 (HvSS4). Loss of HvPHO1 increased the abundance of B-type starch granules and shifted their size distribution, indicating a parallel role in storage-starch organization. pho1 lines showed greater grain dry weight and test weight. Thus, loss of HvPHO1 initiates G1P-mediated metabolic feedback that reconfigures the balance between sucrose utilization and starch accumulation and is associated with enhanced grain carbon deposition and grain weight. These findings reveal G1P-dependent feedback linking starch-precursor status to SnRK1-mediated carbon allocation in barley endosperm.

title: QTC-019 — Earth's Thermostat / El termostato de la Tierra
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: English abstract Earth has kept surface water through most of its history even though the Sun brightened, continents moved and volcanic carbon sources changed. The familiar explanation is a carbonate-silicate 'thermostat': warming and an in
content: English abstract Earth has kept surface water through most of its history even though the Sun brightened, continents moved and volcanic carbon sources changed. The familiar explanation is a carbonate-silicate 'thermostat': warming and an intensified water cycle can accelerate silicate weathering, transferring carbon dioxide into carbonate rock, while cooling weakens the sink and allows geological emissions to rebuild the greenhouse. That account is real but incomplete. Weathering also depends on fresh mineral supply, runoff, lithology, biology and topography; ocean crust consumes carbon too; and global glaciation can interrupt the continental pathway. This article follows carbon from volcanic release to rock storage, distinguishes a negative feedback from a temperature set point, and explains why a process operating over hundreds of thousands of years cannot cancel modern warming on human timescales. Resumen en español La Tierra ha conservado agua superficial durante la mayor parte de su historia aunque el Sol se volvió más luminoso, los continentes se desplazaron y cambiaron las fuentes volcánicas de carbono. La explicación habitual es un «termostato» carbonato-silicato: el calentamiento y un ciclo del agua más intenso pueden acelerar la meteorización de silicatos, transferir dióxido de carbono a rocas carbonatadas, mientras el enfriamiento debilita el sumidero y permite que las emisiones geológicas reconstruyan el efecto invernadero. El mecanismo es real, pero incompleto. La meteorización depende también de suministro mineral fresco, escorrentía, litología, biología y topografía; la corteza oceánica consume carbono; y una glaciación global puede interrumpir la vía continental. Este artículo sigue el carbono desde su liberación volcánica hasta su almacenamiento rocoso, distingue una retroalimentación negativa de una temperatura objetivo y explica por qué un proceso de cientos de miles de años no puede cancelar el calentamiento moderno en escalas humanas.

title: Investigating corrosion mechanisms and the electrochemical performance of ferrosilicon for dense medium separation operations in Botswana
summary: Ferrosilicon (FeSi) is widely used in dense medium separation (DMS) processes for mineral beneficiation, however, its degradation due to corrosion presents significant operational challenges. Despite its industrial importance, limited resea
content: Ferrosilicon (FeSi) is widely used in dense medium separation (DMS) processes for mineral beneficiation, however, its degradation due to corrosion presents significant operational challenges. Despite its industrial importance, limited research has addressed the electrochemical behavior of FeSi under the conditions specific to Botswana’s mining operations. This study investigates the corrosion mechanisms and electrochemical performance of three milled FeSi grades (100D, 150D, and 270D) using open circuit potential (OCP), potentiodynamic polarization (PDP), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), and surface characterization techniques (SEM-EDS, XRD, Raman Spectroscopy, and particle size distribution). The results reveal that 270D demonstrated the best overall corrosion resistance, exhibiting the highest charge transfer resistance ( R ct = 139,370 Ω·cm 2 ), followed by 100D ( R ct = 139,700 Ω·cm 2 ), and lastly 150D ( R ct = 51,020 Ω·cm 2 ), which consistently exhibited the poorest corrosion resistance across all techniques. 150D showed the highest corrosion current density (I corr = 1.57 × 10 −3 A/cm 2 , while 100D; I corr = 1.94 × 10 −4 A/cm 2 , and 270D; I corr = 1.50 × 10 −4 A/cm 2 ) and the most negative corrosion potential (E corr ), indicating poorest corrosion resistance. OCP measurement confirmed that 150D exhibited more frequent electrochemical fluctuations, indicative of lower surface stability. Particle size distribution shifted from unimodal to bimodal in all corroded samples, suggesting corrosion-induced particle fragmentation and agglomeration. These finding contribute to material selection and process optimization for more cost-effective and sustainable DMS operations in Botswana.

title: Volatile Organic Compounds in Rainwater: A New Frontier in Atmosphere–Biosphere Interactions
summary: Abstract Rainwater is a key vector of atmospheric deposition, linking the atmosphere with terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. While the inorganic chemistry of precipitation (dominated by sulfate, nitrate, ammonium, and trace metals) has bee
content: Abstract Rainwater is a key vector of atmospheric deposition, linking the atmosphere with terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. While the inorganic chemistry of precipitation (dominated by sulfate, nitrate, ammonium, and trace metals) has been extensively studied, organic compounds in rainwater have received less attention, and Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) in particular have been practically overlooked. Recent methodological advances have revealed that a diverse suite of VOCs can be detected in rainwater along with VOC‐derived compounds, challenging the long‐held assumption that wet deposition plays a negligible role in VOC cycling. Although wet deposition is generally thought to be a minor atmospheric sink for VOCs (∼13.3% of total VOC emissions), rainborne VOCs are chemically reactive and biologically labile, such that even small quantities may exert disproportionate effects on soil microbial activity, plants, short‐term biogeochemical cycling, and water chemistry at local to regional scales. This article combines a synthesis of the current state of knowledge on rainborne VOCs and VOCs‐derived compounds with a particular focus on VOC occurrence, sources, partitioning, and transformation processes, with a forward‐looking perspective on the potential significance of rainborne VOCs for carbon cycling and atmosphere–biosphere interactions. We identify major gaps in observations, analytical capability, and modeling frameworks that limit quantitative understanding of VOC wet deposition and its ecological significance. Finally, we outline priority research directions, including improved sampling strategies, advanced analytical techniques, and integration into Earth system models. Together, these advances are needed to reassess the role of precipitation not only as a passive sink for atmospheric pollutants, but as an active driver of ecosystem functioning and Earth system processes in a changing climate.

title: Controls on carbon and nutrient transport in a tidal creek across a coastal forest-marsh transition under sea-level rise
summary: Sea level rise (SLR) and saltwater intrusion (SWI) drive ecological and biogeochemical changes in coastal forests that alter solute fluxes between marshes and estuaries. Tidal creeks mediate transport of carbon (C), iron (Fe), and nitrogen
content: Sea level rise (SLR) and saltwater intrusion (SWI) drive ecological and biogeochemical changes in coastal forests that alter solute fluxes between marshes and estuaries. Tidal creeks mediate transport of carbon (C), iron (Fe), and nitrogen (N) during flood and ebb tides, yet quantifying elemental fluxes is challenging due to bidirectional tidal flow and frequent bank overtopping. We quantified surface-water transport of C, Fe, and N during spring tides and storm events (2022–2023) in a tidal creek draining a transitioning coastal forest along the Delaware Bay. Discharge was estimated using a novel rating-curve model that incorporates bank overtopping dynamics. Groundwater wells and redox probes along a marsh-to-forest transect monitored water table elevation, salinity, and redox potential. We observed net imports of dissolved organic carbon (DOC), dissolved organic nitrogen (DON), dissolved Fe, and ammonium (NH4-N). DOC hourly loads were positively correlated with dissolved Fe loads, suggesting microbial dissolution of C-bearing Fe oxides during flood tides, and reprecipitation and C retention on ebb tides. Plant uptake and nitrification drove NH4-N and DON imports, as plant uptake during high tide could remove N from the water column. There was no import or export of nitrate (NO3-N), but NO3-N hourly loads were positively correlated with marsh redox potential, consistent with denitrification under reduced conditions. As the coastal zone responds to accelerating SLR, dissolution of Fe protected C will inhibit C sequestration and marsh loss to SLR could increase N delivery to coastal waters as plants uptake less N, with downstream implications for eutrophication.

title: Integrated photochemical and transcriptomic responses reveal an adaptive strategy of the Antarctic snow alga Chlorominima collina (Chlorophyta) for surviving freezing and darkness
summary: Snow algae represent important primary producers and carbon sinks in the cryosphere. Disentangling the physiological and molecular responses that these organisms display in the face of acute abiotic stress caused by snow dynamics is key to
content: Snow algae represent important primary producers and carbon sinks in the cryosphere. Disentangling the physiological and molecular responses that these organisms display in the face of acute abiotic stress caused by snow dynamics is key to revealing survival strategies and monitoring climate change effects. Here, we examine the tolerance to a short-term (4 h) freezing condition (-20°C) in darkness, followed by a recovery period, in the Antarctic snow alga Chlorominima collina. The responses were analyzed in contrast to a light control (2 °C) by integrating of chlorophyll fluorescence of PSII, mRNA-sequencing and oxidative stress detection. The treated cells reduce PSII photochemical efficiency and suppress the light harvesting process. Simultaneously abiotic stress-responsive genes were expressed, suggested a reprograming of metabolism and process, orchestrated by key signaling pathways and transcription factors. This profile revealed common elements of states prior to hypometabolism such as, the fuel switch from carbohydrate to lipid catabolism, improved defenses, repression of biosynthetic processes, induction of mitophagy and autophagy, and regulation of transcription and translation. These adjustments promoted the maintenance of cellular homeostasis, as evidenced by enrichment of this process and the recovery of PSII efficiency. Therefore, we proposed that the integration of the reduction of efficiency with which PSII captures energy and the regulation of genes involved in the induction of hypometabolism constitutes an adaptive strategy that confers at snow algae freezing and darkness tolerance. Collectively, the observed functional changes may be relevant for understanding the survival and subsequent adaptation of Chlorophyta to the Antarctic snow environment.

title: Does contamination with legacy persistent organic pollutants still prevail over emerging compounds in Arctic marine mammals?
summary: Transboundary pollution with harmful chemicals triggers research in remote regions such as the Arctic. Legacy and emerging hydrophobic organic contaminants, including persistent organic pollutants, biomagnify and are of particular concern i
content: Transboundary pollution with harmful chemicals triggers research in remote regions such as the Arctic. Legacy and emerging hydrophobic organic contaminants, including persistent organic pollutants, biomagnify and are of particular concern in marine top predators and humans. Each chemical group can exceed effect thresholds in apex predators without considering mixture effects with other contaminants nor multiple stressor settings. We used silicone chemometers to investigate the contaminant profiles in blubber tissues collected from 84 individuals covering six Arctic marine mammal species from East Greenland during 2012-2021: long-finned pilot whales, white-beaked dolphins, Atlantic white-sided dolphins, killer whales, narwhals, and polar bears. Of 98 analyzed chemicals we found 53 at least once, and we observed widespread contamination in which legacy, regulated pollutants and their degradation products prevailed over emerging compounds, in numerous cases (up to 81%) exceeding effect thresholds. The species showed distinct patterns of polychlorinated biphenyls, organochlorine pesticides, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, pyrethroids, musk compounds, antioxidants, and UV stabilizers. The highest contamination was observed for dichlorodiphenyldichloroethylene and polychlorinated biphenyls in killer whales. No differences between sex were found in pilot whales, but in some cases concentrations correlated with age. Our results stress the importance of reducing use and emissions of industrial chemicals to support protection of these iconic species in our planet’s remotest regions.

title: Synergistic Segregation and Precipitation of MNSPs in RPV Steels: A multiphase-field study
source: Journal of Materials Research and Technology
summary: : The synergistic co-precipitation of Cu-rich phases and manganese-nickel-silicon-dominated phases (MNSPs include T6 and T3 phases) plays a critical role in the irradiation embrittlement of reactor pressure vessel (RPV) steels. In this work
content: : The synergistic co-precipitation of Cu-rich phases and manganese-nickel-silicon-dominated phases (MNSPs include T6 and T3 phases) plays a critical role in the irradiation embrittlement of reactor pressure vessel (RPV) steels. In this work, a five-component Fe-Cu-Mn-Ni-Si multiphase-field model is developed to describe the coupled evolution of the ferritic matrix, Cu-rich phase, T3 phase, and T6 phase. The simulations reveal a composition-dependent transition in the precipitation pathway. In high-Cu alloys, Cu, Ni, and Si first form solute clusters, while Mn partitions more slowly; with further evolution, Cu becomes enriched in the core and Mn-Ni-Si segregates around it, producing a Cu-rich core/Mn-Ni-Si-enriched shell morphology. In low-Cu alloys with high Mn-Ni-Si supersaturation, trace Cu accelerates early solute clustering, but subsequent precipitation is dominated by Mn-Ni-Si phases. T6 forms first as the main precipitate phase, whereas T3 appears later at the T6/matrix interface after local solute redistribution. Increasing the Mn or Si concentration weakens this coupled T6/T3 pathway and promotes separate precipitation of T6 and T3. In realistic low-solute compositions, a pre-existing T6-like embryo remains stable and grows by absorbing dilute Mn, Ni, and Si from the matrix, while T3 enrichment appears only after T6 growth slows. These results suggest a sequential chemical-precipitation mechanism in which residual Cu promotes early solute clustering, T6 governs the principal growth stage, and delayed T3 interfacial enrichment accompanies late-stage stabilization. The seeded calculation evaluates the conditional growth of an assumed T6-like embryo and does not model defect-assisted nucleation.

title: ChamberFlux: an open-source interactive analysis platform for soil GHG flux analysis from trace gas analyzers
summary: Soil greenhouse gas (GHG) flux campaigns based on portable laser-based trace gas analyzers (LI-COR LI-7810 and LI-7820) generate tabular CSV/XLSX exports whose conversion into a publishable analysis currently depends on commercial software
content: Soil greenhouse gas (GHG) flux campaigns based on portable laser-based trace gas analyzers (LI-COR LI-7810 and LI-7820) generate tabular CSV/XLSX exports whose conversion into a publishable analysis currently depends on commercial software or ad-hoc scripts that demand programming skills and offer little reproducibility. We present ChamberFlux , an open-source Python/Streamlit web platform for the post-processing and exploratory analysis of analyzer-derived chamber GHG flux outputs : it begins where the manufacturer’s flux-fitting stage ends, taking the already-computed flux estimates through a single, code-free, multilingual (PT/EN/ES) interface covering data cleaning, exploratory and spatial analysis, time-series decomposition and supervised regression. Distributed on GitHub under the GPL-2.0-only licence, the application is validated by 71 pytest unit tests, an explicit data-dictionary schema and a synthetic reference dataset, and is already in production in the Goiás Verde initiative across the Brazilian Cerrado, offering the soil-flux community a free, transparent and reproducible alternative to commercial packages and one-off scripts.

title: Resolving bottom-up and top-down food-web structure and function for Everglades restoration
summary: Many ecosystem functions and services that sustain biodiversity and human well-being are rooted in food-web processes, yet food-web studies often fail to integrate multiple ways of quantifying trophic links or to clearly distinguish top-dow
content: Many ecosystem functions and services that sustain biodiversity and human well-being are rooted in food-web processes, yet food-web studies often fail to integrate multiple ways of quantifying trophic links or to clearly distinguish top-down from bottom-up effects. To address these gaps in support of on-going Everglades restoration, we combined diet data with studies quantifying top-down effects to construct a high-resolution energetic food web for freshwater marshes. Our goal was to identify highly connected nodes relevant to restoration and to evaluate how bottom-up and top-down links interact to shape community structure and ecosystem function. Our review compiled diets for 107 consumers from 82 publications, revealing a food web reliant on detrital-based energy pathways, with notable exceptions for some invasive fishes. The detrital-energy pathway was characterized by highly connected consumer nodes including amphipods, grass shrimp ( Palaemon paludosus ), and cyprinodontid fishes. Most indicators of restoration success, like American alligators ( Alligator mississippiensis ), were highly connected. Comparisons of dynamic and energetic links indicated that strong top-down effects often occurred between consumer-resource pairs with weak energetic links; diet importance for predators failed to predict strength of population dynamic effects for prey. Further, top-down effects of some invasive fishes may limit bottom-up effects of Everglades restoration. Using both types of information and visualizing yielded a more complete, though still imperfect, food web, which can better inform ecological restoration strategies. In the Everglades, this means improving resolution for indicator species (higher predators) combined with understanding limitations of their prey and food-web responses to hydrologic and biogeochemical drivers.

title: Redox-driven dissolution of bulk cadmium sulfide triggers in-root immobilization as cadmium–phosphate nanocrystals
summary: Cadmium sulfide, a sparingly soluble product of cadmium immobilization in flooded paddy soils, is generally considered environmentally inert. Here, we show that cadmium sulfide transforms under flooded soil–rice conditions, releasing labile
content: Cadmium sulfide, a sparingly soluble product of cadmium immobilization in flooded paddy soils, is generally considered environmentally inert. Here, we show that cadmium sulfide transforms under flooded soil–rice conditions, releasing labile cadmium and increasing its bioavailability. In pot experiments, cadmium sulfide increased dissolved and extractable cadmium, altered bulk pore-water geochemistry, activated iron-regulated transporters, enhanced cadmium uptake, and elevated grain cadmium above food-safety limits. Within roots, the remobilized cadmium was partly retained on cell walls and partly immobilized through phosphate-driven intracellular complexation and precipitation, forming amorphous cadmium–phosphorus–oxygen phases and crystalline cadmium–phosphate nanocrystals. Density functional theory calculations indicate that cadmium promotes phosphate-cluster nucleation and growth rather than binding preferentially to organic ligands. These findings reveal a soil-to-root transfer pathway in which phosphate-mediated immobilization provides only a partial sink and does not offset increased cadmium influx, highlighting the long-term food-safety risks of sulfide-based cadmium immobilization in flooded paddy soils. Within rice roots, cadmium is partly immobilized by cell-wall retention and phosphate-driven formation of cadmium-phosphate phases, but this sequestration does not offset the increased cadmium influx, based on sampling analysis in Minhou County, China.

title: Restoring Wetlands to Strengthen Resilience Against Climate Change
summary: Wetlands play a crucial role in climate change resilience, offering invaluable ecological services and acting as natural buffers against environmental disturbances. However, these ecosystems are increasingly vulnerable to the impacts of cli
content: Wetlands play a crucial role in climate change resilience, offering invaluable ecological services and acting as natural buffers against environmental disturbances. However, these ecosystems are increasingly vulnerable to the impacts of climate change, necessitating proactive measures to restore and conserve them. This chapter provides an in-depth exploration of wetland restoration as a proactive strategy to enhance climate resilience. It begins with an overview of the significance of wetlands in climate change resilience, emphasizing their role as vital carbon sinks and natural flood regulators. The importance of wetland restoration as a proactive measure against climate impacts is underscored, highlighting its potential to mitigate the adverse effects of climate-induced stressors such as sea-level rise and extreme weather events. The ecological benefits of wetland restoration are discussed, with a focus on the crucial role that restored wetlands play in carbon sequestration, flood regulation, and habitat provision. Additionally, this study provides an overview of different wetland restoration techniques and approaches. Restoration efforts in different geographical areas are also discussed, emphasizing the global perspective and diverse approaches to restoring wetlands worldwide. Overall, this chapter highlights the importance 44 of wetland restoration as a proactive measure to enhance climate resilience and provides insights into effective restoration practices for conserving these invaluable ecological systems, encountering the impacts of climate change.

title: Effect of ethephon concentrations and application stages on growth, physiology and yield of sorghum
summary: A field experiment was conducted at the Research Station of the College of Agriculture Al Hamidiya affiliated with the Desert Studies Center during the spring and fall seasons of 2024 to evaluate the effect of ethephon concentrations and sp
content: A field experiment was conducted at the Research Station of the College of Agriculture Al Hamidiya affiliated with the Desert Studies Center during the spring and fall seasons of 2024 to evaluate the effect of ethephon concentrations and spraying dates on growth traits yield and yield components of sorghum cultivar Giza 113. A split plot arrangement within a randomised complete block design (RCBD) with 3 replications was used. The main plots included spraying dates at 4, 6 and 8 weeks after emergence while the subplots included ethephon concentrations at 0, 100 and 200 mg L-1. The results showed that increasing ethephon concentration significantly reduced the number of days to physiological maturity as the concentration of 200 mg L-1 recorded the shortest duration in both seasons. The same concentration also showed superiority in the studied traits. Spraying at 6 weeks after emergence improved most of the studied traits particularly grain yield (GY) and its components. The interaction between 200 mg L-1 and spraying at 6 weeks produced the best performance as it recorded the highest number of grains per head (GPH), thousand-grain weight (TGW) and GY which reached 4.78 and 5.97 t ha-1 in the spring and fall seasons respectively in addition to reducing the maturity period. In contrast the control treatment without spraying combined with late spraying at 8 weeks gave the lowest value for most traits. Ethephon application also reduced plant height (PH) while improving physiological efficiency and increasing chlorophyll content.

title: Restoration Ecology in India: A Synthesis of Recent Trends, Key Actors, and Future Directions
source: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
summary: Ecological restoration has become a critical global priority. India plays a central role in this effort. This is because India has large areas of degraded land and very high biodiversity. This paper reviews developments in restoration ecolo
content: Ecological restoration has become a critical global priority. India plays a central role in this effort. This is because India has large areas of degraded land and very high biodiversity. This paper reviews developments in restoration ecology in India between 2014 and 2024. It looks at government-led initiatives, community-based efforts, individual environmental leadership, and ongoing methodological debates. The paper analyses major programmes such as the National Mission for a Green India. It also analyses the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority. It highlights a key imbalance: large-scale afforestation and monoculture plantations have often been prioritised over holistic ecosystem restoration. The paper also examines small public movements. These include community-led conservation efforts. It also covers citizen mobilisation inspired by figures such as Peepal Baba. The paper further discusses the growing popularity of the Miyawaki method. It compares this method with assisted natural regeneration and other ecologically informed approaches. The review argues that restoration success in India depends on three things. First, policy ambition must be integrated with local ecological knowledge. Second, the focus must shift from tree-planting targets to overall ecosystem functionality. Third, robust long-term scientific monitoring must be established.

title: Assessment of yield-limiting nutrients in finger millet (Eleusine coracana L.) grown in light-textured soils
source: International Journal of Research in Agronomy
summary: A field experiment was conducted during the Kharif season of 2025 at the Crop Research Centre, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel University of Agriculture and Technology, Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, Assessment of yield-limiting nutrients in finger millet
content: A field experiment was conducted during the Kharif season of 2025 at the Crop Research Centre, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel University of Agriculture and Technology, Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, Assessment of yield-limiting nutrients in finger millet (Eleusine coracana L.) grown under light-textured soil conditions. The experiment was laid out in a Randomized Block Design (RBD) with eight treatments and three replications, comprising nutrient omission treatments, the recommended dose of fertilizers (RDF), and foliar application of ZnSO₄ (0.5%) and FeSO₄ (0.2%). Balanced nutrient management significantly improved crop growth, yield attributes, and yield compared to nutrient omission treatments. The combined application of RDF with ZnSO₄ at 0.5% and FeSO₄ at 0.2% foliar spray (T₈) recorded the highest grain yield (31.50 q ha⁻¹), straw yield (62.30 q ha⁻¹), and biological yield (93.80 q ha⁻¹). Among the nutrient omission treatments, nitrogen omission (T₂) resulted in the greatest reduction in crop productivity, confirming nitrogen as the primary yield-limiting nutrient under light-textured soils. Application of RDF alone (T₅) produced 26.23 q ha⁻¹ grain yield, 53.34 q ha⁻¹ straw yield, and 79.57 q ha⁻¹ biological yield, whereas foliar application of FeSO₄ (T₆) and ZnSO₄ (T₇) further enhanced yield over RDF alone. The highest harvest index (37.71%) was recorded under T₂ (P₂O₅ + K₂O), although differences among treatments were statistically non-significant. The study concludes that the combined application of RDF with zinc and iron foliar spray is an effective and sustainable nutrient management strategy for maximizing finger millet productivity in light-textured soils.

title: Mobile‐Chain‐Assisted Flow Alignment and Interfacial Adaptation Enable Elastomeric Thermal Interface Materials with High through‐Plane Thermal Conductivity and Low Contact Thermal Resistance
summary: ABSTRACT The performance of conventional chemically cross‐linked elastomeric thermal interface materials (E‐TIMs) is fundamentally limited by the intrinsic trade‐off between through‐plane thermal conductivity and interfacial contact resista
content: ABSTRACT The performance of conventional chemically cross‐linked elastomeric thermal interface materials (E‐TIMs) is fundamentally limited by the intrinsic trade‐off between through‐plane thermal conductivity and interfacial contact resistance. In this work, we propose a mobile‐chain‐assisted flow‐alignment and interfacial‐adaptation strategy by introducing free high‐molecular‐weight hydroxyl‐functional silicone chains into a silicone cross‐linked network. The mobile hydroxyl‐functional chains act as a dual regulator: they facilitate flow‐field‐induced vertical alignment of carbon fibers during extrusion and endow the elastomer matrix with enhanced interfacial wettability, chain mobility, and adaptive conformability. Consequently, the fabricated V‐cSi/fSi‐OH/CF TIM achieves a remarkable through‐plane thermal conductivity of 54.7 W·m −1 ·K −1 . More importantly, the mobile hydroxyl‐functional chains enable near‐conformal interfacial adaptation with heat‐sink surfaces even under a low pressure (1 psi), yielding a calculated contact thermal resistance of 11.2 K·mm 2 ·W −1 (an 84% reduction compared to conventional cross‐linked counterparts). This mobile‐chain‐assisted design strategy provides a generalizable route for developing elastomeric TIMs that combine efficient through‐plane heat conduction with low‐resistance interfacial heat transfer.

title: Multilayer soil moisture depletion intensifies drought impacts on global ecosystems
summary: When soil moisture across all layers of the entire profile is depleted, ecosystems face the highest risk because they lose all vertical buffering capacity against drought. However, these vertically compound soil moisture droughts, in which
content: When soil moisture across all layers of the entire profile is depleted, ecosystems face the highest risk because they lose all vertical buffering capacity against drought. However, these vertically compound soil moisture droughts, in which every soil layer suffers simultaneous water deficits, have been largely ignored because previous monitoring and risk assessments relied on entire-profile mean soil moisture. Here we identify vertically (0–100 cm) compound droughts worldwide during warm seasons of 1981–2020 using multilayer soil moisture products. Their annual duration and ratio have increased across more than half of global lands over the past four decades, with pronounced hotspots in southwestern North America, South America, Africa, mid-latitude Eurasia, southeastern Asia and Australia. Vertically compound droughts cause substantial declines in ecosystem productivity, particularly in forests and croplands, threatening carbon sink stability and food security. By contrast, diagnosing drought solely from entire-profile averages causes an overestimation of vertically compound drought duration by about 128.3% but an underestimation of associated ecosystem losses by about 27.8%. These projections and systematic biases highlight the urgency of developing multilayer monitoring, mitigation and adaptation strategies for vertically compound droughts. Vertically compound soil moisture droughts—when all soil layers are depleted—have intensified worldwide, driving sharper ecosystem losses than single-layer droughts, according to global analyses of multilayer soil moisture.

title: Global spatial heterogeneity of changes in vegetation resistance to compound drought and heat events during 2001–2020
summary: : Vegetation resistance plays a vital role in sustaining ecosystem stability, but it is increasingly threatened by the rising frequency of compound drought and heat events (CDHEs). Despite the growing prevalence of these stressors, how vege
content: : Vegetation resistance plays a vital role in sustaining ecosystem stability, but it is increasingly threatened by the rising frequency of compound drought and heat events (CDHEs). Despite the growing prevalence of these stressors, how vegetation resistance is changing and what mechanisms underlie these changes remain unclear, limiting our capacity to project future carbon sinks. This study examines the responses of leaf area index (LAI) and solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) to CDHEs. Using a geographic detector (GD) model, we explore underlying factors governing the spatial distribution of vegetation resistance changes globally during 2001–2020. The results show that CDHEs occur every 2.92 years on average and approximately 80% of vegetation response times (RTs) fall within a 2–4 mon window. Northern ecosystems generally exhibit longer RTs than southern ones. The spatial patterns of vegetation resistance, assessed through both LAI and SIF, are broadly consistent. However, SIF-based assessments indicate low resistance across a larger number of regions. Over 2001–2020, 52.1% of areas show a decrease in LAI-based resistance, and 47.1% show a similar trend for SIF-based resistance. Some regions, such as central North America and southern South America demonstrate a notable decline in resistance, whereas western Australia and central China show an increase in resistance. GD analysis identifies key climate factors, such as vapor pressure deficit, temperature, and surface net solar radiation, as the primary drivers of vegetation resistance changes in most hotspot regions. These factors interact through nonlinear effects, further influencing vegetation resistance. Overall, this study offers a scientific foundation for improving ecosystem conservation and enhancing regional ecological resistance.

title: Changes in Southern Ocean Circulation Across Climate Transitions and Their Impacts on Carbon and Heat Fluxes
summary: Today, the Southern Ocean (SO) is the primary sink of anthropogenic heat and carbon, yet anthropogenic warming and ozone depletion have altered its circulation and stratification, creating uncertainty about the persistence of this sink. Evi
content: Today, the Southern Ocean (SO) is the primary sink of anthropogenic heat and carbon, yet anthropogenic warming and ozone depletion have altered its circulation and stratification, creating uncertainty about the persistence of this sink. Evidence from the last glacial period and deglaciation shows that the SO played a central role in past climate transitions by releasing heat and carbon to the atmosphere through sea-ice retreat and enhanced ventilation of deep and abyssal waters. Antarctic warming during weak Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) phases was likely amplified by SO feedbacks, such as increased deep-ocean convection, and a strengthening/poleward shift of Southern Hemisphere westerlies. However, changes in the abyssal circulation, its interaction with North Atlantic Deep Water, and its impact on oceanic carbon during the deglaciation remain debated. Finally, although sediment and modeling evidence suggests that Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS) discharge can significantly affect climate and biogeochemistry, clear signals remain scarce in existing proxy records-either masked by dominant AMOC-driven variability or unresolved due to limited temporal resolution. Improved model representation and proxy records are needed to clarify the role of abyssal circulation and the interaction between the ocean and AIS.

title: Physiological basis of evaluation of grape varieties under northern dry zone of Karnataka
source: International Journal of Research in Agronomy
summary: A study entitled “Physiological basis of evaluation of grape varieties under northern dry zone of Karnataka” was conducted at Horticulture Research and Extension Centre, Vijayapur (Tidagundi). For the experiment, ten grape varieties were se
content: A study entitled “Physiological basis of evaluation of grape varieties under northern dry zone of Karnataka” was conducted at Horticulture Research and Extension Centre, Vijayapur (Tidagundi). For the experiment, ten grape varieties were selected and data concerning vine physiological, growth, yield and quality parameters of the ten varieties were recorded. The experiment was laid out in Randomized Block Design (RBD) with ten varieties and three replications. The varieties were Red Globe, Fantasy Seedless, Crimson Seedless, Manjari Shyama (A-18/3), Nanasaheb Purple Seedless, Sharad Seedless, Merbein Seedless, 2A-Clone, Manjari Kishmish (Kishmish Rozavis White) and Thompson Seedless. Among all the varieties studied, the variety Thompson Seedless, followed by Manjari Kishmish demonstrated its superiority among green grape varieties, boasting robust physiological characteristics, strong growth parameters and high yields. In coloured grape varieties, Crimson Seedless and Manjari Shyama emerged as the top performer, primarily due to its exceptional fruit quality attributes, including firmness and relatively higher organoleptic qualities.

title: Observation‐Based Constraints on Anthropogenic Carbonyl Sulfide Emissions in Southeastern China From High‐Frequency Measurements in Urban Guangzhou
summary: Abstract Carbonyl sulfide (COS) is the most abundant sulfur‐containing trace gas in the troposphere and an important tracer of terrestrial gross primary productivity (GPP), but its application is limited by uncertain regional emissions, esp
content: Abstract Carbonyl sulfide (COS) is the most abundant sulfur‐containing trace gas in the troposphere and an important tracer of terrestrial gross primary productivity (GPP), but its application is limited by uncertain regional emissions, especially in East Asia. Here we present one year (April 2022–March 2023) of 3‐hourly online COS measurements at an urban receptor site in Guangzhou, south China. The annual mean COS mixing ratio was 599.8 ± 6.2 pptv, while the annual mean urban baseline derived from the lowest 25% of observations in a centered 7‐day moving window was 569.2 ± 5.4 pptv, about 16.1% higher than the remote National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration baseline at Mauna Loa Observatory on their respective calibration scales. COS exhibited a winter maximum (741.6 ± 7.7 pptv) and a summer minimum (478.1 ± 2.9 pptv). Trajectory clustering indicates that this contrast primarily reflected a monsoon‐driven transition from marine‐influenced transport and stronger ventilation in summer to continental influence and less efficient dispersion in winter; terrestrial uptake may have made a secondary contribution to the summer decline. Weighted potential source contribution function analyses associated elevated COS with industrialized corridors in eastern and southern China, while fire hotspots indicated possible episodic contributions from biomass burning. A CHCl 3 ‐based tracer‐ratio analysis yielded a receptor‐based constraint of 41.0 ± 6.4 Gg yr −1 for the anthropogenic COS emissions in southeastern China that co‐varied with CHCl 3 in air masses reaching Guangzhou. These results provide new observational benchmarks for improving regional COS inventories and for reducing anthropogenic bias in COS‐based estimates of GPP over East Asia.

title: Exploratory comparative profiling of 22 macro- and trace elements reveals disrupted elemental homeostasis in colorectal cancer tissues
