content: Superabsorbent carbon-based materials (CB) have been shown to ameliorate saline soils in arid regions; however, their synergistic effects with flue gas desulfurization gypsum (FGD) on soil health and seed cotton yield remain poorly understood. A field experiment was conducted with six treatments: control, FGD, biochar (BC), BC + FGD, CB, and CB + FGD to evaluate the individual and combined effects of these amendments on soil properties and cotton performance. The results showed that all amendment treatments improved soil aggregate structure, water retention capacity, salt suppression, and nutrient availability, thereby promoting cotton growth and increasing seed cotton yield. Although treatment advantages varied among individual indicators, CB + FGD showed the greatest overall improvement. Compared with the control, CB + FGD increased the mean weight diameter (MWD) of soil aggregates by 73.33% and decreased total soluble salts (TSS) by 21.37% in the 0–20 cm plow layer, while achieving the highest seed cotton yield of 6125.7 kg ha −1 . Other indicators, including geometric mean diameter (GMD), water-stable macroaggregates, Na + concentration, electrical conductivity (EC), soil nutrients, soil moisture, plant growth, and root traits, also improved markedly. Random forest analysis identified soil aggregates and salinity as core drivers of soil health. Partial least squares path modelling further revealed that CB + FGD enhanced aggregate structure and moisture, which in turn drove salt suppression and nutrient retention, indirectly promoting cotton growth and seed cotton yield. These findings suggest that improving soil structure and alleviating salt stress should be prioritized in saline-alkali drylands. Combining CB with FGD offers a promising strategy for sustainable agriculture in arid regions.

title: Strategic Procurement Prioritization for Sustainable Aviation Fuel: An Integrated Pythagorean Fuzzy SWARA–RAM Decision Support Framework
source: Spectrum of Engineering and Management Sciences
summary: The transition toward sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) has become a strategic priority for commercial airlines seeking to reduce aviation-related emissions while maintaining secure and economically viable fuel procurement. However, procureme
content: The transition toward sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) has become a strategic priority for commercial airlines seeking to reduce aviation-related emissions while maintaining secure and economically viable fuel procurement. However, procurement decisions remain challenging because airlines must simultaneously balance environmental objectives, supply security, economic feasibility, operational considerations, and evolving policy requirements under substantial uncertainty. Existing studies primarily focus on technological production pathways or policy issues, whereas systematic evaluations of alternative SAF procurement strategies from an airline procurement perspective remain limited. This study develops an integrated multi-criteria decision support framework to prioritize sustainable aviation fuel procurement strategies for commercial airlines under uncertainty. The proposed framework combines Pythagorean fuzzy sets, Stepwise Weight Assessment Ratio Analysis (SWARA), and the Reliability, Availability and Maintainability (RAM) method to represent uncertainty in expert judgments, determine the relative importance of evaluation criteria, and prioritize procurement alternatives. The findings indicate that lifecycle carbon reduction potential and local emission reduction are the highest-priority evaluation criteria, while partnership or investment in SAF production facilities represents the highest-ranked procurement strategy according to the participating experts, with comparative analysis using the COPRAS method confirming the consistency of the ranking results. The proposed framework provides structured decision support for strategic procurement planning by integrating environmental, economic, operational, and geopolitical considerations, offering expert-informed guidance for airline procurement managers and a foundation for future studies incorporating operational and market-based evidence.

title: Evaluating Off-Grid Energy Solutions for Rural Demand in Brazil – A Case study
source: Latin American Journal of Energy Research
summary: Recently, Electrical energy enables the operation of machinery, heat generation, and information transmission. This energy is generated, transmitted, and distributed until it reaches the end consumer; however, interruptions in the power sup
content: Recently, Electrical energy enables the operation of machinery, heat generation, and information transmission. This energy is generated, transmitted, and distributed until it reaches the end consumer; however, interruptions in the power supply pose significant challenges, especially for rural producers in the state of Goiás, who face losses such as food spoilage and the death of animals in breeding facilities. With the advancement of distributed generation, consumers are increasingly able to produce their own energy, becoming prosumers. This study presents a case analysis of a rural property located in Cezarina, Goiás, Brazil, aiming to identify the most suitable solution for ensuring a reliable energy supply through alternative generation sources. Three scenarios are evaluated: (1) Grid Electricity + Backup Generator, (2) Grid Electricity + Off-Grid Photovoltaic System, and (3) Grid Electricity + Off-Grid Photovoltaic System + Battery Storage. Based on the property’s energy demand, equipment is dimensioned for each configuration, and a financial analysis is conducted using key indicators such as Net Present Value (NPV), Internal Rate of Return (IRR), Discounted Payback Period, and Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE). The results indicate that the "Grid Electricity + Off-Grid Photovoltaic System + Battery Storage" scenario presents the best overall feasibility. Although it requires an initial investment nearly nine times higher than the traditional "Grid Electricity + Backup Generator" configuration, it offers a lower LCOE and demonstrates greater long-term financial and operational advantages over a 30-year analysis horizon.

title: How much is too much? Carbon tax thresholds for climate mitigation and social equity
summary: This study investigates how carbon taxation simultaneously affects climate change mitigation and income inequality through potential nonlinear threshold effects. Using a dynamic panel threshold approach and data from 70 countries over the p
content: This study investigates how carbon taxation simultaneously affects climate change mitigation and income inequality through potential nonlinear threshold effects. Using a dynamic panel threshold approach and data from 70 countries over the period 2000–2022, the analysis identifies two critical turning points in the effectiveness of carbon taxation. The results show that a carbon tax below $31 per tonne of CO₂ fails to generate sufficient incentives to reduce emissions. Furthermore, while a tax exceeding this level becomes environmentally effective, it also introduces a significant social trade-off: once the tax surpasses $84 per ton of CO₂, it tends to worsen income inequality by disproportionately affecting low-income households. This highlights a narrow policy window where carbon pricing is both environmentally effective and socially neutral. To achieve both objectives, policymakers should adopt a dual strategy — setting carbon taxes above the environmental threshold while simultaneously redistributing revenues to offset regressive effects. Robustness tests using an alternative carbon tax proxy and multiple climate indicators (CO₂ emissions, precipitation, humidity, and temperature) confirm the consistency of the results. Overall, the study provides new empirical evidence on how the precise calibration of carbon taxation can balance sustainability and equity goals in climate policy.

title: Microbial enzyme-driven carbon-nitrogen cycling processes of greenhouse gases in sandy sediments of river-oasis systems in arid regions
summary: Arid inland rivers are important components of the land–water–ocean continuum, yet the linkages among sediment texture, microbial-mediated processes, and greenhouse gas (GHG) production remain poorly understood in sandy systems. Here, we in
content: Arid inland rivers are important components of the land–water–ocean continuum, yet the linkages among sediment texture, microbial-mediated processes, and greenhouse gas (GHG) production remain poorly understood in sandy systems. Here, we investigated surface (0–5 cm) and subsurface (5–10 cm) sediments from the Niya River Basin, a desert–oasis agricultural river in northwestern China, by integrating sediment particle-size characterization, physicochemical measurements, extracellular enzyme assays, GHG production experiments, and multivariate analyses. We examined how sediment texture and carbon–nitrogen substrate availability regulate enzyme activities and CO₂, CH₄, and N₂O production potentials. Sediments were dominated by sand (>78%) but exhibited pronounced spatial heterogeneity in enzyme activities and GHG production. Localized hotspots of enzyme activities and CH₄/N₂O production were associated with enriched TOC, TN, and NH₄ + . Multivariate analyses revealed depth-dependent environmental associations: surface processes were primarily linked to TOC and pH, whereas very coarse sand showed increased relative importance in subsurface sediments, particularly for GHG production. These findings demonstrate that sandy sediments in arid inland rivers are not inert environments; rather, carbon–nitrogen substrate availability and particle-size heterogeneity jointly shape microbial enzyme-mediated transformation processes and spatially variable GHG production potentials.

title: Multidimensional contemporaneous prediction of harmonized consumer price index levels across countries using reproducible machine learning and deep learning models
summary: Accurate modeling of the consumer price index (CPI) is important for inflation monitoring and policy analysis. This study develops a multidimensional cross-country framework for CPI prediction and, in response to reproducibility concerns, r
content: Accurate modeling of the consumer price index (CPI) is important for inflation monitoring and policy analysis. This study develops a multidimensional cross-country framework for CPI prediction and, in response to reproducibility concerns, replaces the principal neural-architecture ranking with a fully re-estimated and documented benchmark. The reproducible benchmark uses the supplied 545-observation, 39-country common-feature panel for 1995–2020, partitioned chronologically into 337 training observations (through 2014), 102 validation observations (2015–2017), and 106 holdout observations (2018–2020). For each country-year, CNN, RNN, and LSTM models receive up to the four most recent observed predictor vectors ending in year t; CPI itself is excluded from the input. Scaling is fitted on the training period only. Final architectures, selected hyperparameters, trainable-parameter counts, software versions, five fixed random seeds (101, 202, 303, 404, 505), per-seed holdout predictions, selected checkpoints, learning curves, and three expanding-window fold forecasts are reported and archived. The CNN contains 2,433 trainable parameters, the RNN 641, and the LSTM 7,073. Across five seeds, CNN has the lowest mean RMSE (0.1943, SD = 0.0094) and ranks first by RMSE in all five runs; LSTM has the lowest mean MAE (0.1128) and MAPE (0.0803). CNN also has the lowest RMSE in each of the three 2018–2020 expanding-window folds. Because the original TFT, GNN, and hybrid implementations cannot be reconstructed from the archived materials, they are removed from the principal comparative conclusions rather than assigned reconstructed architectures. The full-feature CatBoost/SHAP analysis and the lagged ex-ante benchmark branch remain separate analyses with their original information-set qualifications. The resulting conclusions emphasize reproducible performance, metric-specific trade-offs, and model-ranking stability rather than unsupported architecture superiority. Any legacy TFT, GNN, or hybrid point estimates that remain solely for traceability are explicitly treated as archived exploratory results and are not used for reproducibility claims, model rankings, inferential comparisons, or substantive conclusions. The chronological split is instantiated before every sample-dependent fitting operation, and the fitted StandardScaler objects, target-normalization parameters, split-membership files, and sequence-construction audits are preserved for the main split and for each expanding-window fold. No sample-dependent variable screening, PCA, graph construction, wavelet transformation, or imputation is used in this confirmatory principal benchmark; historical analyses requiring unavailable preprocessing objects remain outside the confirmatory conclusions. Because the exact row-level inclusion key and complete variable matrix for the historical 396-observation full-feature branch are not available in the current archive, that branch is retained only as archived explor

title: Optimizing Environmental Sanitation Management at The Perawang Container Terminal to Achieve A Healthy Port
summary: Environmental sanitation management in port areas has become increasingly important amid the growing intensity of global logistics activities. Perawang Container Terminal (PCT), one of the major ports in Riau Province, continues to face sev
content: Environmental sanitation management in port areas has become increasingly important amid the growing intensity of global logistics activities. Perawang Container Terminal (PCT), one of the major ports in Riau Province, continues to face several unresolved sanitation issues, including the absence of a waste segregation system, temporary waste storage facilities that do not meet technical standards, irregular monitoring of clean water quality, management of hazardous and toxic waste (Bahan Berbahaya dan Beracun [B3]) without the required permits, and the absence of a disease vector control program. These conditions indicate a gap between current practices and healthy port standards as stipulated in Indonesian Ministry of Health Regulation No. 44 of 2014. This study aimed to assess the existing condition of environmental sanitation management at PCT, identify supporting and inhibiting factors, and formulate optimization strategies to achieve a sustainable healthy port. A qualitative case study approach was employed, involving 10 key informants selected through purposive sampling from PCT management, the Class I Health Quarantine Office of Pekanbaru, and the surrounding port community. Primary data were collected through observations using the Healthy Port Self-Assessment Form, semi-structured interviews, and document review, while secondary data were obtained from relevant institutional records. Existing conditions were analyzed descriptively, followed by SWOT analysis and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to determine priority optimization strategies. These strategies were integrated with the Triple Bottom Line framework, encompassing environmental, social, and economic dimensions, to support the development of a sustainable healthy port.

title: Drought development characteristics modulate global dry–wet abrupt alternation through distinct land–atmosphere feedbacks
summary: Rapid transitions from drought to extreme precipitation can trigger cascading impacts, but the influence of antecedent drought development on subsequent precipitation remains unclear. Dry–wet abrupt alternation events were identified using
content: Rapid transitions from drought to extreme precipitation can trigger cascading impacts, but the influence of antecedent drought development on subsequent precipitation remains unclear. Dry–wet abrupt alternation events were identified using a global event-scale framework and separated into successive dry and wet phases. These events followed approximately 32% of droughts, and their frequency increased significantly in 58% of the 26 IPCC-SREX regions assessed in 1951-2020. Model-based analysis showed that drought-development characteristics contributed 25.7% of the predictive information distinguishing droughts with and without subsequent extreme precipitation. Rapid and intense soil-moisture decline was associated with earlier, more convective precipitation, particularly in mid- and high-latitude climate-transition regions, whereas prolonged and severe drought development was associated with delayed, more stratiform precipitation, especially in arid and tropical regions. Here, we show that antecedent drought development is linked to distinct, region-dependent pathways from drought to extreme precipitation, providing a basis for anticipating compound hydrological extremes. The study finds that nearly one-third of droughts worldwide are followed by extreme precipitation, with drought-development characteristics distinguishing distinct pathways to these dry–wet transitions.

title: Public Emotions and Climate Change Awareness: Understanding Shifting Perceptions for Sustainable Futures
summary: ABSTRACT Understanding the evolving emotional landscape surrounding climate change is critical for developing effective environmental strategies and communication. This study offers an analysis of public emotions toward human‐induced climat
content: ABSTRACT Understanding the evolving emotional landscape surrounding climate change is critical for developing effective environmental strategies and communication. This study offers an analysis of public emotions toward human‐induced climate change by leveraging big data analytics and machine learning techniques on social media content from platform X. Grounded in the collective emotions framework, we trained a model to classify emotional responses—joy, anger, fear, sadness, disgust, and surprise—based on emotion‐related hashtags. We then analyzed climate change–related posts collected from the first week of each year between 2013 and 2022 to predict emotional trends. The findings reveal substantial year‐to‐year fluctuations in emotional expression, with fear consistently emerging as the dominant sentiment. Although no clear linear trajectory was identified, the results highlight patterns of public concern and awareness. By integrating computational methods with social theory, this research contributes to a deeper understanding of how collective emotions surrounding climate change evolve, offering implications for policymakers, communicators, and organizations aiming to enhance climate engagement and sustainable behavior.

title: Melatonin Mitigates the Impacts of Recurrent Water Deficit in Robusta Coffee Plants by Modulating Photosynthesis and Biomass Partitioning
summary: Melatonin (N-acetyl-5-methoxytryptamine) is a regulatory molecule with potential to increase plant tolerance to water stress by modulating stomatal function, redox balance, and photosynthetic efficiency. However, its physiological effects d
content: Melatonin (N-acetyl-5-methoxytryptamine) is a regulatory molecule with potential to increase plant tolerance to water stress by modulating stomatal function, redox balance, and photosynthetic efficiency. However, its physiological effects depend on dose, species, and stress intensity, and studies on Coffea canephora under recurrent drought are scarce. This study evaluated the effects of exogenous melatonin (0, 100, 200, 300, and 400 µM) on young plants of conilon coffee genotype 02 (Clone V12) subjected to three consecutive cycles of water deficit and rehydration. The experiment was conducted in a greenhouse using a randomized block design, with evaluations of gas exchange, water potential, and biomass allocation. Melatonin improved physiological recovery after rehydration, particularly at 100 and 300 µM during the second stress cycle, when photosynthesis reached values similar to the irrigated control. The 400 µM treatment maintained root dry mass close to the control under prolonged deficit, suggesting preferential biomass allocation to the root system. Overall, melatonin effects were more pronounced during recovery than stress, indicating a possible priming action. These results highlight the potential of melatonin as a phytoprotective agent in C. canephora, although responses depend on dose and stress cycle.

title: Technical Note: Sub-millimetre real-time GNSS precipitable water vapor conversion using AI weather forecast foundation models
summary: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSSs) networks provide high-quality, high-temporal-resolution (5-min) tropospheric delay products at over 20,000 stations worldwide. However, the vertical meteorological information remains inaccessible
content: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSSs) networks provide high-quality, high-temporal-resolution (5-min) tropospheric delay products at over 20,000 stations worldwide. However, the vertical meteorological information remains inaccessible at most sites due to the lack of in-situ meteorological sensors, which makes it challenging to convert high-accuracy tropospheric products to accurate precipitable water vapor (PWV). The continued development of empirical models has provided feasible solutions, but their inherent modelling errors continue to restrict the accuracy of real-time PWV conversion, and the current optimal method is still limited to the 2–3 mm level. We propose a real-time high-accuracy GNSS PWV conversion method based on artificial intelligence weather forecast foundation models. This innovative approach efficiently calculates path-integrated zenith hydrostatic delay (ZHD) and weighted mean temperature (Tm) at any global location locally within seconds, bypassing inaccuracies inherent in empirical ZHD and Tm models, significantly reducing PWV errors. The method is evaluated on three representative foundation models, Pangu-Weather, GraphCast, and FengWu, showing root-mean-square errors of real-time GNSS PWV less than 1 mm (refer to 5-day forecast time, for the 5-day delay in ERA5 reported by ECMWF). It offers a robust solution for real-time GNSS PWV conversion and has the potential to facilitate the assimilation of the increasing GNSS observations into global numerical weather prediction. In turn, employing more accurate atmospheric states that assimilate more GNSS observations as input can further enhance the method itself.

title: Assessing Government Subsidies for Reducing Pesticide Use: A Meta‐Analysis
summary: ABSTRACT In the efforts being made by governments to reduce pesticide use, subsidies are an important instrument to encourage farmers to adopt more sustainable practices. Yet, their effectiveness remains uncertain due to diverse designs and
content: ABSTRACT In the efforts being made by governments to reduce pesticide use, subsidies are an important instrument to encourage farmers to adopt more sustainable practices. Yet, their effectiveness remains uncertain due to diverse designs and contexts. To date, there are no studies that provide systematic synthesized evidence on the potentially heterogeneous effects of subsidies on pesticide use. The present study addresses this gap by conducting a meta‐analysis of 39 empirical studies (208 models) from the EU and other developed countries that examine the effects of subsidies on (i) direct measurement of pesticide use and (ii) indirect measurement of pesticide use based on the adoption of pesticide‐reducing practices. Using probit meta‐regressions and qualitative appraisal, we find two key results. First, for EU studies, Pillar I and Pillar II subsidies from the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) have opposite effects on pesticide use: Pillar II subsidies are more likely than Pillar I subsidies to reduce pesticide use. Second, if we consider studies from both the EU and the US, subsidies that target adoption of whole‐farm systems or bundles of practices outperform those targeting a single practice in reducing pesticide use. We provide some policy recommendations for policy design and highlight future research priorities.

title: Are just energy transition investment plans tailored to country-specific challenges? Comparing South Africa and Indonesia
summary: This paper provides a comparative analysis of the Just Energy Transition Investment Plans (JET-IPs) of South Africa and Indonesia, focusing on their effectiveness in driving private investment in renewable energy (RE). Using a three-level f
content: This paper provides a comparative analysis of the Just Energy Transition Investment Plans (JET-IPs) of South Africa and Indonesia, focusing on their effectiveness in driving private investment in renewable energy (RE). Using a three-level framework, it examines country-specific barriers and enablers at the country, programme, and project levels. Both JET-IPs aim to align economic development and emission reduction goals, with significant reliance on private investment for RE projects. The analysis reveals key differences in energy policy frameworks, sectoral planning approaches, and governance structures between the two countries. It underscores the pivotal role of concessional finance and regulatory reforms in addressing investment risks, emphasizing the need for stronger institutional coordination and long-term planning to accelerate the energy transition. Lessons from the two JET-IPs offer insights for other countries embarking on similar initiatives, particularly in tailoring energy transition strategies to address unique domestic challenges.

title: Recent Advances and Challenges in Single‐Atom Catalysts for Thermocatalytic CO 2 Hydrogenation
summary: ABSTRACT Thermocatalytic hydrogenation of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) offers a promising route for carbon recycling and sustainable chemical production, yet its efficiency and selectivity are limited by the chemical inertness of CO 2 and the str
content: ABSTRACT Thermocatalytic hydrogenation of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) offers a promising route for carbon recycling and sustainable chemical production, yet its efficiency and selectivity are limited by the chemical inertness of CO 2 and the structural complexity of conventional heterogeneous catalysts. In recent years, single‐atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as an attractive platform for CO 2 hydrogenation due to their atomically defined active sites, high metal utilization efficiency, and tunable electronic structures. This review summarizes recent advances in SACs for thermocatalytic CO 2 hydrogenation, with emphasis on structure‐activity relationships, reaction mechanisms, and selectivity control toward C 1 and economically more valuable C 2 + products. We highlight how coordination environment, metal‐support interactions, and spatial confinement govern the electron transfer and catalytic performance. Emerging strategies such as cooperative and cascade catalysis, single atom‐zeolite coupling, and confinement engineering are emphasized for overcoming intrinsic limitations of isolated single‐atom sites. Finally, remaining challenges and future opportunities are outlined, focusing on catalyst stability, scalability, and the rational integration of SACs into industrially relevant catalytic architectures.

title: Decarbonizing Air Transport: Policy Pathways, Sustainable Aviation Fuels, and Airline Transition Strategies
source: Journal of Airline and Airport Management
summary: Purpose: This study develops an integrated policy–technology–airport–strategy framework to examine aviation decarbonization pathways under uncertainty. Specifically, it investigates how climate policy instruments, sustainable aviation fuel
content: Purpose: This study develops an integrated policy–technology–airport–strategy framework to examine aviation decarbonization pathways under uncertainty. Specifically, it investigates how climate policy instruments, sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) deployment, airport infrastructure readiness, and heterogeneous airline strategic responses jointly influence long-term emissions reduction trajectories. The study seeks to address important gaps in the aviation sustainability literature by explicitly incorporating airport management, airline heterogeneity, and probabilistic transition dynamics within a unified analytical framework.Design/methodology: The study adopts a scenario-based systems modelling approach that integrates institutional theory, socio-technical transition theory, and strategic firm behavior. A transparent Monte Carlo simulation framework is developed and calibrated using publicly available aviation, energy, and climate-policy data. Three transition scenarios—conservative, moderate, and accelerated—are evaluated over the 2025–2050 period using 10,000 simulation iterations per scenario. The model explicitly incorporates stochastic demand growth, SAF cost trajectories, airport infrastructure readiness, differentiated airline business models, and multiple policy instruments, including carbon pricing, SAF mandates, production subsidies, and infrastructure support.Findings: The results indicate that aviation decarbonization exhibits strongly non-linear and threshold-dependent dynamics. Deep emissions reductions do not arise from individual policy instruments alone but require coordinated interactions among policy intensity, SAF production expansion, airport infrastructure readiness, and airline strategic adaptation. SAF deployment emerges as the dominant medium-term decarbonization pathway, although its effectiveness remains highly sensitive to production costs, infrastructure constraints, and airline procurement behavior. The analysis further demonstrates that network carriers adapt more rapidly than low-cost and regional airlines, while major hub airports become critical nodes for SAF deployment. Airport infrastructure readiness is identified as a significant enabling factor, with insufficient infrastructure substantially slowing transition pathways even under strong policy conditions.Research limitations/implications: The simulation represents a stylized systems-transition model rather than a fully disaggregated airline-network optimization model. Airport readiness is operationalized using an aggregate infrastructure index, and non-CO₂ climate effects are not explicitly modelled. Nevertheless, the framework provides a transparent and replicable foundation for future research integrating agent-based modelling, airport-specific infrastructure analysis, endogenous SAF supply-chain dynamics, and regional aviation transition pathways.Practical implications: The findings suggest that aviation decarbonization strategies should extend beyond carb

title: Global surveillance of offshore oil slicks: Linking satellite detection with marine biodiversity patterns and conservation priorities
summary: By combining satellite technology with ecological risk analysis, this study establishes a scalable global framework for tracking the environmental effects of chronic oil slicks. We used Sentinel-1 SAR from SkyTruth's Cerulean platform to de
content: By combining satellite technology with ecological risk analysis, this study establishes a scalable global framework for tracking the environmental effects of chronic oil slicks. We used Sentinel-1 SAR from SkyTruth's Cerulean platform to detect surface slicks potentially attributable to over 24,000 fixed oil infrastructure and 326 FxO operating locations. We validated >2000 detections through expert review. This approach generates a replicable global database of offshore oil pollution sources, exemplifying a systematic method for identifying chronic polluters. We ranked offshore oil sources globally and within European and Mediterranean EEZs based on the percentage of satellite captures that contain attributed oil slicks. We overlaid validated slick locations with marine ecoregions, protected areas, and species occurrence data from the Map of Life. For nine identified chronically polluted regions-five global and four European/Mediterranean-we extracted species assemblages across concentric 50 km buffers. Chronic oil slicking correlated with consistent differences in assemblage composition and threatened species indicators. Species richness remains relatively stable across distance classes, but species composition shifts significantly. In European/Mediterranean waters, slick proximity explained >40% of the variation in community structure, surpassing the influence of fishing intensity or coastal proximity. Globally, polygons closer to chronic slick sites contain higher threatened-species representation in the Map of Life species lists. Beta diversity partitioning suggested that turnover dominated compositional differences among slick-proximate versus farther polygons, which supports compositional differences not explained by richness alone. These results pinpoint pollution hotspots with elevated ecological vulnerability, offering a pathway to align environmental monitoring with spatial conservation priorities.

title: Agri-Food Waste as a Source of Active Ingredients for Plant-Protection Products
summary: Can waste serve as a source of known or novel molecules for plant disease management? This review explores this question, which is closely linked to the necessity of mitigating the environmental impact of agriculture, specifically in terms
content: Can waste serve as a source of known or novel molecules for plant disease management? This review explores this question, which is closely linked to the necessity of mitigating the environmental impact of agriculture, specifically in terms of waste generation and greenhouse gas emissions. Furthermore, it addresses the increasing demand for safer, environmentally friendly alternatives to ensure sustainable plant production and protection. To satisfy these needs, research efforts over the past few decades have primarily focused on biocontrol strategies, with the valorization of waste being addressed only recently. Different approaches have been applied for extracting bioactive molecules from waste, ranging from green chemistry to microbial fermentation. We discuss secondary metabolites, elicitors, and biosurfactants obtained chemically and from fermentation. Microorganisms growing on waste can produce biomass or spores [bioactive ingredients of plant-protection products (PPPs)] and facilitate the extraction of active compounds. Although the production of spores on waste material is now well-established on an industrial scale, the extraction of biologicals from waste and/or their production through fermentation are still at the experimental stage. The growing knowledge on the bioactivity of agri-food waste-derived molecules against phytopathogens is paving the way for the development of new PPPs suitable for integrated pest management. The waste-based PPPs pipeline described here shows strong potential to generate both established and novel, regulation-compliant compounds without sacrificing disease-control efficacy.

title: Protest, pandemic, and war: the political discourse reshaping Germany’s Energiewende
summary: Abstract Background The ongoing threat of climate change necessitates a comprehensive restructuring of national energy systems, shifting them from a fossil-fuel basis toward low-carbon pathways to achieve substantial reductions in greenhous
content: Abstract Background The ongoing threat of climate change necessitates a comprehensive restructuring of national energy systems, shifting them from a fossil-fuel basis toward low-carbon pathways to achieve substantial reductions in greenhouse gas emissions. In this context, this work examines the effects of national and global events on climate change mitigation policy, taking the German energy transition, also known as “Energiewende” as a case study. By tracing shifts in political discourse, this study examines changing prioritizations among energy policy targets and explores the circumstances that shaped discourse developments during periods of crisis and transformation, as well as the role of key triggers or pre-existing “windows of opportunity” presented by political and social events. The analysis places particular emphasis on specific systemic factors, including the Fridays For Future demonstrations, the 2021 government change, the COVID-19 Pandemic, and the war in Ukraine. Results Using a mixed qualitative/semi-quantitative discourse analysis of Bundestag plenary sessions from 2017 to 2022, the study evaluates the ongoing relevance of the energy triangle approach’s qualitative targets. The energy triangle retained its focus on the three primary energy policy objectives despite the occurrence of various significant systemic events. However, the relative prominence of these targets changed over time and temporally coincided with major systemic developments. Within the energy triangle approach, security of supply in particular assumed a distinctive role within the evolving discourse framework. Conclusions Examining Germany’s political discourse provides insight into the dynamics of energy policy debates during periods of crisis and transformation. Furthermore, the study demonstrates how analyzing parliamentary debates can inform comparative assessments of energy policy developments in various European countries and beyond.

title: Renewable energy mapping in Northeastern Morocco: A geographic information system‐based comparison of geothermal, solar, and wind potential in the Guercif‐Guilliz and Beni Snassen regions
summary: Abstract The development of hybrid renewable energy systems is increasingly recognized as a viable solution for improving energy access and system reliability in resource‐diverse but infrastructure‐limited regions. However, in Northeastern
content: Abstract The development of hybrid renewable energy systems is increasingly recognized as a viable solution for improving energy access and system reliability in resource‐diverse but infrastructure‐limited regions. However, in Northeastern Morocco, the combined renewable energy potential of geothermal, solar, and wind resources has not been assessed from a spatial and integrative perspective. This paper presents a geographic information system (GIS)‐based review and comparative analysis of geothermal, solar, and wind energy resources in Northeastern Morocco, with particular emphasis on the Guercif‐Guilliz and Beni Snassen regions. By compiling and analyzing existing geospatial, geological, and environmental datasets, the study evaluates geothermal gradients and hydrothermal manifestations alongside solar irradiance and wind field characteristics. The analysis highlights the complementarity of these renewable resources and reviews the feasibility of hybrid geothermal‐solar and geothermal‐wind systems as sustainable energy solutions for off‐grid and underserved areas. Furthermore, the paper discusses the conditions under which three‐source hybrid configurations (geothermal‐solar‐wind) may become technically and economically viable. By synthesizing dispersed data into a coherent spatial framework, this review provides a structured basis for future planning and investment, supporting Morocco's strategic objectives for renewable energy expansion and long‐term energy security.

title: A longitudinal study of Ti-6Al-4V ELI powder reuse for laser powder bed fusion in a certified medical device manufacturing facility
source: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
summary: Abstract Powder feedstock is the primary input to metal additive manufacturing processes such as laser powder bed fusion. Its characteristics are crucial for producing high-quality components. Realization of the waste reduction and cost ben
content: Abstract Powder feedstock is the primary input to metal additive manufacturing processes such as laser powder bed fusion. Its characteristics are crucial for producing high-quality components. Realization of the waste reduction and cost benefits that this technology offers requires reclaiming, processing, and reusing powder feedstock. While these benefits can be significant, there are challenges related to the industrial implementation of powder reuse, including the variability in powder quality that can propagate through to the produced material. This variability can be both negative and positive, but ultimately leads to uncertainty for both users and regulators. This means material and process qualifications are difficult to achieve when powder feedstock is being repeatedly reused. This study reports the effects of 175 Ti-6Al-4V ELI powder reuse cycles, characterized at 23, 104, and 175 reuses, in a certified medical device production facility, whereby powder was topped up with virgin powder from the same production lot after each build cycle. To the best of our knowledge, this is the longest reuse campaign reported in the literature. During this campaign, flowability improved with Hall flow rate decreasing by 5.4% and apparent density increasing by 0.8%. The particle size distribution remained stable, with net changes of no more than 2.1%. Particle elongation decreased by 2.9%, and the form factor distribution narrowed around its unchanged mean. Oxygen concentration progressively increased in both the powder (8.2%) and the produced material (25.1%). The average microhardness increased by 3.7% at all measured indentation depths, which is attributed to this oxygen pickup. All property means remained within the material specification limits for both powder and produced material throughout the reuse campaign. The findings of this study suggest that such extensive reuse campaigns can be implemented while fulfilling the requirements of industry powder material specifications, although such reuse processes do induce variability in the properties of both the powder and produced material. The degree of this variability is specific to the type of powder reuse approach implemented and the specific characteristics of the associated powder processing environments.

title: Microbial-Based Self-Healing Concrete in Railway Engineering: Current Advances and Future Opportunities
summary: Abstract Microbial-based self-healing concrete offers a promising approach to extending the service life of railway infrastructure by autonomously repairing cracks through biologically induced mineral precipitation. Key mechanisms are achie
content: Abstract Microbial-based self-healing concrete offers a promising approach to extending the service life of railway infrastructure by autonomously repairing cracks through biologically induced mineral precipitation. Key mechanisms are achieved through the metabolic activities of sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB), nitrate-reducing bacteria (NRB), ureolytic bacteria, fungi, and algae, supported by porous carriers and capsules that protect microbial viability, control activation, and enable targeted delivery of healing agents. Microbial-based self-healing performance has been evaluated through crack closure measurements, water permeability reduction, and recovery of mechanical strength, providing quantitative assessment of healing efficiency. Numerical modeling approaches help identify the governing factors that influence healing performance and enable optimization of design parameters, and machine-learning techniques provide powerful predictive capabilities for self-healing behavior, including crack closure, strength recovery, and reductions in water permeability. Field applications, such as the pioneering deployment in the Vijfeiken Tunnel and self-healing railway station structures, demonstrate significant potential for reducing maintenance needs, improving durability, and lowering environmental impact. However, future research needs to be conducted to maintain microbial viability under harsh environmental conditions, minimize associated costs and environmental impacts, experimentally validate self-healing performance under realistic service conditions, and develop intelligent predictive models to guide large-scale implementation. Effectively addressing these challenges will provide a strategic pathway for the wider adoption of microbial-based self-healing concrete in railway engineering.

title: Iron‐Catalyzed Hydrodecarboxylation of Fatty Acids From Vegetable Oils for Drop‐In Biofuel Production
summary: An iron‐catalyzed hydrodecarboxylation procedure was developed to produce drop‐in biofuels from redox‐active esters directly derived from vegetable oils. A commercially available iron salt, Fe(acac) 3 , was employed as a homogeneous catalys
content: An iron‐catalyzed hydrodecarboxylation procedure was developed to produce drop‐in biofuels from redox‐active esters directly derived from vegetable oils. A commercially available iron salt, Fe(acac) 3 , was employed as a homogeneous catalyst, while phenylsilane (PhSiH 3 ) served as an alternative hydrogen source under mild reaction conditions. After optimization, the method enabled the formation of renewable hydrocarbons with conversions exceeding 88% and yields of up to 89%. Furthermore, a one‐pot procedure was developed to simplify the overall process. In addition, the methodology was successfully applied to a variety of fatty acid mixtures obtained from a wide range of vegetable oils, affording conversions of 60%–95% and hydrocarbon yields of 15%–94%. This approach represents a promising alternative to traditional deoxygenation processes, promoting the production of biofuels from renewable and feasible feedstocks.

title: Current and potential industrial and environmental applications of chitosan and chitosan-derived nanocomposites
summary: Chitosan, a partially deacetylated derivative of chitin, has emerged as one of the most promising sustainable biopolymers because of its biodegradability, biocompatibility, low toxicity, and versatile functional chemistry. This review criti
content: Chitosan, a partially deacetylated derivative of chitin, has emerged as one of the most promising sustainable biopolymers because of its biodegradability, biocompatibility, low toxicity, and versatile functional chemistry. This review critically examines the current and emerging industrial and environmental applications of chitosan and chitosan-derived nanocomposites, with particular emphasis on the relationship between molecular structure, physicochemical properties, and functional performance. The roles of degree of deacetylation, molecular weight, crystallinity, and surface functionalization in governing adsorption capacity, antimicrobial activity, film-forming ability, and chemical reactivity are discussed. Recent advances in engineered chitosan systems, including nanoparticles, hybrid nanocomposites, and chemically modified derivatives, are evaluated for applications in wastewater treatment, portable water purification, food preservation and intelligent packaging, sustainable agriculture, drug delivery, wound healing, catalysis, and energy-related technologies. Attention is given to heavy metal and dye removal, controlled-release agrochemical systems, antimicrobial packaging materials, and targeted biomedical delivery platforms. In addition, the review highlights green synthesis approaches, circular bioeconomy opportunities, commercialization prospects, and the environmental implications of large-scale deployment. By integrating recent developments reported up to 2026, this review provides a comprehensive assessment of chitosan-based materials and identifies key research gaps related to process standardization, long-term safety, techno-economic feasibility, and industrial scalability. The findings underscore the potential of chitosan and its nanocomposites as multifunctional materials for sustainable industrial development and environmental remediation.

title: Fully model predictive control-based solar water pumping system with sensorless induction motor drive
summary: Solar water pumping systems offer a practical and sustainable solution for irrigation and water supply in remote areas without access to the electrical grid. This article proposes a standalone photovoltaic (PV) water pumping system based on
content: Solar water pumping systems offer a practical and sustainable solution for irrigation and water supply in remote areas without access to the electrical grid. This article proposes a standalone photovoltaic (PV) water pumping system based on an induction motor (IM) drive operating under a fully model predictive control (MPC) framework. The system consists of a DC–DC boost converter for maximum power point tracking (MPPT) and a three-level neutral-point-clamped (3L-NPC) inverter supplying an IM-driven centrifugal pump. Both the DC–DC and DC–AC converters are controlled using dedicated MPC schemes to maximize energy extraction from the PV system under varying environmental conditions while ensuring high-performance motor control. In addition, a weighting-factor-free control strategy based on a normalized multi-objective decision mechanism is developed for the 3L-NPC inverter to improve control performance under varying operating conditions while reducing design complexity. A model reference adaptive system (MRAS) estimator is also employed for rotor speed and flux estimation, thereby enabling sensorless operation. Simulation results demonstrate a reduction of up to 70% in PV power settling time, a decrease in total harmonic distortion from 5.26% to 2.63%, and robust control performance under changing operating conditions.

title: Coupling the FVCOM-CICE Lake Model to NOAA’s Near-Operational RRFSv1 Forecast Model over the Great Lakes Region: Impact on Lake-Effect Snow
summary: The Laurentian Great Lakes exhibit variations in lake water surface temperature and ice coverage on the time scale of days to weeks during the winter months. The hydrodynamics and thermodynamics of these freshwater lakes influence the cloud
content: The Laurentian Great Lakes exhibit variations in lake water surface temperature and ice coverage on the time scale of days to weeks during the winter months. The hydrodynamics and thermodynamics of these freshwater lakes influence the cloud formation and snow deposition in downwind regions. Lake-effect snowfall forecasts are sensitive to the evolving water temperature and ice conditions, yet the dynamic evolution of lake conditions is not commonly considered for short-range forecasting models. We implement an asynchronous, one-way coupling that supplies hourly lake surface temperature, ice fraction, ice thickness, and ice-surface temperature from NOAA’s Great Lakes Operational Forecast System (GLOFS), based on the model FVCOM-CICE, to NOAA’s Unified Forecast System (UFS). UFS’ coupling infrastructure uses the Earth System Modeling Framework (ESMF) which we enhance with an “inline” functionality for ESMF’s Community Data Models for Earth Prediction Systems (CDEPS). The lake coupling is evaluated in a 3 km UFS Short-Range Weather (SRW) configuration that resembles the near-operational Rapid Refresh Forecast System version 1 (RRFSv1). To demonstrate the lake coupling capabilities we run 60-hour hindcast experiments for five lake-effect snow events from December 2022 to January 2026 using either hourly evolving or static, initial-time lake conditions. The predicted snow water equivalent is evaluated against observational data products over regions downwind of each lake. Dynamic lake conditions influence the surface heat fluxes, and impact of snowfall is shown to vary by lake and snowfall accumulation. These results demonstrate a computationally practical pathway for incorporating time-evolving Great Lakes conditions into the UFS-SRW/RRFSv1 for short-range forecasts.

title: Characterizing spatiotemporal dynamics of hourly extreme precipitation in China with an adaptive 3D clustering approach
summary: Study region China, spanning the East Asian monsoon region and its northwestern inland transition zones, where extreme precipitation events (EPEs) show strong spatial heterogeneity and pose substantial hydrological-disaster risks. Study foc
content: Study region China, spanning the East Asian monsoon region and its northwestern inland transition zones, where extreme precipitation events (EPEs) show strong spatial heterogeneity and pose substantial hydrological-disaster risks. Study focus This study investigates the spatiotemporal evolution characteristics and propagation patterns of EPEs across China during 1985–2024. The central objective is to move beyond station-based, two-dimensional, or daily-scale descriptions and reconstruct complete precipitation-system trajectories in a continuous three-dimensional space. To achieve this, an adaptive 3D spatiotemporal clustering framework based on 3D-DBSCAN was developed and applied to ERA5 hourly precipitation data. Extreme precipitation grids were mapped into a standardized longitude-latitude-time space, while k-distance-based parameter optimization and physical constraint filtering were used to reduce subjective parameter selection and avoid artificial fragmentation of fast-moving or intermittent events. Precipitation-weighted centroids were then used to quantify event movement distance and direction, and to classify typical propagation patterns. New hydrological insights for the region The framework identified independent EPEs and revealed five dominant propagation patterns. EPEs in China show a clear northwestward movement preference, whereas southward events are infrequent and spatially limited. Northwestward events, especially ultra-long-distance events, exhibit the greatest hydrological extremeness, with longer durations, larger affected areas, and higher cumulative magnitudes. These trajectories indicate a regional “westward shift and northward leap” of extreme-rainfall activity, linked to the East Asian summer monsoon, western Pacific subtropical high, and mid-latitude westerlies.

title: Climate change, vegetation dynamics, and maize production in Mozambique: evidence from method of moments quantile regression and machine learning
summary: This study examines the impacts of climate variability and vegetation dynamics on maize production across 10 provinces in Mozambique using a balanced panel dataset covering the period 2002–2023. Following confirmation of cross-sectional dep
content: This study examines the impacts of climate variability and vegetation dynamics on maize production across 10 provinces in Mozambique using a balanced panel dataset covering the period 2002–2023. Following confirmation of cross-sectional dependence, second-generation panel techniques are employed. The Kao and Westerlund cointegration tests reveal a stable long-run relationship among the variables. Results from the Method of Moments Quantile Regression (MMQREG) indicate significant distributional heterogeneity in climate–maize relationships. Rainfall and the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) positively influence maize output, with stronger effects observed in lower-producing provinces, whereas temperature exerts a negative and statistically significant impact, particularly at the median and upper quantiles. Mediation analysis further confirms that NDVI partially transmits the effects of climatic variables to maize production, providing empirical support for the proposed climate–vegetation–production pathway. Interaction analysis shows that adequate rainfall and healthier vegetation conditions help mitigate temperature-induced stress. In addition, regional analysis across Northern, Central, and Southern Mozambique reveals substantial spatial heterogeneity, with semi-arid provinces exhibiting greater climate sensitivity. Complementary machine learning analysis identifies the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) model as the most accurate predictor of maize production, while temperature, NDVI, and rainfall emerge as the most influential predictors. The findings underscore the importance of accounting for both distributional and spatial heterogeneity in climate–agriculture linkages and highlight the need for climate-smart, region-specific interventions and data-driven forecasting tools to strengthen maize productivity and resilience in Mozambique.

title: DIAGNOSIS OF THE LEVEL OF ADOPTION OF GREEN LOGISTICS PRACTICES IN FREIGHT TRANSPORT COMPANIES IN LÁZARO CÁRDENAS, MICHOACÁN
source: Veredas do Direito Direito Ambiental e Desenvolvimento Sustentável
summary: The objective of this research was to diagnose the level of adoption of green logistics practices in federal freight transportation companies operating in Lázaro Cárdenas, Michoacán. A quantitative, descriptive, non-experimental, and cross-
content: The objective of this research was to diagnose the level of adoption of green logistics practices in federal freight transportation companies operating in Lázaro Cárdenas, Michoacán. A quantitative, descriptive, non-experimental, and cross-sectional study was conducted using a structured questionnaire that assessed the dimensions of fleet management, route optimization, energy efficiency, environmental management, and information technologies. The results show a moderate level of adoption of green practices. The sample consisted of 95 production units in the sector, whose managers answered a structured questionnaire with 35 items rated using a Likert scale. Key strengths included widespread preventive maintenance, route planning, the use of GPS systems, fuel consumption tracking, and coordination with customers to optimize deliveries. However, shortcomings were observed in the adoption of hybrid or electric vehicles, vehicle renewal based on environmental criteria, greenhouse gas emissions measurement, environmental certifications, and the formalization of environmental policies. Furthermore, training in eco-efficient driving and staff incentives have limited implementation. The main barrier identified is the high implementation costs, which restrict the adoption of clean technologies and advanced environmental practices. It is concluded that companies have primarily incorporated green actions related to operational efficiency and cost reduction, but they require financing, training, government incentives, and institutional policies that promote a transition to more sustainable transportation systems.

title: Role of Black Soldier Fly Larvae in Sub-Saharan Africa Circular Bioeconomy
summary: Insects used for feed can improve waste management and enhance food security. Black soldier fly production systems utilize diverse feedstocks, including fruits, vegetables, animal byproducts, and food waste to nourish larvae, which are then
content: Insects used for feed can improve waste management and enhance food security. Black soldier fly production systems utilize diverse feedstocks, including fruits, vegetables, animal byproducts, and food waste to nourish larvae, which are then processed into products such as live or dried larvae, protein meal, and oil for animal feed. Thus, black soldier fly larvae technology presents an innovative, circular bioeconomy solution that offers waste bioconversion and sustainable feed production.

title: Heart‐rot is not a disease: reframing wood decay in living trees
summary: When fungi are seen fruiting on tree trunks, branches and twigs, they are often automatically thought to be causing disease. Likewise, the hollowing of dead woody tissue in the centre of trunks is often instantly thought of as harmful. Yet
content: When fungi are seen fruiting on tree trunks, branches and twigs, they are often automatically thought to be causing disease. Likewise, the hollowing of dead woody tissue in the centre of trunks is often instantly thought of as harmful. Yet there is a wide diversity of tree-fungus interactions, and the majority of those involving wood decay fungi do not have negative consequences for the tree. This biologically inaccurate framing of wood decay fungi in general, and heart-rot in particular, has major consequences for research priorities, forest management, and public perceptions of fungi-tree interactions. Heart-rot has important ecological functions, to the extent that research to accelerate heart-rot is ongoing. We must actively reframe the narrative more precisely to represent the actual role of heart-rot as a functional component of tree and forest systems because the logical consequence of describing heart-rot as disease is that valuable trees and the species they support will be lost.

title: From Resilience Architecture to Implementation Friction: Integrating PSPK 1, ISO 22301, and GRC across Indonesia’s Palm Oil Value Chain- A Review
summary: Indonesia’s palm oil sector provides an unusually demanding setting in which to examine the gap between formally coherent resilience frameworks and their practical implementation. Sustainability-related financial disclosure, certification,
content: Indonesia’s palm oil sector provides an unusually demanding setting in which to examine the gap between formally coherent resilience frameworks and their practical implementation. Sustainability-related financial disclosure, certification, deforestation-free supply-chain requirements, business continuity, governance, risk and compliance (GRC), energy policy, and financial decision-making increasingly converge within a value chain characterized by heterogeneous smallholders, intermediated fresh fruit bunch transactions, contested land legality, uneven data quality, and asymmetric organizational capabilities. This qualitative literature review examines these interactions using the Indonesian palm oil sector as a sectoral use case rather than as a primary empirical case study. The synthesis identifies implementation friction as the central mechanism explaining why individually rational standards and management systems can generate difficult cross-system interfaces. Nine thematic findings reveal friction arising from regulatory layering, traceability, land legality, smallholder inclusion, physical continuity, financial translation, financing asymmetry, domestic energy policy, and assurance. The article develops a Palm Oil Resilience Implementation Architecture (PORIA) that connects regulatory alignment, identity and provenance, value-chain risk translation, financial materiality, transition financing, continuity testing, governance, assurance, and adaptive learning. The study argues that resilience depends less on adding further standards than on improving interoperability among institutions, information systems, actors, financial resources, and operational dependencies. The framework offers implications for palm oil companies, mills, smallholders, financial institutions, regulators, and assurance providers.

title: Meituan's Instant Delivery in the “Lazy Economy”: Impacts on Rider Health and Industry Growth in Hangzhou, China
summary: The rise of the “lazy person economy” has fueled demand for instant delivery services. This study aims to explore the impact of Meituan’s instant delivery service on rider health and the growth of the local delivery industry. Utilizing a se
content: The rise of the “lazy person economy” has fueled demand for instant delivery services. This study aims to explore the impact of Meituan’s instant delivery service on rider health and the growth of the local delivery industry. Utilizing a sequential explanatory research design, the study surveyed 376 respondents and interviewed 10 Meituan employees including delivery riders, technical staff and managers. The findings revealed that the riders face work pressure eventhough they come from diverse backgrounds in terms of age, gender, education, and income. Time constraints, complex routes, and safety risks emerged as the top stressors. Health issues such as sleep disorders, anxiety, and burnout were reported across all income levels, with more severe symptoms among riders with longer tenure. Despite technological advancements, manual delivery remains essential in navigating complex urban terrains, especially when personalized service is needed. However, AI-based delivery systems are increasingly being introduced to ease workload and improve efficiency. Operations managers acknowledged the need for reform and suggested humanized scheduling systems, improved safety infrastructure, and better rider support services. The study highlights the duality of Meituan’s growth. It helps in boosting economic activity and meets consumer demand, but places psychological and physical strain on its riders. Thus, a hybrid model that balances automation with human-centered practices is important for sustainable progress. This study stresses the need for policy reforms and industry innovations that protect rider well-being while sustaining the growth of China’s delivery economy, toward a more sustainable and equitable delivery system.

title: Environmental indicators and land-use change in the Amazon-Cerrado-Pantanal transition zone of Cáceres, Mato Grosso: a Pressure-State-Response assessment
source: Ambiente e Agua - An Interdisciplinary Journal of Applied Science
summary: This study analyzes the environmental indicators of the municipality of Cáceres, Mato Grosso, a territory that encompasses portions of three major Brazilian biomes: Amazon, Cerrado, and Pantanal. Due to its location at the convergence of th
content: This study analyzes the environmental indicators of the municipality of Cáceres, Mato Grosso, a territory that encompasses portions of three major Brazilian biomes: Amazon, Cerrado, and Pantanal. Due to its location at the convergence of these biomes, Cáceres represents an ecologically sensitive mosaic where land-use pressures interact with fragile transitional dynamics. The methodology combined a systematic literature review with geotechnological analysis based on data from the MapBiomas Project and Landsat images (1985–2022), integrated into the Pressure-State-Response model. The biome figures reported here refer to the fraction of each biome contained within the municipal boundary, not to the biomes in their entirety. Anthropic conversion was highest in the Amazon portion (57.8% of its area), followed by the Cerrado (33.8%) and the Pantanal (16.5%). Under a continuation of recent trends, the Amazon portion remains within the range that biome-scale studies associate with severe ecological degradation. The multivariate analysis identified cattle ranching, rather than crop expansion, as the driver whose annual dynamics most closely track native-vegetation loss. The institutional responses identified in this study encompass federal, state, and municipal legislation in environmental, economic, and social dimensions, including the Forest Code, Climate Change Policies, and specific measures for fisheries. However, gaps in implementation were revealed, particularly at the local scale. These results demand the development of integrated local environmental planning capable of articulating effective institutional responses to the ongoing environmental pressures. Keywords: biomes, deforestation, environmental indicators, environmental planning, land use.

title: Assessment of Women Involvement in the Household Energy Consumption and Other Roles Played in View to Improve and Innovating Propositions in Five Perriferic Villages of Garoua City in Benoue Division in North Cameroon
source: International Journal of Advanced Multidisciplinary Research and Studies
summary: The paper aimed to assess the poor Women in five periferic village of Garoua city depend on natural resources for house hold survival. Including walking longer distances for wood, water collesting, farming, annimal gardenning, post harvest
content: The paper aimed to assess the poor Women in five periferic village of Garoua city depend on natural resources for house hold survival. Including walking longer distances for wood, water collesting, farming, annimal gardenning, post harvest of crops.In view to improve and innovating solutions.
