title: Effects of Stropharia rugosoannulata–Tomato Rotation Coupled with Spent Mushroom Substrate Incorporation on Soil Fertility, Yield and Fruit Quality of Tomato
summary: Continuous monocropping of tomato causes soil degradation, secondary salinization, and yield decline. Mushroom–vegetable rotation coupled with spent mushroom substrate (SMS) incorporation offers a recycling strategy to mitigate these obstac
content: Continuous monocropping of tomato causes soil degradation, secondary salinization, and yield decline. Mushroom–vegetable rotation coupled with spent mushroom substrate (SMS) incorporation offers a recycling strategy to mitigate these obstacles. Here, a five-stage progressive field experiment (2023–2025, Yantai, Shandong, China) was conducted to screen the optimal local configuration of Stropharia rugosoannulata–tomato rotation and reveal its soil improvement mechanisms. The combination of variety Nieyang and an apple woodchip-based substrate achieved the highest mushroom yield, with the substrate formula (F = 11.64, p = 0.0006) dominating productivity. Deep incorporation of SMS into the 0–20 cm plow layer (M treatment) avoided the seedling stress and mortality caused by surface mulching and increased the marketable yield of the large-fruited tomato R35 by 28.0% (79,560 kg·ha−1, p < 0.05) without altering fruit soluble solids (p = 0.611). Two consecutive rotation years increased soil organic carbon by 17.6% (from 3.29 to 3.87 g·kg−1) and total nitrogen by 243% (from 0.79 to 2.71 g·kg−1) and raised soil desalination efficiency from 33.5% to 56.2%, while soil EC and pH remained within the optimal range for tomato growth. Cross-regional verification showed universal regulation of soil pH and EC but background-dependent nutrient accumulation. The system improves soil fertility through mycelium-mediated biological desalination, progressive SMS-derived carbon pool accumulation, and complementary acid–base homeostasis, generating a net annual economic benefit of approximately 255,000 CNY·ha−1 (≈38,060 USD·ha−1). This recyclable rotation pattern is suitable for popularization in Jiaodong facility-grown tomato production.

title: Structurally Inhospitable: Why Methanol Will Not Power Japan’s Passenger Cars and Where It Belongs Instead
summary: Methanol is frequently promoted as a low-carbon “bridge fuel” for road transport: it is liquid at ambient conditions, burns cleanly, integrates into existing fuel-handling infrastructure, and can be produced from renewable hydrogen and capt
content: Methanol is frequently promoted as a low-carbon “bridge fuel” for road transport: it is liquid at ambient conditions, burns cleanly, integrates into existing fuel-handling infrastructure, and can be produced from renewable hydrogen and captured carbon dioxide. Yet in Japan, one of the world’s largest and most technologically capable automotive markets, methanol has virtually no presence in passenger vehicles, and current policy makes a future presence unlikely. This essay argues that Japan’s passenger-car market is structurally inhospitable to methanol along four reinforcing dimensions: the physical and materials properties of the fuel, which impose cost and durability penalties on light vehicles; the economics of fuel distribution, which defeated methanol passenger programs elsewhere; a policy architecture that commits the passenger segment to electrification while steering alternative liquid fuels toward ethanol blending, aviation, and commercial vehicles; and the strategy of the automakers themselves, none of which is developing methanol drivetrains. Contrasting Japan with China, the essay shows that the divergence reflects feedstock endowment and industrial policy rather than any technical superiority of the Chinese approach. It concludes that methanol nonetheless has a defensible and growing role in Japan, not in passenger cars but in maritime shipping, heavy-duty fleets, and the chemical feedstock chain. The question is not whether Japan should adopt methanol, but where.

title: Aging Phenomena in TiS4- and VS4-based All-Solid-State Lithium Sulfide Batteries Analyzed by ToF-SIMS
summary: Abstract Nowadays, lithium ion batteries (LIBs) are dominating the rechargeable energy storage market. However, lithium/sulfur batteries (LSBs) offer higher energy densities with sulfur's economic and ecologic advantages, but exhibit poor c
content: Abstract Nowadays, lithium ion batteries (LIBs) are dominating the rechargeable energy storage market. However, lithium/sulfur batteries (LSBs) offer higher energy densities with sulfur's economic and ecologic advantages, but exhibit poor cyclability, capacity utilization and lifetime. The utilization of metal sulfide active materials and solid-state electrolytes (SSE) show promise to alleviate these issues but coming with their own challenges such as material integrity. This study is focused on analyzing these aging effects by utilizing high lateral and mass resolution time-of-flight-secondary ion-mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS) imaging of focused ion beam (FIB) cross sections. By measuring the pristine components, the identification of newly formed species as well as the individual particles in a composite was enabled. This work shows among others the formation of a carbon-electrolyte interphase, the accumulation of sodium, the degradation of the metal polysulfide and the decomposition of the SSE. By revealing different aging mechanisms, this research takes part in paving the way for long-lasting, energy dense, and safe SSE LSBs as a more environmentally friendly alternative to conventional commercial LIBs.

title: Olive Tree By-products as a Source of Bioactive Molecules
summary: Abstract The olive sector generates millions of tons of annual residues including leaves, pomace, pits, olive mill wastewater, and table olive effluents that impose an environmental burden while harboring structurally diverse, high-value ph
content: Abstract The olive sector generates millions of tons of annual residues including leaves, pomace, pits, olive mill wastewater, and table olive effluents that impose an environmental burden while harboring structurally diverse, high-value phenolic bioactives including hydroxytyrosol, oleuropein, tyrosol, ligstroside, oleacein, and oleocanthal. Despite growing interest in valorizing these matrices within a circular bioeconomy framework, a fragmented literature has obscured the most productive sources, dominant bioactive profiles, and scalable processing routes relevant to the food industry. This review comprehensively examines the phenolic composition, green extraction technologies, antimicrobial, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory mechanisms, and food-system applications of the principal olive by-product streams. Key findings reveal that olive leaves deliver the highest oleuropein concentration (up to 160 g/kg DW), olive mill wastewater supplies the richest free hydroxytyrosol pools (50–300 mg/L), and olive pomace provides oleacein and oleocanthal at commercially relevant levels. Antimicrobial efficacy against priority foodborne pathogens including Listeria monocytogenes , Escherichia coli O157:H7, and Salmonella enterica operates through simultaneous membrane disruption, enzyme inhibition, reactive oxygen species generation, metal chelation, and quorum-sensing interference. Validated food-system applications include phenolic nanocomposite coatings, pH-responsive smart packaging films, and microencapsulated functional ingredients with preserved bioactivity over extended storage. Future research should prioritize standardized characterization protocols, AI-assisted biorefinery optimization, and robust in vivo bioavailability validation to bridge the gap between demonstrated bioactive potential and commercially viable, clean-label food preservation solutions.

title: From enabler to gatekeeper: digital product passports and the blind spot in circular trade governance
summary: When the WTO Committee on Technical Barriers to Trade met in July 2026, its agenda included a cluster of concerns raised by members about digital product passports: the scope of the requirements, the time available to comply, and the recogn
content: When the WTO Committee on Technical Barriers to Trade met in July 2026, its agenda included a cluster of concerns raised by members about digital product passports: the scope of the requirements, the time available to comply, and the recognition of equivalent regulations and of conformity assessment carried out abroad (WTO, 2026a;WTO, 2026b). An instrument conceived as an enabler of circular trade had, before its principal rules were even in force, become the object of formal trade concerns. That juxtaposition is the starting point of this article.The passport is the centrepiece of the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR), the framework instrument of the EU's circular economy agenda, which replaced the earlier Ecodesign Directive and extended its logic from energy-related products to almost all goods placed on the Union market (Regulation (EU) 2024/1781). It will carry the material and lifecycle data on which reuse, repair and recycling decisions depend, and textiles are the first sector in line. The first content specification for textile apparel, issued by the Joint Research Centre (JRC) in May 2026, sets out 49 data points to be reported at the level of the production batch, ahead of a delegated act expected around 2027 (González-Torres and Arcipowska, 2026); the revised Waste Framework Directive, in force since October 2025, has meanwhile placed extended producer responsibility for textiles on the same trajectory (Directive (EU) 2025/1892). Because the obligation attaches to placing a product on the Union market, it reaches every supplier that sells into the Union, wherever located -a reach that commentators have already read as a textbook instance of the "Brussels effect," the EU's capacity to set de facto global standards through market access rather than negotiation (Bradford, 2020), though the reach of that effect is itself contested, since on some accounts the stringency of EU rules makes it a preference outlier with limited pull over international standards (Young, 2015).The circular economy seeks to decouple growth from resource use by closing material loops, and international trade determines whether those loops can close across borders or remain confined within them (Bato and Kašťáková, 2025). Reliable information about what a product contains is a genuine precondition for circularity: in textiles, a sector whose globalised structure has steadily eroded supply-chain transparency, traceability is widely identified as a prerequisite for any credible circular transition (Das et al., 2025). The case for the passport, in these terms, is strong. Yet the scholarship on passports has developed largely along technical and managerial lines, data architecture, adoption barriers, standardisation, while giving comparatively little attention to their legal and institutional consequences, and in particular to how they intersect with the rules of international trade and whether their design might entrench asymmetries among the actors

title: Agro-industrial clusters and export trajectories in Ecuador: a comparative analysis of cluster governance maturity and development
summary: Industrial clusters have become central to policy debates on competitiveness and structural transformation in emerging economies; however, robust empirical evidence regarding their effectiveness remains limited. This study develops a compar
content: Industrial clusters have become central to policy debates on competitiveness and structural transformation in emerging economies; however, robust empirical evidence regarding their effectiveness remains limited. This study develops a comparative framework to characterize agro-industrial cluster initiatives in Ecuador based on export trajectories, governance structures, and organizational maturity. A mixed-methods design combines quantitative analysis of export dynamics using compound annual growth rates with a qualitative assessment of policy frameworks and institutional arrangements across seven agro-industrial clusters. The findings reveal substantial heterogeneity in cluster performance. Recently established clusters initiatives, including rice, dairy, and beef, exhibit growth rates exceeding 40%, whereas more mature clusters such as banana and forestry follow more stable trajectories. The findings indicate that variations in cluster maturity are associated with distinct export trajectories. By integrating export performance, governance characteristics into a comparative framework, the study provides empirical evidence on cluster development in emerging economies, highlighting the importance of policy continuity, institutional capacity, and effective coordination for long-term cluster consolidation.

title: Optical Remote Sensing and Machine Learning Enable Scalable Carbon Mapping in Himalayan Forests Despite Spectral Saturation Challenges
summary: Accurate aboveground biomass (AGB) estimation is critical for climate change mitigation and carbon accounting in mountain regions, yet spatially explicit mapping remains limited by reliance on conventional field methods and underexplored ma
content: Accurate aboveground biomass (AGB) estimation is critical for climate change mitigation and carbon accounting in mountain regions, yet spatially explicit mapping remains limited by reliance on conventional field methods and underexplored machine learning approaches in the Himalaya. Bhutan, a carbon-negative nation maintaining 70% forest cover, faces urgent demand to develop robust monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) systems for carbon market participation under the Paris Agreement Article 6. This study developed a random forest (RF) model that integrates Sentinel-2A multispectral imagery, nine vegetation indices, topographic variables, and field-measured AGB from 99 plots across 244.6 hectares in the Kyentshen Community Forest. Using recursive feature elimination, 10 key predictors were identified from 27 candidate variables: Band 11, SLAVI, Band 12, WDRVI, NDVI, elevation, NDWI, GNDVI, band ratio (r3), and Band 9. The optimized RF model achieved R² = 0.34 and RMSE = 67.98 ± 19.79 t/ha on training data (Ntree = 500, Mtry = 3). However, test-set performance declined substantially (R² = 0.42, RMSE = 86.14 t/ha), indicating overfitting and reflecting limitations of spectral saturation in high-biomass stands (>300 t/ha). A Wilcoxon signed-rank test revealed systematic overestimation (predicted median: 118.36 t/ha vs. observed: 105.15 t/ha; p = 0.03). Despite moderate accuracy, this study demonstrates that freely available Sentinel-2 data combined with machine learning offers a cost-effective, scalable alternative to traditional field mapping for rapid AGB assessment across Bhutan's temperate forests. Vegetation indices, particularly SLAVI and WDRVI, proved superior to raw spectral bands, offering improved sensitivity to dense canopies. The spatial-transect methodology and 10-predictor framework provide a replicable foundation for advancing Bhutan's forest carbon accounting systems. We recommend integrating synthetic aperture radar (SAR) or LiDAR to overcome optical saturation, enabling higher accuracy for robust MRV compliance and carbon credit monetization. This work directly supports the maintenance of Bhutan's carbon-neutral status and establishes the technical baseline for scaling AGB monitoring across mountain regions where engineered infrastructure capacity is limited, but climate action urgency is paramount.

title: Financial Pain Points in BYD's Premiumization Strategy: An Analysis Based on the Profitability of Denza, Fangchengbao, and Yangwang
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: Against the backdrop of the global new energy vehicle market shifting from policy-driven growth to market-driven competition, Chinese domestic brands face the dual pressure of low-end lock-in and price wars, making brand premiumization an i
content: Against the backdrop of the global new energy vehicle market shifting from policy-driven growth to market-driven competition, Chinese domestic brands face the dual pressure of low-end lock-in and price wars, making brand premiumization an important path for breaking through profitability constraints. Taking BYD as a case study, this paper focuses on its three premium brands, Denza, Fangchengbao, and Yangwang. Based on annual reports from 2021 to 2025 and publicly available literature, this paper applies a three-dimensional strategy-input-output framework to analyze the financial performance of BYD's premiumization strategy. The study finds that BYD's premiumization is supported by a solid technological foundation, including the second-generation Blade Battery, which improves safety and charging, the fifth-generation DM technology, which optimizes energy consumption, the DiSus system, which upgrades chassis experience, and God's Eye, which strengthens intelligent driving. These technologies significantly enhance product competitiveness. However, premium-brand sales have not yet been effectively converted into profits. In 2025, the gross margin of the automobile business, net profit attributable to shareholders, net profit excluding non-recurring gains and losses, and operating cash flow all came under pressure, indicating that BYD remains in transition from the investment stage to the return stage. The core financial pain points lie in insufficient scale, limited brand premium, and an imbalance between input and output. This paper provides a staged financial evaluation perspective for the premiumization transformation of domestic brands.

title: ESG Rating Divergence, Information Frictions, and Capital Market Efficiency: A Mechanism-Based Synthesis from China
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: The rapid expansion of ESG (Environment, Society and Governance) investment has placed ESG ratings at the core of capital market decisions. Nevertheless, the significant differences among various rating agencies have drawn widespread attent
content: The rapid expansion of ESG (Environment, Society and Governance) investment has placed ESG ratings at the core of capital market decisions. Nevertheless, the significant differences among various rating agencies have drawn widespread attention to the reliability of ESG information and its impact on market efficiency. To this end, this paper establishes a comprehensive analytical framework to assess the impact of ESG rating discrepancies on the information of the capital market, with stock price synchronicity serving as the measurement indicator. Based on a review of the relevant literature, it integrates studies on information asymmetry, limited investor attention, and analyst information intermediation. On this basis, it summarizes three main transmission paths through which ESG rating discrepancies impact information efficiency: heightened information asymmetry, scattered investor attention, and reduced analyst prediction quality. The results suggest that, taking into account the institutional features of China's capital market, including the dominance of retail investors, relatively weak information disclosure, and the strong policy-driven ESG, the aforementioned effects may be significantly amplified in the Chinese context.

title: Sustainable Ergonomic Highchair Design for Toddlers with Environmental Responsibility
source: Mindanao Journal of Science and Technology
summary: Toddler highchairs are essential for parents, restaurants, and daycares to support children’s eating activities. However, products on the market have several limitations, including insufficient stability, limited height adjustment, and unco
content: Toddler highchairs are essential for parents, restaurants, and daycares to support children’s eating activities. However, products on the market have several limitations, including insufficient stability, limited height adjustment, and uncomfortable materials. This study aims to develop a safer, more comfortable, and flexible ergonomic toddler feeding chair using a structured product development approach supported by computer-aided design (CAD) in SolidWorks, digital structural analysis, and considerations of environmental responsibility. The research follows a phased product development methodology: needs identification, concept development, system design, structural analysis, digital validation, and production cost estimation. The chair incorporates an aluminum frame to enhance stability. The seat combines polypropylene and foam for user comfort, while folding and height-adjustment mechanisms ensure adaptability across different conditions. Static simulation in SolidWorks confirmed that the design withstands loads up to 30 kg, with stress, deformation, and safety factor values within acceptable limits. Environmental responsibility was considered at the material level through the selection of recyclable materials (such as aluminum and polypropylene) with anticipated long product life and efficient resource use; no formal life-cycle assessment was conducted. Although digital validation produced promising results, further work is required to develop prototypes and conduct physical user testing to evaluate ergonomics and usability under real conditions. With these improvements, the proposed design shows potential to outperform conventional products and achieve broad applicability, while further environmental validation remains necessary to substantiate sustainability outcomes.

title: Revolutionizing Financial Management Through Artificial Intelligence
source: mLAC Journal for Arts Commerce and Sciences (m-JACS) ISSN 2584-1920
summary: In the monetary economy, banks and financial institutions were established for money creation. Both organised and unorganized sector have a mushroom growth of development in capital and money market. Apart from banks and financial instituti
content: In the monetary economy, banks and financial institutions were established for money creation. Both organised and unorganized sector have a mushroom growth of development in capital and money market. Apart from banks and financial institutions, stock markets were established in Metro-Politian cities. In the developing economy like India, shortage of finance is the major problem for the budding entrepreneurs. Traditionally, the work of finance managers are limited to maintain the accounts of the business only. Now, the function of finance manager is to acquire finance and utilization of finance. In the modern economy, Artificial Intelligence is a boon to finance managers to find out the new sources of finance and investment of finance in proper avenues. The objectives of the study are to know about the benefits of AI in financial management, to study the methods through which AI is used by financial institutions, to identify the stakeholders of AI in finance and to predict the future trends of AI in finance.

title: ESG Comparison and Stock Price Crash Risk
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: A firm's ESG score is usually read as a stand-alone measure, even though managers also watch how that score compares with those of industry peers. We use Chinese listed-company data for 2015-2024 to ask whether this relative position is con
content: A firm's ESG score is usually read as a stand-alone measure, even though managers also watch how that score compares with those of industry peers. We use Chinese listed-company data for 2015-2024 to ask whether this relative position is connected to stock price crash risk. The estimated relation is positive and statistically significant. It remains so after lagging the ESG comparison measure, replacing NCSKEW with DUVOL, and using the industry median rather than the mean as the peer benchmark. The financing-constraint tests are consistent with one route through which peer-oriented ESG behavior may translate into crash exposure. The ownership split adds an important boundary: the association is statistically significant for non-state-owned enterprises but not for state-owned enterprises. Taken together, the evidence suggests that competition over relative ESG standing can carry capital-market costs that are obscured when ESG performance is considered only in absolute terms.

title: Intelligent discovery and precision regulation of taste peptides: a systematic review from taste mechanisms to health applications
summary: Taste peptides uniquely bridge sensory pleasure and bioactivity, yet their industrial translation is hindered by empirical discovery bottlenecks and a limited understanding of their behavior within complex food systems. This review provides
content: Taste peptides uniquely bridge sensory pleasure and bioactivity, yet their industrial translation is hindered by empirical discovery bottlenecks and a limited understanding of their behavior within complex food systems. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of cutting-edge artificial intelligence (AI)-driven prediction platforms, highlighting the paradigm shift from traditional trial-and-error screening to rational, high-throughput design across diverse taste modalities. Also, we critically evaluate how dynamic oral physiological environments and complex food matrix components profoundly modulate gustatory transduction and signaling efficacy. Furthermore, to bridge the gap between fundamental perception and industrial application, we systematically detail targeted modulation strategies for amplifying desirable tastes and suppressing off-flavors. Finally, we explore the immense translational potential of these dual-functional peptides in precision nutrition, specialized elderly diets, and sodium/sugar reduction. By merging AI-assisted discovery, taste transduction mechanism and influencing factors, and practical modulation strategies, this review delivers a definitive strategic guidance to accelerate the targeted development and health-oriented application of taste peptides in the functional food industry.

title: From policy commitment to biodiversity action: Implementation gaps and governance barriers to the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework in Asia and the Pacific
summary: The Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF) establishes an ambitious global pathway to halt and reverse biodiversity loss by 2030, but its success depends on national capacity to translate commitments into effective action. T
content: The Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF) establishes an ambitious global pathway to halt and reverse biodiversity loss by 2030, but its success depends on national capacity to translate commitments into effective action. This study assesses governance gaps, and priority actions implementation across Asia and the Pacific through comparative analysis of National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans (NBSAPs) and Seventh National Reports (7NRs). We reviewed reporting from 41 countries out of 60 identified in the IPBES Asia-Pacific regional assessment. A mixed-method approach combining both qualitative and quantitative methods was adopted. The most frequently reported constraint was inadequate data, monitoring and information systems, identified in 68.3% of countries, followed by compounding ecological and environmental pressures (53.7%) and financial and resource constraints (48.8%). Institutional fragmentation and cross-sector coordination gaps were reported by 43.9% of countries. Although 87.8% of countries reported actions relating to legal and policy frameworks, few reported efforts in enforcement and compliance, gender-responsive and socially inclusive conservation, capacity development, private-sector engagement, and access and benefit-sharing. Conversely, monitoring and digital information systems, biodiversity finance, and policy strengthening were among the most frequently identified future priorities. The findings demonstrate a substantial asymmetry between policy development and implementation capacity. We argue that NBSAP adoption and national reporting should not be interpreted as evidence of implementation readiness. Accelerating KMGBF delivery requires long-term financing, institutional strengthening, interoperable biodiversity monitoring systems, regional knowledge exchange, and inclusive governance. Regional institutions and networks can play a critical role in enabling cross-country learning, technical cooperation, and implementation.

title: Institution Layer
summary: This chapter examines how decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs) can structure governance for sustainability outcomes. Drawing on cybernetic principles, it analyzes how crypto-institutions leverage transparency, immutability, and pro
content: This chapter examines how decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs) can structure governance for sustainability outcomes. Drawing on cybernetic principles, it analyzes how crypto-institutions leverage transparency, immutability, and programmable governance to address coordination problems constraining environmental action. The chapter surveys governance design parameters—from voting mechanisms to human versus algorithmic decision-making—that practitioners must navigate, then demonstrates configuration reasoning across three scales: building-level energy cooperatives, bioregional financing facilities with conservation sub-entities, and planetary carbon markets. Throughout, the chapter emphasizes that effective green crypto-institutional design requires matching governance surfaces to institutional purpose, participant characteristics, and the permanence of ecological commitments. Practical checklists and governance parameter tables equip readers to evaluate and configure these systems.

title: Board Demographics and Tax Planning Strategies of Listed Pharmaceutical Companies in Nigeria
source: JOURNAL OF BUSINESS AND AFRICAN ECONOMY
summary: The multiplicity of tax laws and heavy tax burden facing companies in developing countries has resulted in the adoption of different strategies to reduce tax liabilities. The main objective of this study was to examine the effect of board a
content: The multiplicity of tax laws and heavy tax burden facing companies in developing countries has resulted in the adoption of different strategies to reduce tax liabilities. The main objective of this study was to examine the effect of board attributes on the tax planning strategies of listed pharmaceutical companies in Nigeria from 2015 to 2024. The independent variable, board attributes was proxied by board academic qualification, board financial expertise and board experience. The dependent variable tax planning was proxied by effective tax rate. The research design adopted in this study was ex post facto, secondary data were used and the population of the study was 7 listed pharmaceutical companies of which census sampling technique was employed to retain them as the sample size of the study. The technique of data analysis that was employed in this study was ordinary least square regression analysis and the statistical package employed was E views version 13. The findings of the study revealed that board academic qualification (Coef. 0.027902; p-value = 0.0023) has significant negative effect on effective tax rate; board financial expertise (Coef. 0.162092; p-value = 0.0001) has significant negative effect on effective tax rate; board experience (Coef. 0.034529; p-value = 0.0003) has significant negative effect on effective tax rate of listed pharmaceutical companies in Nigeria. Therefore, it was concluded that board attributes can significantly affect tax planning strategies of listed pharmaceutical firms in Nigeria reducing their tax liabilities. Thus, it was therefore recommended among others that pharmaceutical companies in Nigeria should appoint board members with strong academic backgrounds, particularly in fields relevant to finance, accounting or economics.

title: Learning and practicing active democratic citizenship in the struggle against growing authoritarianism
summary: s from the conference in which authors explore significant changes in policy, statecraft and patterns of mobilisation in relation to ALE. They return to the question of how neoliberalism relates to democracy and the practice of democratic c
content: s from the conference in which authors explore significant changes in policy, statecraft and patterns of mobilisation in relation to ALE. They return to the question of how neoliberalism relates to democracy and the practice of democratic citizenship, and open up the question of how to think about and respond to increasing authoritarianism. Authors also examine how neoliberalism relates to authoritarianism and consider how these phenomena might be usefully distinguished. The aim is to make a collective effort to find adequate terms for what has occurred in recent years and what is emerging from a period of rapid change in capitalism.

title: The making of digital rangelands: Navigating the implications of rangeland datafication and smartification in Kenya
source: Environment and Planning E Nature and Space
summary: A shift is occurring in how the global environmental community understands and talks about rangelands. Long seen as economically unproductive and environmentally degraded environments, rangelands are now being recast as sources of untapped
content: A shift is occurring in how the global environmental community understands and talks about rangelands. Long seen as economically unproductive and environmentally degraded environments, rangelands are now being recast as sources of untapped ecological benefit and climate optimism. This is due to growing awareness of the significant contributions rangelands make to biological diversity, carbon sequestration, and nature-based economies worldwide. In this article, we argue that digital technologies and the data they produce are contributing significantly to shifting narratives about rangelands. The rapid advancement of digital technologies have rendered rangelands legible in new ways, transforming rangelands into data that can be acted on to both understand and, purportedly, help transform environmental crises. We identify six areas where digital tools are increasingly applied in rangelands: (1) livestock monitoring and management; (2) livestock market access and information; (3) property and asset monitoring and management; (4) ecological monitoring and management; (5) payments for ecosystem services; and (6) disaster preparedness and management. We then reveal the wider effects of this trend, demonstrating how datafication and smartification contribute to making rangelands more governable, commodifiable, and useful for the global environmental community. Despite the potential benefits and opportunities this shift poses for rangeland users, not all groups are empowered equally by the making of digital rangelands. We caution that as digital technologies rework understandings of what and who rangelands are for, how they should be managed and what purpose they should serve, there is a risk that existing rangeland users and ways of using, managing, and governing rangelands will be marginalised and replaced. Our analysis and argument are developed through a qualitative case study of rangelands in Kenya and informed by the websites and social media pages of 65 organisations in Kenya's rangelands who use digital technologies.

title: How Are Green Financial Markets Linked to Green Cryptocurrency Return States? Evidence from a Cross-Quantilogram Approach
summary: This paper examines directional quantile dependence from green bonds, clean energy markets, and carbon markets to the return states of five literature-classified green cryptocurrencies. Using daily returns from 25 September 2019 to 23 May 2
content: This paper examines directional quantile dependence from green bonds, clean energy markets, and carbon markets to the return states of five literature-classified green cryptocurrencies. Using daily returns from 25 September 2019 to 23 May 2025, we estimate static cross-quantilograms on a 19×19 quantile grid at lags 1, 5, and 22, 500-observation rolling cross-quantilograms, bootstrap surface tests, and green-specificity comparisons with five cryptocurrencies that used proof-of-work (PoW) consensus throughout the comparison sample. Point estimates display heterogeneous short-run patterns in selected green-bond and carbon-market pairs, but none of the 45 forward surfaces rejects the omnibus null at the 5% level. Rolling estimates vary across windows and tail cutoffs. The largest raw green-group contrast occurs for carbon quota prices at lag five, although its time-series bootstrap interval includes zero and factor-adjusted tests do not detect systematic green-minus-PoW separation. Descriptive quantile-on-quantile connectedness estimates are higher at extreme quantiles than at the median–median state. Overall, the evidence is more consistent with broad cryptocurrency-market conditions than with a uniform dependence pattern associated with the environmental label.

title: Breaking the Wall of Inequality: The Hybrid Academic Habitus of Rural Students in the Heart of Kalimantan’s Academia
source: KOMUNITAS INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF INDONESIAN SOCIETY AND CULTURE
summary: Educational inequality remains one of the most persistent challenges in higher education, particularly for students from rural and remote areas who often experience unequal access to educational resources, digital technologies, and academic
content: Educational inequality remains one of the most persistent challenges in higher education, particularly for students from rural and remote areas who often experience unequal access to educational resources, digital technologies, and academic opportunities. While several studies have explored educational disparities and student adaptation, the study of how rural students reconstruct their dispositions during university life remains scarce. This study aims to examine how rural students navigate structural inequalities and construct a hybrid academic habitus in the context of higher education. The study employed a qualitative research design with a phenomenological approach. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with twelve rural students enrolled at Mulawarman University, East Kalimantan, Indonesia. Participants were purposively selected to represent diverse rural backgrounds. The data were analyzed using thematic analysis based on Bourdieu's concepts of habitus, capital, and field, complemented by Giddens' agency theory. The findings reveal that rural students experience multiple, interrelated forms of educational inequality, including limited educational resources, academic culture shock, symbolic exclusion, and financial insecurity. Rather than remaining passive recipients of these structural constraints, they actively developed learning, social, and economic adaptation strategies through self-directed learning, digital literacy, peer solidarity, and entrepreneurial activities. These adaptive practices gradually transformed their dispositions by integrating rural collectivist values ​​with modern academic competencies, resulting in the emergence of a hybrid academic habitus. This new socio-cultural disposition enabled students to navigate structural inequalities while maintaining meaningful connections to their rural identities. This study contributes to extending Bourdieu's concept of habitus beyond social reproduction to a more dynamic understanding of identity transformation through the interaction of structure and agency.

title: Effects of Some Processing Methods on Organoleptic Properties and Proximate Composition of Coptodon guineensis (Günther, 1862)
source: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF FOOD SCIENCE AND QUALITY CONTROL
summary: This study evaluated the effects of selected processing methods on the proximate composition and organoleptic properties of Coptodon guineensis. Fresh samples were procured from Choba market in Obio-Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers Sta
content: This study evaluated the effects of selected processing methods on the proximate composition and organoleptic properties of Coptodon guineensis. Fresh samples were procured from Choba market in Obio-Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State, Nigeria, and subjected to three processing methods: frying, smoking, and oven drying. Standard procedures were followed for sample preparation, including cleaning, evisceration, brining, and seasoning. The experiment was arranged in a completely randomized design with three treatments and triplicates. Proximate analysis was conducted using standard AOAC methods, while sensory evaluation was carried out by a 12-member panel using a 5-point hedonic scale. Data were analyzed using one-way ANOVA, and means were separated using Tukey’s test at p < 0.05. Results obtained revealed significant differences (p < 0.05) in both proximate composition and sensory attributes among processing methods. Moisture content decreased significantly after processing, with smoked samples recording the lowest value (25.88%), indicating higher preservation potential. Protein content increased significantly in processed samples, with smoked (63.88%) and oven-dried (61.87%) fish exhibiting the highest values due to moisture loss and nutrient concentration. Lipid content was highest in fresh (36.88%) and fried samples (30.59%), suggesting oil absorption during frying, while smoked fish had the lowest lipid content (6.45%). Ash and crude fibre contents also varied significantly across treatments. Sensory evaluation showed that fried fish had the highest scores for flavor (4.74), taste (4.91), and overall acceptability (4.72), indicating superior palatability. Smoked fish was rated highest in texture (4.91), while oven-dried samples consistently recorded the lowest scores across most sensory parameters. In conclusion, processing methods significantly influence the nutritional quality and consumer acceptability of C. guineensis. Smoking and oven drying enhanced protein content and shelf stability, whereas frying improved sensory appeal. These findings have important implications for fish processing, preservation, and value addition in developing economies.

title: Postharvest Quality and Functional Stability of White-Fleshed Sweet Potatoes with Cactus Mucilage Coatings and Packaging
summary: Abstract Edible coatings based on plant-derived biopolymers are promising tools to preserve the functional quality of fresh foods. Sweet potato is considered a functional food due to its bioactive compound content, although these attributes
content: Abstract Edible coatings based on plant-derived biopolymers are promising tools to preserve the functional quality of fresh foods. Sweet potato is considered a functional food due to its bioactive compound content, although these attributes may be compromised during postharvest storage. This study evaluated edible coatings formulated with cactus mucilage from Nopalea cochenillifera and Opuntia stricta, applied alone or combined with polypropylene packaging, on the physicochemical quality, bioactive compounds, and antioxidant activity of white-fleshed sweet potatoes. Roots were stored under refrigeration followed by shelf-life simulation. The combined use of coating and packaging reduced fresh weight loss from 22.95% in untreated roots to 1.93% in the best-performing treatment, preserved visual quality, and maintained higher total phenolic compound levels. In addition, coated roots exhibited DPPH radical scavenging activity of up to 22.9% and FRAP values up to 2.61 mmol Fe2+ kg–1 FW during storage. Optical microscopy confirmed the adhesion of the mucilage coating. While packaging primarily controlled dehydration, edible coatings contributed to the stabilization of functional attributes, supporting cactus mucilage as a sustainable strategy to enhance sweet potato functional quality.

title: Nano-enabled disruption of bacterial virulence and communication in plant pathosystems: emerging strategies for sustainable disease management
summary: Bacterial diseases are a major cause of crop losses worldwide, threatening food security and the sustainability of agricultural production. Traditional management practices heavily rely on antibiotics, resistant strains and copper-based com
content: Bacterial diseases are a major cause of crop losses worldwide, threatening food security and the sustainability of agricultural production. Traditional management practices heavily rely on antibiotics, resistant strains and copper-based compounds but their continued efficiency is hampered by antimicrobial resistance, ecological issues and rapid evolution of pathogens. Nano-enabled anti-virulence strategies offer a novel approach that specifically targets bacterial virulence instead of the killing of the pathogens alone, which can potentially reduce the pressure for resistance development. This review rigorously investigates mechanistic basis of nano-facilitated interference in bacterial communication and pathogenicity in the plant pathosystems. We evaluated the impact of metallic, metal oxide, silica-based, carbon-based and polymeric nanomaterials on quorum sensing (QS), biofilm formation, extracellular polysaccharide synthesis, motility, secretion pathways, phytotoxin production and host colonization. Particular emphasis is placed on nanoparticle–pathogen interactions, nano-enabled delivery of quorum quenchers, RNA molecules and biological agents, microbiome compatibility, and the integration of these processes within a mechanistic anti-virulence framework. Current evidence indicates that nanomaterial efficacy is strongly influenced by physicochemical properties, target virulence mechanisms, delivery efficiency, and environmental conditions; therefore, no single nanoplatform is universally optimal across plant–pathogen systems. Although smart delivery systems provide opportunities to simultaneously interfere with interconnected virulence pathways, their practical application remains constrained by field stability, biosafety, non-target effects, scalability, and regulatory uncertainty. Overall, advancing nano-enabled anti-virulence technologies from laboratory efficacy toward sustainable crop protection will require mechanism-guided nanomaterial design, microbiome-compatible formulations, rigorous field validation, and comprehensive environmental risk assessment.

title: Tributyrin and its importance in fish and shrimp nutrition
summary: Abstract Aquaculture faces increasing challenge related to plant-based diets and the sustainability of feed ingredients. Tributyrin, a triglyceride ester of butyric acid, has gained attention as a functional feed additive in aquaculture due
content: Abstract Aquaculture faces increasing challenge related to plant-based diets and the sustainability of feed ingredients. Tributyrin, a triglyceride ester of butyric acid, has gained attention as a functional feed additive in aquaculture due to its potential to enhance gut health, immunity, and metabolic performance in various aquatic species. Tributyrin offers a promising solution by improving nutrient absorption, promoting immune responses, and supporting digestive health. While the effects of tributyrin in shellfish remain underexplored, theoretical benefits suggest that it may enhance digestive efficiency and stress resistance. This review highlights the promising role of tributyrin in aquaculture, particularly in promoting sustainable feed practices, while calling for more targeted research to determine its effectiveness across a wider range of species and environmental conditions.

title: Asset Layer
summary: This chapter provides a systematic analysis of the properties, functions, and types of green crypto-assets—defined as transferable, programmable financial instruments whose value proposition is explicitly linked to measurable ecological pro
content: This chapter provides a systematic analysis of the properties, functions, and types of green crypto-assets—defined as transferable, programmable financial instruments whose value proposition is explicitly linked to measurable ecological processes or outcomes, such as carbon sequestration, biodiversity protection, renewable energy generation, or environmental data production. The chapter proposes a structured yet non-exhaustive mapping of existing and emergent green crypto-asset types, spanning ownership claims, non-possessory rights, environmental process tokens, derivatives, insurance instruments, currencies, and portfolio vehicles. Rather than advancing a fixed taxonomy, the chapter foregrounds three defining design properties (composability, adaptability, and material modularity) that distinguish green crypto-assets from conventional green finance instruments. By articulating how these properties reshape market organization, asset materiality, and capital allocation, the chapter equips sustainability professionals, policymakers, and financial actors with an analytical framework to assess the opportunities and limitations of existing and emerging green crypto-assets.

title: GREEN HYDROGEN AND THE PRICE OF WATER: CHALLENGES FOR THE CASPIAN REGION OF KAZAKHSTAN
summary: The article examines the prospects for the development of green hydrogen energy in the western regions of Kazakhstan, with a particular focus on water resource constraints. The relevance of the study is specified growing global interest in
content: The article examines the prospects for the development of green hydrogen energy in the western regions of Kazakhstan, with a particular focus on water resource constraints. The relevance of the study is specified growing global interest in hydrogen as a key element of decarbonization strategies. The purpose of the research is to assess the relationship between hydrogen production and water availability in arid regions. The methodological basis includes analytical review, comparative analysis, and quantitative estimation of water consumption in electrolysis processes. The results show that large-scale hydrogen production requires significant water resources, which may become a limiting factor in regions with existing water scarcity, such as the Caspian region. The study also identifies the environmental and economic limitations of desalination as an alternative water source. It is concluded that the sustainable development of hydrogen energy in Kazakhstan requires integration with water resource management systems and coordinated policy approaches.

title: The Underlying Material Reality
summary: Every green crypto-asset rests on a claim about the physical world: carbon sequestered, biodiversity protected, clean energy generated. This chapter introduces the underlying material reality —the diverse family of planetary systems from wh
content: Every green crypto-asset rests on a claim about the physical world: carbon sequestered, biodiversity protected, clean energy generated. This chapter introduces the underlying material reality —the diverse family of planetary systems from which all financial abstractions are derived—as the foundational layer of the environmental finance stack. It examines the scientific observation technologies used to translate the physical world into data, surveys environmental indices that compress complex ecological data into actionable metrics, and reviews existing nature accounting frameworks that structure how ecosystem services are identified, valued, and integrated into economic systems. Throughout, a core principle emerges: measurement infrastructure determines market access. The choice of observation technology and the accounting framework it situates itself within directly shapes which markets a green asset can enter, what verification costs it will bear, and how defensible its green claims will be.

title: Traditional rural livelihoods and environmental degradation among forest-edge communities in Kenema District, Sierra Leone: Implications for sustainable rural development
summary: Rural households living along forest frontiers depend on land, forests, water and wildlife for food, energy, income and other everyday needs. In Sierra Leone, this dependence is particularly visible around the Gola Rainforest landscape, whe
content: Rural households living along forest frontiers depend on land, forests, water and wildlife for food, energy, income and other everyday needs. In Sierra Leone, this dependence is particularly visible around the Gola Rainforest landscape, where subsistence agriculture remains the foundation of livelihood for most forest-edge communities. Yet the same livelihood systems that sustain households can place pressure on forest and soil resources when farming expands, fallow periods shorten, wood extraction intensifies or households have few viable income alternatives. This article develops an empirical framework for examining the relationship between traditional rural livelihoods and environmental degradation among forest-edge communities in Kenema District. Drawing on the Sustainable Livelihoods Framework and a political-ecology perspective, the study treats environmental degradation as a multidimensional process involving forest-cover loss, declining forest quality, soil erosion and fertility decline, biodiversity loss, water degradation and habitat disturbance. A mixed-methods cross-sectional design is proposed, combining a household survey with key-informant interviews, focus-group discussions, field observation and, where technically feasible, geospatial analysis of land-cover change. The analytical strategy will examine not only whether particular livelihood activities are associated with environmental pressure, but also how poverty, household assets, education, market access, land availability and local institutions shape resource dependence. The article argues that conservation policy should avoid treating forest-edge households simply as agents of degradation. A more useful approach is to understand environmental pressure as part of a livelihood-environment feedback process in which economic vulnerability can increase dependence on natural capital, while degradation of that capital can deepen future vulnerability. The proposed study is expected to generate locally grounded evidence for rural-development strategies that combine sustainable agriculture, agroforestry, livelihood diversification, community-based resource governance and environmental stewardship.

title: Development of a 30 m spatiotemporal land use and land cover dataset (1985–2025) for the Allal El Fassi Watershed (Morocco) using Landsat time series and Google Earth Engine
summary: Understanding environmental changes and promoting the sustainable management of watersheds requires long-term monitoring of land use and land cover (LULC), especially in Mediterranean regions subject to high climate variability and growing
content: Understanding environmental changes and promoting the sustainable management of watersheds requires long-term monitoring of land use and land cover (LULC), especially in Mediterranean regions subject to high climate variability and growing anthropogenic pressure.Using the whole Landsat imagery archive accessible via the Google Earth Engine platform, this study introduces a novel spatiotemporal land use and land cover dataset (LULC_AllalElFassi) for the Allal El Fassi Watershed spanning the years 1985-2025.The methodology ensures the geographical and temporal coherence of the produced maps while detecting changes in land use and land cover by combining a locally adaptive classification strategy with the Continuous Change Detection and Classification (CCDC) algorithm.Eight land use and land cover classifications could be mapped at a spatial resolution of 30 m thanks to the dataset, which was created using 2000 training samples and 800 independent validation points.The total accuracy of the results was 82.8282.82±0.45percentage points.Water bodies (93.65%), built-up areas (92.65%), agricultural land (87.64%), and dense woods (87.81%) had especially good categorization accuracy.Long-term landscape dynamics investigation showed a significant increase in open forests (+898.50%), a notable expansion of agricultural land (+10.38%) and built-up areas (+789.63%),and a decrease in thick forests (-9.35%) and herbaceous and poorly vegetated regions (-4.73%).These alterations show that the forest canopy is gradually opening, agricultural production is becoming more intensive, and urbanization is increasing across the watershed.The suggested dataset is a useful decision-support tool for hydrological modeling, water erosion assessment, forest resource management, and sustainable planning of Mediterranean watersheds.It also provides a reliable data source for long-term environmental monitoring.

title: Valuation of Intangible Expenditures: Revisiting Bublitz and Ettredge (1989)
summary: An extensive body of accounting research documents the difficulty of measuring the value of intangibles and the issues surrounding recording them in company financial statements. Early studies examined advertising and research and developme
content: An extensive body of accounting research documents the difficulty of measuring the value of intangibles and the issues surrounding recording them in company financial statements. Early studies examined advertising and research and development (R&D) expenditures when companies began reporting them in their financials in 1972. A lot has changed in the years subsequent to the early studies: investments have shifted from tangible to intangible, more data are available, and statistical techniques have improved. This study replicates and extends the findings in Bublitz and Ettredge (1989) using data from 1984 to 2018, finding similar relationships between returns and advertising and R&D expenditures in the later time period. The paper also extends their study by investigating the relationship between intangible expenditures and future payoffs, finding mixed results.

title: When the bill comes due: Climate risk plans are not prepared to fund themselves
summary: Abstract Amidst urgent global calls for climate action, city governments face a problem: although they increasingly recognize the necessity of climate adaptation, the financial strategies essential for implementing these plans remain largel
content: Abstract Amidst urgent global calls for climate action, city governments face a problem: although they increasingly recognize the necessity of climate adaptation, the financial strategies essential for implementing these plans remain largely neglected. Such oversight undermines climate adaptation. To understand how cities are considering financial risks in the context of climate risk, we reviewed 151 city-level climate risk reports from 143 cities internationally concerning their adaptation costs, climate risk costs, insurance costs, and who would pay for adaptation. In terms of financial risks, 73% of reports acknowledged that climate change would impact their local economies. However, less than half of the reports identified how to pay for a plan, and even fewer identified who would pay for the plan. Given this context, we highlight a need for risk assessors to develop strategies to integrate climate and financial risks at the local level. We also identify trailblazing cities with effective climate financing strategies underway.

title: Rewiring lactobacilli: challenges, opportunities, and the translational path to therapeutics
summary: Lactobacilli have long been regarded as promising probiotic bacteria due to their safety profile, host compatibility, and beneficial roles in modulating human health. However, the therapeutic efficacy of wild-type probiotics remains constra
content: Lactobacilli have long been regarded as promising probiotic bacteria due to their safety profile, host compatibility, and beneficial roles in modulating human health. However, the therapeutic efficacy of wild-type probiotics remains constrained by limited target specificity, lack of control over their activity, and variability in clinical responses. Recent advances in synthetic biology have enabled the possibility of overcoming these constraints through precise engineering of bacterial functions, such as therapeutics production. Despite these advances, significant challenges remain in engineering lactobacilli, including limited genetic toolkits, species- and strain-dependent variability, and uncertainty regarding the stability and safety of engineered strains. This review discusses the current landscape of engineering lactobacilli for therapeutic applications, with particular emphasis on candidates undergoing clinical evaluation. Furthermore, it outlines key technical hurdles to overcome and suggests potential solutions to accelerate their translation into clinically effective and reliable microbial therapeutics.

title: Situating Policy Entrepreneurship in the Policy Sciences
source: Journal of Comparative Policy Analysis Research and Practice
summary: This article argues that the policy entrepreneurship (PE) literature exemplifies and contributes to the new policy sciences, a development that seeks to recover Harold Lasswell’s vision of a contextualized, problem-oriented, multi-method di
content: This article argues that the policy entrepreneurship (PE) literature exemplifies and contributes to the new policy sciences, a development that seeks to recover Harold Lasswell’s vision of a contextualized, problem-oriented, multi-method discipline bridging basic and applied research. Using tools from the tradition of practical argumentation and formal debate, the article builds a prima facie case, tracing PE scholarship from collective action theory through Kingdon, Capano and colleagues, and Mintrom to show its emphasis on agency and context, and an extended case identifying two connected research practices: an empirical practice generating generalizable knowledge and a translational practice rendering it usable for practitioners.
