title: Dynamic vegetation–soil–water feedbacks as an under-recognised source of structural uncertainty in digital soil mapping
summary: Abstract. Digital soil mapping (DSM) produces spatially continuous soil information for land-use planning, carbon accounting, and Earth system analysis, resting on the SCORPAN framework and its use of remote-sensing and terrain covariates a
content: Abstract. Digital soil mapping (DSM) produces spatially continuous soil information for land-use planning, carbon accounting, and Earth system analysis, resting on the SCORPAN framework and its use of remote-sensing and terrain covariates as indicators of soil-forming processes. Similar approaches estimate ecological and hydrological conditions from vegetation, moisture, and climate data. Two assumptions receive little scrutiny: that soil-covariate relationships stay constant in space and time, and that covariates act as independent predictors. In reality vegetation, soil, and water form a coupled system in which each influences the others, and the strength and even the direction of these interactions vary across landscapes and shift over time. We argue that these dynamic relationships are an important but under-recognised source of structural uncertainty, distinct from the sampling, measurement, and model-fitting error usually partitioned in DSM. Drawing on wetlands, drylands, sloping farmland, burned watersheds, drought-affected forests, and thawing permafrost, we show how the feedbacks break the assumptions behind DSM, why the same problem affects land-surface, ecological, and hydrological models, and how mapping might be made feedback-aware.

title: Compound microbial intelligent membrane fermentation reshapes the virome and reduces various resistance genes in duck litter
summary: Contamination of duck litter is a major contributor to frequent disease outbreaks in the scaled dry-litter rearing system, posing serious threats to duck health. Although compound microbial intelligent membrane fermentation has multiple adv
content: Contamination of duck litter is a major contributor to frequent disease outbreaks in the scaled dry-litter rearing system, posing serious threats to duck health. Although compound microbial intelligent membrane fermentation has multiple advantages, its impacts on the litter virome and resistome remain poorly characterized. This study employed metaviromics to examine the effects of compound microbial intelligent membrane high-temperature fermentation on duck litter from four treatment groups: deep-layer fermentation (DL-D), shallow-layer fermentation (DL-S-NAF), shallow-layer without fermentation (DL-S), and shallow-layer from an antibiotic-using farm without fermentation (DL-S-ANF). We observed that fermentation treatments (DL-D and DL-S-NAF) significantly reduced RNA viral abundance, with a corresponding decreasing trend for DNA viruses. Fermentation treatments also markedly decreased the loads of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) including sul1 , sul2 , tetB(P) , and qacEdelta1 ; metal resistance genes ( MRGs ) including arsC , arsM , merA , copR , and corR ; biocide resistance genes including mdeA , actP , smdB , cpxA , and galE ; and bacterial virulence factors including g groEL2 and lirB . In duck litter, viral communities were dominated by Uroviricota and Nucleocytoviricota (DNA viruses) and Pisuviricota and Lenarviricota (RNA viruses), with Caudoviricetes and Megaviricetes as the predominant DNA virus classes. Single-sample metavirome analysis identified 34 viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs) and 343 viral genes. ARG abundance followed a hierarchical trend of DL-D < DL-S-NAF < DL-S < DL-S-ANF, while MRG abundance showed DL-D < DL-S-NAF < DL-S-ANF < DL-S. Compound microbial intelligent membrane fermentation effectively reduced both DNA and RNA viral abundance, diminished resistance gene loads, and attenuated virulence factors in duck litter. These data indicate that RNA viruses, particularly Pisuviricota , are sensitive bioindicators for ecological health assessment. Additionally, this antibiotic-free fermentation system may provide an important strategy for curbing dissemination of antimicrobial resistance at its source.

title: Design and Realization of Double-star Squirrel Cage Induction Motor
source: Periodica Polytechnica Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
summary: This article presents an in-depth study and a systematic design of a double-star squirrel-cage induction motor with a rated power of 3 kW and a synchronous speed of 3000 rpm. The proposed design method is supported by a thorough finite elem
content: This article presents an in-depth study and a systematic design of a double-star squirrel-cage induction motor with a rated power of 3 kW and a synchronous speed of 3000 rpm. The proposed design method is supported by a thorough finite element analysis performed using electromagnetic simulation tools. The design calculations and simulation results were validated through the fabrication and experimental testing of a prototype of the machine. The test results show excellent agreement with the theoretical predictions and numerical simulations, thereby confirming the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed design method. In fact, the calculated stator resistance R1 at 20°C is 13.24 Ω, while the simulated value is 13 Ω. The experimental measurement taken at 23 °C yields a resistance of 13.22 Ω. The expected rotational speed is 2880 rpm, and the simulation speed is Nr = 2940 rpm, whereas the rotor speed obtained during the experimental tests is 2931 rpm. The rated power factor cos φ = 0.84, while the value obtained experimentally is 0.82. This deviation is small and is consistent with the expected behavior of the machine.The results obtained highlight a strong correlation between theoretical analyses, numerical simulations, and experimental tests, thereby demonstrating the suitability of the double-star squirrel-cage induction motor configuration for high-performance industrial applications.

title: Limited mitigation potential of downstream waste management: A facility-level life cycle assessment of hospital PPE systems
summary: Healthcare systems generate substantial volumes of plastic-rich waste, with single-use personal protective equipment (PPE) accounting for an increasingly large share. While healthcare waste management has received significant attention, the
content: Healthcare systems generate substantial volumes of plastic-rich waste, with single-use personal protective equipment (PPE) accounting for an increasingly large share. While healthcare waste management has received significant attention, the real-world mitigation potential of downstream interventions remains insufficiently quantified. This study presents a facility-level life cycle assessment (LCA) of hospital PPE waste management based on multi-year operational data (2019–2023) from a Hungarian hospital. Using a cradle-to-grave system boundary with defined upstream exclusions and the ReCiPe 2016 Midpoint (H) method, environmental impacts were evaluated across alternative end-of-life (EoL) routing and waste segregation scenarios under real operating conditions. Results show that impacts are primarily driven by upstream material production and consumption, with PPE throughput directly determining system-level burdens. Across all scenarios, human and freshwater toxicity dominate the environmental profile, exceeding climate-related impacts. Scenario analysis indicates that even under optimized conditions, downstream interventions—such as improved segregation and alternative EoL routing—provide limited mitigation within the studied system, reducing the combined normalized score for human and freshwater toxicity by less than 7%. These findings highlight a structural constraint in healthcare waste systems, where mitigation potential is inherently limited downstream relative to upstream drivers. While segregation remains an important operational parameter, effective mitigation requires prioritizing upstream strategies, such as demand reduction, material substitution, and procurement-based interventions.

title: ENERGY-CONSUMING SYSTEMS AND ENERGY PERFORMANCE ASSESSMENT OF THE BAYERO UNIVERSITY KANO SENATE BUILDING FOR SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT
source: International Journal of African Sustainable Development Research
summary: Institutional buildings in hot-climate regions are often categorised as high operational energy demanding, because cooling systems operate for extended periods with limited energy-efficiency measures. This study evaluates the energy-consumi
content: Institutional buildings in hot-climate regions are often categorised as high operational energy demanding, because cooling systems operate for extended periods with limited energy-efficiency measures. This study evaluates the energy-consuming systems and energy performance of the Senate Building at Bayero University Kano (BUK), which is located within the Sahel Savannah ecological zone of north-western Nigeria, in order to establish an empirical baseline for subsequent energy optimisation. Building energy audit was undertaken using systematic on-site inspection, inventory of equipment, load assessment, and analysis of operational characteristics. A total of 380 split-unit air-conditioning systems with a combined cooling capacity of 2,004.5 kW thermal was identified, 1,564 lighting fixtures with a total installed load of 39.03 kW, and a total measured electrical demand of 193.51 kW was recorded. The Energy Use Intensity (EUI) calculated (1,020.7 kWh/m²/year) significantly exceeds the UNEP benchmark of 250 kWh/m²/year for institutional buildings in developing nations. Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems were identified as the major energy consumers. Contributing factors to this high demand include extended daily operating hours (15 hours/day), absence of automated environmental controls, absence of Energy efficiency measures and exclusive reliance on decentralized split-unit air conditioners. This study establishes a foundation for empirical data necessary for formulating targeted energy optimization strategies and developing AI-based energy management frameworks for institutional buildings in Northern Nigeria, directly supporting Sustainable Development Goal 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

title: The dual role of biochar in modulating microplastic effects on soil nitrogen
summary: Microplastics persist in the environment due to their resistance to degradation and pose an increasing concern for terrestrial ecosystems, threatening soil physicochemical properties and nitrogen (N) cycling. Biochar is widely used to impro
content: Microplastics persist in the environment due to their resistance to degradation and pose an increasing concern for terrestrial ecosystems, threatening soil physicochemical properties and nitrogen (N) cycling. Biochar is widely used to improve soil quality and mitigate contamination. However little is known about how biochar modulates microplastic effects on soil N cycling. Therefore, we conducted a soil incubation experiment to investigate the effects of different polyethylene microplastic particle sizes (6.5, 600 and 1700 μm) on soil N dynamics and to evaluate the combined influence of biochar in microplastic-contaminated soils. Although significant differences among individual microplastic-size treatments were observed at some sampling times, no consistent particle-size dependent effect on soil nitrogen pools was observed throughout the incubation period. However, the addition of biochar significantly increased soil total N, nitrate-N, and alkali-hydrolyzable N contents. Microbial community analysis revealed that the 1700 μm polyethylene microplastic combined with biochar resulted in distinct microbial community structures compared with the control treatment, particularly after 45 days of incubation. Microbial community analysis revealed that the combination of polyethylene microplastics and biochar altered the composition of the dominant bacterial genera, with the greatest community shift observed under the 1700 μm microplastic treatment after 45 days of incubation. Overall, both microplastic presence and biochar amendment altered soil microbial community composition. These findings suggest that corn straw biochar may improve soil nitrogen availability under the experimental conditions of this study and provide insight into microbial responses to polyethylene microplastics. Additional studies across different soil types, biochar feedstocks, microplastic polymers, and field conditions are needed to evaluate the broader applicability of these findings.

title: Fungal‐Assisted Recycling of Carbon‐Fiber‐Reinforced Polymer Waste via Mechanistically Informed Hybrid Pathways
summary: ABSTRACT Epoxy‐based carbon‐fiber‐reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites are increasingly used in high‐performance applications, yet their highly cross‐linked and chemically resistant matrices remain difficult to recycle sustainably. Conventi
content: ABSTRACT Epoxy‐based carbon‐fiber‐reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites are increasingly used in high‐performance applications, yet their highly cross‐linked and chemically resistant matrices remain difficult to recycle sustainably. Conventional recycling methods typically depend on high temperatures, aggressive chemicals, or intensive mechanical processing, which can degrade fiber integrity and impose substantial environmental burdens. Here, we report a hybrid bio‐enabled recycling strategy that integrates targeted physicochemical pretreatments, fungal‐mediated epoxy degradation, and low‐temperature thermal post‐processing to selectively weaken and remove epoxy matrices under comparatively mild conditions. Acetic‐acid solvolysis, ultraviolet irradiation, and oxidative pretreatments increased epoxy bioavailability through surface oxidation, bond cleavage and defect formation. Among four fungal strains investigated, Aspergillus flavus exhibited the highest degradative activity, achieving 15.5% composite mass loss within 30 days following solvolysis pretreatment, compared with 2.1% for Aspergillus niger . Microscopic and spectroscopic analyses revealed progressive resin thinning, fiber exposure and oxidative–hydrolytic depolymerization, with cumulative mass loss reaching 25.5% over 60 days. The 24–48 h high‐rate interval informed a cyclic treatment that produced increased matrix erosion and fiber exposure. Subsequent low‐temperature treatment at 425°C enabled clean fiber recovery with reduced volatile formation. These findings establish a mechanistically informed biological‐thermal pathway for CFRP recycling that supports progress toward circular composite material systems.

title: Development of Eu 3+ Doped MoO 3 Nanostructures for Emerging Photovoltaic and Photocatalytic Applications
summary: ABSTRACT Introducing Eu into the host lattice modifies its electronic structure for improving the power conversion efficiency of hetero‐junction solar cells and water‐purification technologies. The prepared nanomaterials were well character
content: ABSTRACT Introducing Eu into the host lattice modifies its electronic structure for improving the power conversion efficiency of hetero‐junction solar cells and water‐purification technologies. The prepared nanomaterials were well characterized by various spectral techniques viz; XRD, SEM‐EDX, TEM, XPS and FT‐IR analysis. The phase purity and crystalline structure typically confirming the orthorhombic geometry of Eu‐MoO 3 nanoparticle using XRD study. XPS characterized the successful incorporation of Eu 3+ ions into the lattice and exact chemical valence states of Mo 6+ /Mo 5+ and Eu 3+ /Eu 2+ , maps the concentration of oxygen vacancies induced by green combustion. Under Sun‐light irradiation, the Eu‐MoO 3 nanoparticles demonstrated enhanced degradation kinetics against RhB dye than host‐MoO 3 nanoparticle, which is attributed to efficient charge separation mediated by the Eu 3+ dopant states. The degradation efficiencies of host and Eu‐MoO 3 nanoparticles were found to be 83% and 95% after 165 min under Sun‐light irradiation. The fabricated DSSCs were subjected to J‐V analysis under a solar simulator to evaluate their photovoltaic performance. The open‐circuit voltage of the DSSC fabricated with Eu 3+ was found to be 0.687 V, which is higher than host‐MoO 3 (0.652 V). Eu doped DSSC showed a higher J SC of 4.664 mA/cm 2 than host‐MoO 3 (4.0 mA/cm 2 ). As a result, the power conversion efficiency increased from 0.85% to 1.11% for the Eu‐doped DSSCs. This research work offers valuable insights into modifying nanomaterial electronic properties for highly efficient photocatalytic and photovoltaic applications.

title: Empowering local communities for climate resilience: The role of participatory communication and collective action in West Java's proklim program
summary: Climate change in Indonesia has intensified extreme weather events, disrupted agricultural systems and water availability, increased health risks, and degraded environmental quality. In response, community-based climate adaptation initiativ
content: Climate change in Indonesia has intensified extreme weather events, disrupted agricultural systems and water availability, increased health risks, and degraded environmental quality. In response, community-based climate adaptation initiatives have emerged alongside government programs, including the Climate Village Program (Program Kampung Iklim, Proklim). This study examines how participatory communication, community leadership, and collective environmental practices operate at the local level within Proklim communities in West Java. Adopting a descriptive–interpretive qualitative design, this study draws on in-depth interviews with 14 key informants and field observations conducted in Bandung City, Cimahi City, Bogor Regency, and Subang Regency. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis (Braun and Clarke) to identify patterned meanings across cases. The findings suggest that community-based waste management, the use of household land for urban farming, and the local processing of environmental resources may contribute to forms of grassroots climate resilience. These practices appear to be supported by participatory communication processes characterized by interpersonal engagement, trust, kinship-based relations, and collective learning through face-to-face interaction and group-based forums. Local leadership was interpreted by participants as playing an important role in translating policy frameworks into everyday environmental practices and sustaining community participation. The findings further suggest that perceived community empowerment was reflected in opportunities for community voice, participation in local decision-making, practical capacity development, access to institutional networks, and collective ownership of environmental initiatives. These dimensions are interpreted as contextually situated perceptions rather than as objectively measured outcomes. This study contributes to environmental communication scholarship by showing how participatory communication, trust-based leadership, and collective action may be understood as interconnected social processes associated with perceived community empowerment and grassroots climate resilience in the Indonesian context.

title: Valorization of Wheat Straw Hydrolysate into Succinic Acid by Fermentation with Actinobacillus succinogenes
summary: Succinic acid (SA) production from agro-industrial waste, such as lignocellulosic biomass, has been gaining interest. Traditionally, it is synthesized from petrochemical sources, a process associated with negative environmental impacts. In
content: Succinic acid (SA) production from agro-industrial waste, such as lignocellulosic biomass, has been gaining interest. Traditionally, it is synthesized from petrochemical sources, a process associated with negative environmental impacts. In recent decades, efforts to develop cleaner production methods have led to the establishment of biotechnological routes based on fermentative microorganisms, such as Actinobacillus succinogenes. This strain is well known for its ability to metabolize a wide range of sugars, particularly glucose and xylose, which can be derived from the pretreatment of lignocellulosic biomass. However, due to the variable composition of the starting material, such as differences in fermentable sugar concentrations and the presence of inhibitory compounds, optimization of the fermentation process is necessary. In this study, the fermentation for production of bio-succunic acid from wheat straw hydrolysate was optimized in respect to medium composition. Two different dilutions of hydrolyzed wheat straw (50% and 90% v/v) were tested. In addition, the concentration of yeast extract, used as nutrients as supplement, and magnesium carbonate supplied for pH buffer, were evaluated at two levels: 10 and 25 g·L-1 for yeast extract, and 30 and 60 g·L-1 for magnesium carbonate. Various combinations of these compounds were investigated. The highest SA production (12.87 g·L-1, yield of 62.1%) was achieved using 90% (v/v) hydrolysate combined with 10 g·L-1 yeast extract and 60 g·L-1 magnesium carbonate. The results provide valuable insights into the utilization of challenging lignocellulosic substrates, such as wheat straw, for SA production and lay the groundwork for future process scale-up.

title: A Novel Spherical Fuzzy Schweizer-Sklar Prioritized Framework for Resilient Internet Router Selection in Smart City Digital Infrastructures
source: Journal of Urban Intelligence and Smart Systems
summary: The digital backbone of any smart city rests upon reliable routing infrastructure, where router reliability governs data throughput for traffic management, public safety, and utility grids. Selecting optimal routers involves intricate trade
content: The digital backbone of any smart city rests upon reliable routing infrastructure, where router reliability governs data throughput for traffic management, public safety, and utility grids. Selecting optimal routers involves intricate trade-offs among bandwidth, security, latency, and cost, all shrouded in expert ambiguity. To methodically resolve this inherent uncertainty, we propose a novel and robust multi-attribute decision-making paradigm anchored in spherical fuzzy sets (SFSs), which capture three-dimensional membership, abstinence, and non-membership grades, seamlessly integrated with Schweizer-Sklar t-norms and t-conorms for flexible parameter-sensitive aggregation. We formally introduce two pioneering operators, namely spherical fuzzy Schweizer-Sklar weighted prioritized aggregation (SFSSWPA) and geometric (SFSSWPG), embedding prioritized hierarchical inter-criteria relationships, thereby ensuring that dominant attributes receive proportionally greater decision weight. The complete multi attribute decision making (MADM) algorithm is validated through a real-world router procurement case study situated within urban critical network infrastructure deployments. Exhaustive comparative assessments against several established fuzzy MADM benchmarks consistently confirm our approach's superior ranking stability and remarkable parameter adaptability.

title: Sustainable Aqua-Tech: Transforming Aquaculture in Bangladesh Using Modern Technological Innovations
source: Journal of Scientific and Technological Research
summary: Aquaculture in Bangladesh is primarily characterized by smallholder inland freshwater carp, pangas, and tilapia farming in ponds, as well as some shrimp and prawn farming in coastal areas. It is quite different from the large-scale offshore
content: Aquaculture in Bangladesh is primarily characterized by smallholder inland freshwater carp, pangas, and tilapia farming in ponds, as well as some shrimp and prawn farming in coastal areas. It is quite different from the large-scale offshore systems frequently discussed in global technology reviews, so there is a gap between the available innovations and what is feasible locally. This review covers technologies like IoT, Cloud computing, Artificial intelligence, Robotics, Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS), Integrated Multi-Trophic Aquaculture (IMTA), aquaponics, and Alternative protein feeds for fish. The technologies are assessed for their suitability to the size, infrastructure, and economics of Bangladeshi aquaculture. The results indicate that the most feasible alternatives for the present are the use of low-cost sensor-based aeration, mobile and SMS management tools, small-scale biofloc-assisted RAS for hatcheries and high-value species, and plant or insect-based feed alternatives. This is supported by recent pilot projects on tilapia-catfish RAS (Bangladesh) and on IMTA prawn systems. In contrast, technologies suitable for offshore or larger-scale operations, like full-scale industrial RAS, deep-sea smart cages, and traditional seaweed-based marine IMTA, are hampered by problems of unreliable electricity supply, lack of resources for accessing capital, support services, and IMTA's inability to match the mostly freshwater, inland production in Bangladesh. Thus, technology implementation in Bangladesh must be delivered on a local level and local infrastructure rather than being blindly repeated from foreign models. This review provides a pathway for near- and long-term adoption to inform policy and investment decisions.

title: Arz Yönlü Aksaklıkların Temel Mal Gruplarına Geçişkenliği: Gıda ve Enerji Fiyatları Üzerine Ampirik Bir İnceleme
summary: Bu çalışma, Türkiye ekonomisinde küresel tedarik zinciri aksaklıklarının, hanehalkı tüketim sepetinde yüksek oynaklığa ve katı talebe sahip gıda ve enerji enflasyonu alt kalemleri üzerindeki geçişkenliğini 2021:M1- 2025:M12 dönemini kapsaya
content: Bu çalışma, Türkiye ekonomisinde küresel tedarik zinciri aksaklıklarının, hanehalkı tüketim sepetinde yüksek oynaklığa ve katı talebe sahip gıda ve enerji enflasyonu alt kalemleri üzerindeki geçişkenliğini 2021:M1- 2025:M12 dönemini kapsayan aylık verilerle yapısal vektör otoregresyon (SVAR) yöntemiyle ampirik olarak incelemektedir. Model kapsamında dışsal arz şoklarını temsil eden küresel tedarik zinciri baskı endeksi (GSCPI), reel efektif döviz kuru, TCMB politika faiz oranı ile gıda ve enerji enflasyonu değişkenleri arasındaki eş anlı ve dinamik ilişkiler analiz edilmiştir. Elde edilen etki-tepki fonksiyonları bulguları, küresel tedarik zinciri baskılarının hem gıda hem de enerji fiyatları üzerinde kısa vadede yadsınamaz bir geçişkenliğe sahip olduğunu göstermektedir. Çalışmanın en çarpıcı sonucu, Türkiye'deki yüksek ithalat bağımlılığı nedeniyle döviz kuru kanalının dışsal maliyet şoklarını yerel fiyatlara aktarmada ana hızlandırıcı ve şiddetlendirici rol oynamasıdır. Diğer taraftan, merkez bankasının politika faiz artış şoklarının gıda fiyatları üzerindeki etkisi istatistiki olarak zayıf kalırken; enerji fiyatları üzerinde literatürdeki "Fiyat Bilmecesi" (Price Puzzle) fenomeniyle uyumlu şekilde gecikmeli bir fiyat artış baskısı yarattığı saptanmıştır. Bu durum, arz yönlü ve yapısal kökenli enflasyonist baskılarla mücadelede sadece geleneksel para politikasının yeterli olmadığını, makro-ihtiyati tedbirlerin, döviz kuru istikrarının ve arz güvenliğinin eş güdümlü olarak devreye sokulması gerektiğini ortaya koymaktadır.

title: Petrol İhracatçısı Bir Ekonomide Ödemeler Dengesi Kısıtı: Azerbaycan'da Thirlwall Yasası'nın Geçerliliği
summary: Bu çalışmanın amacı, petrol ihracatçısı bir ülke olan Azerbaycan ekonomisinde 1993-2024 dönemi için Thirlwall Yasası’nın geçerliliğini incelemektir. Thirlwall Yasası, ülkelerin ödemeler dengesi kısıtlı büyüme oranını (Balance of Payments Co
content: Bu çalışmanın amacı, petrol ihracatçısı bir ülke olan Azerbaycan ekonomisinde 1993-2024 dönemi için Thirlwall Yasası’nın geçerliliğini incelemektir. Thirlwall Yasası, ülkelerin ödemeler dengesi kısıtlı büyüme oranını (Balance of Payments Constrained Growth-BPCG), ihracat büyüme oranının ithalat talebinin gelir esnekliğine bölünmesi yoluyla hesaplamaktadır. İthalat talebinin gelir esnekliğinin tahmin edilmesinde ARDL sınır testi yaklaşımından yararlanılmıştır. Elde edilen ithalat gelir esnekliği katsayısı, hem Thirlwall’ın orijinal modeli hem de Moreno-Brid (2003) tarafından geliştirilen modifiye edilmiş model çerçevesinde BPCG oranının hesaplanmasında kullanılmıştır. Daha sonra hesaplanan BPCG oranları ile gerçekleşen ekonomik büyüme oranları arasındaki sapmalar analiz edilmiştir. Ampirik bulgular, Azerbaycan ekonomisinde Thirlwall (1979) ve Moreno-Brid (2003) tarafından geliştirilen ödemeler dengesi kısıtlı büyüme modellerinin farklı dönemlerde değişen düzeylerde açıklayıcılığa sahip olduğunu ortaya koymaktadır. Bulgular, ekonomik büyümenin büyük ölçüde petrol gelirlerine ve dış talep koşullarına bağlı olduğunu göstermektedir. Bu durum, ihracat yapısında çeşitlendirme sağlanamadığı takdirde ekonomik büyümenin dışsal şoklara karşı kırılganlığını sürdüreceğine işaret etmektedir. Bu çerçevede, ihracatın yapısal dönüşümünü destekleyecek sanayi politikalarının güçlendirilmesi önem arz etmektedir. Özellikle petrol dışı sektörlerin, imalat sanayinin ve yüksek katma değerli üretim faaliyetlerinin geliştirilmesi, ihracat performansının yalnızca emtia fiyatlarındaki dalgalanmalara değil, aynı zamanda verimlilik artışlarına da dayanmasını sağlayarak daha sürdürülebilir bir büyüme yapısının oluşmasına katkıda bulunacaktır.

title: Bagasse compost pelletization: Sustainable densification for agricultural waste management
summary: This study investigated the physical, mechanical, and microstructural properties of bagasse compost to optimize its densification into durable pellets for agricultural applications. Bagasse compost was initially subjected to hammer milling
content: This study investigated the physical, mechanical, and microstructural properties of bagasse compost to optimize its densification into durable pellets for agricultural applications. Bagasse compost was initially subjected to hammer milling across various moisture contents (8-16% wet basis) and screen sizes (1-4 mm). Results showed that specific grinding energy increased exponentially with moisture content and decreased with larger screen sizes, ranging from 11 to 750 kJ/kg. Particle size distributions were characterized, revealing broader distributions with coarser screens. Pellets were subsequently produced using a closed-die hydraulic press under controlled pressures (50-150 MPa), moisture contents (8-20%), and particle sizes (1-4 mm). Compaction energy, fracture resistance, and pellet density were modeled using Response Surface Methodology. Increasing pressure significantly enhanced compaction energy, fracture resistance, and pellet density. Higher moisture content generally reduced compaction energy but improved fracture resistance, while pellet density exhibited an initial increase followed by a decrease. Particle size had a less pronounced effect on compaction energy and density but positively influenced fracture resistance. Microstructural analysis via Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) revealed more open fiber bundles and cracks in compost compared to raw bagasse, indicative of structural changes. X-Ray Diffraction (XRD) analysis showed an increased crystallinity index in compost due to the degradation of amorphous regions (hemicellulose and lignin), with crystalline cellulose remaining stable. Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) identified the compost's average glass transition temperature at 89.7 °C, highlighting the importance of temperature control during densification to preserve beneficial microorganisms. Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy confirmed significant chemical changes, particularly the degradation of hemicellulose. These findings offer crucial insights for optimizing bagasse compost pelletization for sustainable and efficient utilization.

title: Türkiye ve Küresel Ölçekte Gıda Fiyat Histerisinin Analizi
summary: Ekonomik istikrarın sağlanması açısından en kritik makroekonomik belirleyicilerden biri olan enflasyon kavramı içerisinde, gıda enflasyonu, gerek kendine has dinamikleri gerekse sosyo-ekonomik etkileri bakımından önemli bir bileşen olarak k
content: Ekonomik istikrarın sağlanması açısından en kritik makroekonomik belirleyicilerden biri olan enflasyon kavramı içerisinde, gıda enflasyonu, gerek kendine has dinamikleri gerekse sosyo-ekonomik etkileri bakımından önemli bir bileşen olarak karşımıza çıkmaktadır. Bu bağlamda çalışmada, 2005M01-2026M05 aylık verileri kullanılarak hem Türkiye hem de küresel ölçekte gıda fiyatları histerisi ampirik olarak incelenmiştir. Yöntem olarak, yapısal kırılmaları dikkate alan, ani ve yumuşak değişimleri modele kendiliğinden dahil edebilen, Kesirli Fourier Genişletilmiş Dickey-Fuller (FADF) birim kök testi kullanılmıştır. Analiz bulguları, küresel ölçüde gıda fiyatları histerisinin geçerli olmadığını; Türkiye’de ise gıda fiyatları histerisinin varlığını ortaya koymaktadır.

title: Amino acid metabolism by pig intestinal bacteria and consequences for intestinal health and environment: current knowledge and future directions
source: Journal of Animal Science and Biotechnology/Journal of animal science and biotechnology
summary: Amino acids available for bacteria within the small intestine of pigs are originating mainly from the dietary and endogenous proteins. These amino acids, in addition to those synthesized by the intestinal bacteria, are used in different met
content: Amino acids available for bacteria within the small intestine of pigs are originating mainly from the dietary and endogenous proteins. These amino acids, in addition to those synthesized by the intestinal bacteria, are used in different metabolic pathways. The amino acids that cannot be synthesized by the intestinal bacteria can be considered as indispensable for them and must thus be obtained from the surrounding luminal fluid. In the pig large intestine, the amino acids used by bacteria originate presumably mainly from proteins not fully digested in the small intestine. In this narrative review, we present the current knowledge concerning the metabolism of amino acids by bacteria found in the pig gut and the effects of the different amino acid-derived bacterial metabolites on the metabolism and physiology of the intestinal microbes. The effects of some among these compounds, either beneficial or deleterious, on the intestinal epithelial cells are then recapitulated. Next, the adverse impact of the emission of two bacterial metabolites derived from amino acids, namely ammonia and hydrogen sulfide, on the environment is described. Future directions in the field of the control of the metabolism of amino acids by the intestinal bacteria for the maintenance of pig intestinal health, as well as for the reduction of the emission of polluting substances are proposed.

title: Makro İktisatta Yeni Perspektifler
summary: Küresel ekonominin geçirmekte olduğu derin dönüşüm süreci; geleneksel makroekonomik yaklaşımların, politikaların ve varsayımların yeniden sorgulanmasını zorunlu kılmaktadır. Son yıllarda yaşanan yapısal kırılmalar, jeopolitik riskler, iklim
content: Küresel ekonominin geçirmekte olduğu derin dönüşüm süreci; geleneksel makroekonomik yaklaşımların, politikaların ve varsayımların yeniden sorgulanmasını zorunlu kılmaktadır. Son yıllarda yaşanan yapısal kırılmalar, jeopolitik riskler, iklim krizi, tedarik zincirlerindeki aksaklıklar ve enflasyonist baskılar, makro iktisat literatürüne hem teorik hem de ampirik düzeyde yeni perspektifler kazandırmıştır. Bu dönüşüm; konut piyasalarından dış ticarete, gıda ve enerji fiyat geçişkenliğinden toplumsal cinsiyet dinamiklerine ve merkez bankacılığına kadar geniş bir yelpazede yeni analitik araçların ve ekonometrik yaklaşımların kullanılmasını gerekli kılmaktadır. “Makro İktisatta Yeni Perspektifler” adlı bu eser, söz konusu dinamik ve karmaşık iktisadi yapıyı daha iyi anlayabilmek, ampirik bulgular ışığında özgün katkılar sunmak ve literatürdeki güncel tartışmaları zenginleştirmek amacıyla hazırlanmıştır. Sekiz farklı bölümden oluşan bu çalışma, her biri kendi alanında uzman araştırmacıların dinamik ve yenilikçi yaklaşımlarını bir araya getirmektedir. Kitapta yer alan ana bölümler; Konut Piyasası ve Histeri: Türkiye geneli ve iller bazında konut birim fiyatlarındaki şokların kalıcılığını çok kırılmalı birim kök testleriyle inceleyerek bölgesel dinamiklere ışık tutmakta, Ödemeler Dengesi ve Büyüme: Petrol ihracatçısı bir ülke örneği olarak Azerbaycan özelinde Thirlwall Yasası'nın geçerliliğini ve dışsal kısıtların büyüme üzerindeki etkilerini sınamakta, Fiyat Geçişkenliği ve Enflasyon: Arz yönlü aksaklıkların gıda ve enerji gibi temel mal gruplarına yansıması ile petrol ithalatçısı gelişmekte olan ülkelerde döviz kuru ve petrol fiyatı geçişkenliğinin enflasyonist dinamiklerini ampirik yöntemlerle ortaya koymakta, Toplumsal Cinsiyet ve İşgücü: Tarımda kadın emeğini ve toplumsal cinsiyet dengesizliklerini Türkiye ekonomisi çerçevesinde makroekonomik bir boyutta ele almakta, Gıda Fiyat Histerisi: Hem Türkiye hem de küresel ölçekte gıda fiyatlarındaki şokların kalıcılığını ve yapısal etkilerini analiz etmekte, Para Politikası ve İstihdam: Merkez bankalarının kredibilite açığının istihdam piyasası üzerindeki etkilerini Fourier yaklaşımlı zaman serisi yöntemleriyle inceleyerek politika yapıcılara önemli ampirik bulgular sunmakta, Uluslararası Ticaret ve Sürdürülebilirlik: Küreselleşen ekonomide dış ticaret ile iklim değişikliği arasındaki karşılıklı etkileşimi uluslararası boyutta değerlendirmektedir. Eserin hazırlanmasında kıymetli katkılarını sunan, titiz araştırmaları ve özgün analizleriyle kitaba değer katan tüm bölüm yazarlarımıza şükranlarımı sunarım. Ayrıca kitabın yayına hazırlanmasında, basımında ve sizlerle buluşmasında gösterdikleri titiz ve profesyonel yaklaşımlarından dolayı Özgür Yayınevi yönetimine, değerli editör ekibine ve emeği geçen tüm yayınevi çalışanlarına içtenlikle teşekkür ederim. Bu eserin; akademisyenlere, araştırmacılara, lisansüstü öğrencilere ve makroekonomik dinamikleri analiz etmek isteyen tüm okuyuculara temel bir başvuru kaynağı

title: EMJ.NEXUS IFRS ISSB + SASB to GRI Direct Mapping Guide

content: This independently published methodology guide maps 128 MME task positions to licensed IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards and SASB Standards source relationships and candidate GRI topic and disclosure routes. The analysis preserves the distinction between financial materiality and GRI impact materiality. The mappings do not determine material topics, establish equivalence, or demonstrate that a report has been prepared in accordance with the GRI Standards.

title: Tarımda Kadın Emeği ve Toplumsal Cinsiyet: Türkiye için Makroekonomik Bir İnceleme
summary: Tarım sektörü, kadınların üretim sürecine önemli katkılar sunduğu temel ekonomik faaliyet alanlarından biri olmasına rağmen, üretim kaynaklarına erişim, girişimcilik, dijital teknolojilerden yararlanma, sosyal güvenlik ve karar alma süreçle
content: Tarım sektörü, kadınların üretim sürecine önemli katkılar sunduğu temel ekonomik faaliyet alanlarından biri olmasına rağmen, üretim kaynaklarına erişim, girişimcilik, dijital teknolojilerden yararlanma, sosyal güvenlik ve karar alma süreçleri bakımından toplumsal cinsiyet temelli eşitsizlikler varlığını sürdürmektedir. Bu çalışma, tarımda kadın emeğini toplumsal cinsiyet perspektifi ve makroekonomik bir bakış açısıyla ele almaktadır. Bu kapsamda tarımda kadın emeğinin toplumsal cinsiyet boyutu incelenmekte; kadın girişimciliğinin tarım sektöründeki yeri ve kadın emeğinin makroekonomik etkileri Türkiye örneği üzerinden değerlendirilmektedir. Ayrıca kadınların üretim kaynaklarına erişim, dijital cinsiyet eşitsizliği, kayıt dışı istihdam ve sosyal güvenlik gibi alanlarda karşılaştıkları temel yapısal sorunlar ilgili literatür doğrultusunda tartışılmaktadır. Çalışmada, kadın emeğinin güçlendirilmesinin tarımsal verimlilik, kırsal kalkınma ve sürdürülebilir ekonomik kalkınma açısından stratejik önem taşıdığı vurgulanmakta; kadınların dijital teknolojilere erişiminin artırılması, finansman ve örgütlenme olanaklarının güçlendirilmesi ile sosyal koruma mekanizmalarının geliştirilmesine yönelik politika önerilerine yer verilmektedir.

title: Petrol İthalatçısı Gelişmekte Olan Ülkelerde Enflasyon Dinamikleri: Petrol Fiyatı ve Döviz Kuru Geçişkenliği
summary: Bu çalışma, küresel petrol fiyatlarının enflasyon üzerindeki tetikleyici rolünü enerji ithalatçısı yedi gelişmekte olan ekonomi (Türkiye, Brezilya, Hindistan, Endonezya, Meksika, Güney Afrika ve Tayland) için döviz kuru ve ekonomik büyüme k
content: Bu çalışma, küresel petrol fiyatlarının enflasyon üzerindeki tetikleyici rolünü enerji ithalatçısı yedi gelişmekte olan ekonomi (Türkiye, Brezilya, Hindistan, Endonezya, Meksika, Güney Afrika ve Tayland) için döviz kuru ve ekonomik büyüme kontrol değişkenleri altında analiz etmektedir. 2000-2024 dönemini kapsayan analizler, Pesaran vd. (1999) tarafından geliştirilen, serilerin farklı derecelerde durağan olmasına imkân tanıyan ve yatay kesit bağımlılığını dikkate alan Havuzlanmış Ortalama Grup (PMG) tahmincisi ile yürütülmüştür. Elde edilen ampirik bulgular, petrol fiyatlarının ve döviz kurunun uzun dönemde enflasyonun temel belirleyicileri olduğunu ortaya koymaktadır. Hata düzeltme teriminin istatistiksel olarak anlamlılığı, değişkenler arasındaki uzun dönemli eşbütünleşme ilişkisini teyit etmektedir. Standartlaştırılmış katsayılar, enflasyon varyasyonunu açıklama gücü bakımından döviz kurunun en baskın değişken olduğunu göstermektedir. Buna karşılık elastikiyet bulguları, petrol fiyatlarındaki marjinal değişimlere karşı enflasyonun daha yüksek tepki verdiğine işaret etmektedir. Bu yönüyle petrol fiyatları, enflasyonist şokların şiddeti ve marjinal fiyat baskısı açısından önemli bir tetikleyici gibi görünmektedir. Bu sonuçlar, döviz kurunun sürekli ve birikimli fiyatlama davranışları üzerinde etkili olduğunu, petrol fiyatlarının ise maliyet yönlü şoklar üzerinden daha güçlü marjinal baskılar oluşturduğunu düşündürmektedir. Bu çerçevede, enflasyonla mücadele stratejilerinde yalnızca para ve kur politikalarının değil, aynı zamanda petrol fiyat istikrarını destekleyici enerji politikaları ile arz güvenliğini güçlendiren yapısal önlemlerin de merkezi bir konumda olması gerektiği değerlendirilmektedir.

title: Unveiling green and nature-based solutions through innovative economic assessment- a case for circular water management system
summary: The impetus to move from aggressive environmentally damaging water management systems to sustainable alternatives is increasingly motivating both governments and investors. However, the economic justification for the often-heavy preliminary
content: The impetus to move from aggressive environmentally damaging water management systems to sustainable alternatives is increasingly motivating both governments and investors. However, the economic justification for the often-heavy preliminary capital expenditure becomes a stumbling block. It is found that classical economic assessments fall short of monetising the environmental gains and being incorporated into economic assessments. To address this gap, the proposed method integrates the Pressure–State–Response (PSR) framework with cost–benefit analysis (CBA) and taking three steps of firstly identifying the necessity of implementing circular water system (CWS), second, conducting a holistic cost-benefit analysis considering internal and external impacts, and third providing decision-making support by reviewing and refining the outputs. For proof of concept, a case study for circular water and the relevant Nature based solutions (NBS) is presented that aimed to address Mykonos island's severe water shortages by developing new economic activities. Results show the feasibility of implementing the CWS in the investigated area, with a Payback period (PP) of 3.2 years, Net present value (NPV) of €30,906, Modified internal rate of return (MIRR) of 13%, and Benefit-cost ratio (BCR) of 6.2. The result calculated for the same system without considering environmental and social benefit illustrate a noteworthy difference in system viability. The sensitivity analysis of NPV revealed that the economic viability of the system improves as cash flow and reclaimed water tariffs, increase and the project's lifespan, Operational and maintenance cost (OPEX), and Capital cost (CAPEX) and discount rate decrease. In our view, green technologies should be economically assessed by measuring and monetising its environmental impacts, just as we do for conventional water management.

title: Agricultural By‐Products and Black Soldier Fly Larvae Meal as Alternatives to Soybean Meal in Commercial Broiler Diets: Effects on Meat Quality, Fecal Microbiota, and Environmental Impact
source: Journal of Animal Physiology and Animal Nutrition
summary: ABSTRACT The present study aimed to evaluate the effect of partially replacing soybean meal with agricultural by‐products with or without supplementation of dried black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) meal on meat quality, intestinal microbiota o
content: ABSTRACT The present study aimed to evaluate the effect of partially replacing soybean meal with agricultural by‐products with or without supplementation of dried black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) meal on meat quality, intestinal microbiota of commercial broiler chickens, and environmental sustainability. A total of 252 day‐old Cobb 500 chicks were divided into three dietary treatments, including a corn‐soybean‐based Control diet and two alternative diets. Alternative diets were a diet in which soybean meal was replaced partly (SPR) by sunflower meal, brewers dried grain, and wheat middlings, and a diet in which BSFL meal was added (5%) to the SPR diet. At 39 days of age, the feces of chickens from each dietary treatment were sampled for fecal microbiota analysis. Birds were slaughtered at day 40 to assess breast meat quality. A life cycle assessment (LCA) was conducted to estimate the environmental impacts of each diet. The SPR and SPR+BSFL diets significantly ( p = 0.003) reduced breast meat pH 24 without affecting lightness and yellowness values. While cooking losses were similar in the breast meat of chickens fed the Control and SPR diets, adding BSFL meal to the SPR diet reduced cooking losses ( p < 0.001). The SPR+BSFL diet increased total saturated fatty acids (SFA), while the SPR diet elevated polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) content, particularly linoleic acid ( p < 0.001). Microbiota analysis revealed a higher abundance of Firmicutes, particularly Lactobacillus and Bacillus, in broilers fed the SPR+BSFL diet, while Clostridiaceae was more prevalent in the SPR group compared to the Control ( p < 0.01). These changes in microbiota were likely attributed to the increased fiber content of the diets. Environmental impact analysis showed that both SPR and SPR+BSFL diets reduced global warming potential, damage to ecosystems, human health burden, and resource use compared to the Control diet ( p < 0.001). The two alternative diets performed similarly in most environmental indicators. The results suggested that agricultural by‐products with or without BSFL meal supplementation could be used to partially replace soybean meal in the diets of commercial broiler chickens and would beneficially modulate gut microbiota and reduce the environmental footprint of broiler production.

title: Do productivity and income gains from climate-smart agriculture practices translate into food security? Evidence from smallholder farmers in central Malawi
summary: Climate-smart agriculture (CSA) is widely promoted to improve smallholder livelihoods under increasing climate risks, yet evidence on impacts beyond productivity, particularly multidimensional food security, remains limited. This study exam
content: Climate-smart agriculture (CSA) is widely promoted to improve smallholder livelihoods under increasing climate risks, yet evidence on impacts beyond productivity, particularly multidimensional food security, remains limited. This study examines determinants of adoption of selected CSA practices and their effects on maize productivity, farm income, food expenditure share, and dietary diversity among 510 smallholder households in Kasungu District, central Malawi. Using 2023 cross-sectional survey data, we employ a multinomial endogenous switching regression model to address potential selection bias across eight mutually exclusive adoption options based on three CSA practices. Gender of the household head, extension participation, and cooperative membership are significantly associated with adoption, with female-headed households more likely to adopt multiple-practice combinations. Average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) estimates indicate significant maize-yield and farm-income gains for certain options relative to the estimated non-adoption counterfactual. However, no practice option shows a statistically significant ATT estimate for dietary diversity measured by the Food Consumption Score, indicating a disconnect between estimated farm-income gains and dietary outcomes. The findings suggest that CSA may support productivity and income, but complementary nutrition-sensitive interventions may be needed to achieve multidimensional food security.

title: Vehicle CO₂ emission prediction based on firefly with ant colony optimization tuned long short-term memory model
summary: Accurate vehicle-level CO₂ emission prediction is essential for regulatory planning and greener powertrain design. This study presents an integrated FA-ACO-LSTM framework for estimating vehicle-level tailpipe CO₂ emissions from standard veh
content: Accurate vehicle-level CO₂ emission prediction is essential for regulatory planning and greener powertrain design. This study presents an integrated FA-ACO-LSTM framework for estimating vehicle-level tailpipe CO₂ emissions from standard vehicle descriptors. The contribution lies in combining leakage-aware Binary Firefly feature selection, mixed-variable FA-ACO hyperparameter tuning, repeated-run evaluation, and post hoc interpretability into a unified prediction pipeline. Using a public fuel-consumption dataset sourced from the official Canadian vehicle fuel-consumption and emissions registry (open government portal) (22,556 vehicles), we adopt a 70/20/10 train/validation/test split and perform wrapper-based feature selection with Binary Firefly Algorithm (BFA). The FA-ACO scheduler jointly tunes hyperparameters for five candidate learners (LSTM, CNN, GRU, MLP, TabNet) and selects the best. FA-ACO-LSTM attains MSE = 0.0099, MAE = 0.0791, MedAE = 0.0664, MAPE = 0.84%, and R² = 98.71% on the test set, surpassing FA-ACO-CNN (R² = 93.55%), FA-ACO-GRU (90.03%), FA-ACO-MLP (87.60%), and FA-ACO-TabNet (84.88%). Compared with untuned baselines, FA-ACO improves LSTM from R² = 96.53% to 98.71% and reduces MSE by 45%. BFA yields the lowest average error among feature selectors versus BMWO, BFO, and BGWO, and an ANOVA across models confirms significance (F = 30.2, p < 0.0001). These results represent a fuel-consumption-informed prediction scenario because the selected feature set includes COMB (L/100 km), HWY (L/100 km), and COMB (mpg), which are strongly associated with certified CO₂ emissions. When all fuel-consumption indicators were excluded before feature selection and training, model performance decreased from [Formula: see text]to [Formula: see text]. The ablation confirms that fuel-consumption proxies account for a substantial part of the main predictive performance, while non-consumption vehicle attributes retain meaningful predictive value, and indicates that, under the adopted fixed feature-ordering representation and FA-ACO tuning protocol, LSTM achieved the best performance among the evaluated neural and tabular baselines. However, because the dataset is cross-sectional rather than temporal, the LSTM should be interpreted as a feature-interaction learner rather than a temporal forecasting model.

title: Transition to Electric Vehicles across all spectrums is not just environmentally friendly but also cost effective in the long run
source: International Journal of Science and Social Science Research
summary: India is the world's third largest emitter of greenhouse gases and the second largest importer of crude oil, and its transport sector sits at the center of both problems, which makes the shift to electric vehicles a question of national int
content: India is the world's third largest emitter of greenhouse gases and the second largest importer of crude oil, and its transport sector sits at the center of both problems, which makes the shift to electric vehicles a question of national interest as much as an environmental one. This paper examines whether that shift is both environmentally beneficial and economically viable, and whether the case holds across all five vehicle segments, being two wheelers, three wheelers, four wheelers, trucks, and buses. Using registration data from 2022 to 2026 alongside primary data collected from the commercial vehicle sector, and applying regression analysis to identify trends across segments, the paper finds that EV adoption in India does not behave as a single market but as five distinct ones. Two and three wheelers are the most mature and are approaching the point where they no longer need subsidy to compete, four wheelers are growing quickly but remain constrained by upfront cost and a charging network well behind China and the United States, trucks are accelerating sharply though mostly in small urban cargo vehicles rather than heavy freight, and buses are growing in irregular batches because they are bought through government tenders rather than by individuals. The paper also finds that the environmental benefit of EVs in India is real but conditional on grid decarbonisation, since roughly 70% of the national grid still runs on coal, and that the economic case is strongest wherever vehicle utilisation is highest. Drawing on the experience of countries further along the adoption curve, including Norway, China, Ethiopia, and Nepal, the paper concludes that India's 2030 target of 30% EV penetration will depend less on momentum and more on how well policy, infrastructure, and grid decarbonisation are managed together.

title: Creditor Screening of Voluntary ESG Disclosure: Pillar Specificity and Operational Profitability as a Credibility Cue for Debt Pricing
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT Grounded in signaling and disclosure theory, we examine when and which voluntary ESG disclosure pillars are associated with firms' cost of debt in an emerging market setting characterized by voluntary reporting, concentrated owners
content: ABSTRACT Grounded in signaling and disclosure theory, we examine when and which voluntary ESG disclosure pillars are associated with firms' cost of debt in an emerging market setting characterized by voluntary reporting, concentrated ownership, and debt centered corporate finance. Using firm‐ and year‐fixed‐effects models and several robustness checks on a panel of Chilean listed firms from 2015 to 2022, we find that environmental and governance disclosures are more consistently associated with lower debt costs, whereas social disclosure shows weaker and less stable associations. Higher operational profitability strengthens the negative association between pillar disclosure and the cost of debt, consistent with a credibility‐based mechanism in which creditors appear to place greater weight on voluntary disclosure when it is anchored in observable operational capacity. By contrast, additional information‐channel tests show no robust direct or moderating role for institutional ownership or stock‐market liquidity. Robustness tests using alternative measures and sample restrictions preserve the operational profitability interaction patterns; dynamic specifications suggest that pillar main effects are estimated less precisely, supporting a cautious interpretation centered on credibility‐contingent associations rather than unconditional disclosure effects. Finally, reverse‐causality diagnostics provide no systematic evidence that lower borrowing costs precede higher subsequent ESG disclosure. Overall, the evidence is consistent with pillar specific differences in materiality and verifiability under voluntary disclosure regimes in debt financing centered markets with concentrated ownership. Our study contributes to the literature by clarifying that voluntary ESG disclosure is more likely to be credit‐relevant when creditors can interpret the pillar‐specific signal and when operational profitability enhances its credibility.

title: Merkez Bankası Kredibilite Açığının İstihdam Piyasasına Etkileri: Türkiye Ekonomisi’nden Fourier Yaklaşımlı Bulgular
summary: Bu çalışmada Türkiye ekonomisinde istihdam piyasasının merkez bankası kredibilite açığına nasıl tepki verdiğine odaklanılmaktadır. 2015:01-2026:01 dönemini kapsayan aylık zaman serisi verileriyle işsiz sayısının bağımlı değişken, çıpa sapma
content: Bu çalışmada Türkiye ekonomisinde istihdam piyasasının merkez bankası kredibilite açığına nasıl tepki verdiğine odaklanılmaktadır. 2015:01-2026:01 dönemini kapsayan aylık zaman serisi verileriyle işsiz sayısının bağımlı değişken, çıpa sapmasının ana bağımsız değişken, tüketici fiyat endeksi, döviz kuru, ülke risk primi ve sanayi üretim endeksi değişkenlerinin kontrol değişkenler olduğu bir model kurgulanmıştır. Modelde kullanılan hedef enflasyon serisi TCMB enflasyon raporlarında ilan edilen orta vadeli enflasyon tahmin patikalarının orta noktaları baz alınarak türetilmiştir. Kredibilite açığı değişkeni ise türetilen enflasyon hedefleri ile reel sektörün enflasyon beklentileri arasındaki fark ile temsil edilmektedir. Çalışmada tercih edilen 2015-2026 arası dönem, Türkiye ekonomisinde önce geleneksel iktisat politikalarından uzaklaşılan, ardından bu politikanın yarattığı tahribatı onarmak için tekrar rasyonel zemine dönülen, kalıcı ve güçlü yapısal kırılmaların yaşandığı bir dönemdir. İncelenen dönemde yaşanan radikal politika dönüşümlerini ve zamana yayılan doğrusal olmayan dalgalanmaları kontrol altına alabilmek amacıyla ampirik analizde Fourier fonksiyonlu Bootstrap ARDL metodolojisi tercih edilmiştir. Katsayı tahminlerinin güvenilirliğini artırmak amacıyla yapısal kırılmaların yaşandığı aylardaki anlık şokları izole etmek üzere modele kukla değişkenler eklenmiştir. Çalışmanın bulguları kısa dönemde kredibilite açığının piyasada ani bir şok etkisi yarattığını, firmaların fiyatlama davranışlarını bozarak istihdam piyasasını baskıladığını ileri sürmektedir. Özel ekonomik aktörlerin uzun vadeli istihdam kararlarında ise merkez bankasının resmi enflasyon hedeflerinin çıpa (anchor) olma özelliğini kaybettiği ortaya konmaktadır. Özel ekonomik aktörlerin uzun vadeli kararlarını doğrudan piyasada gerçekleşen maliyetler (gerçekleşen enflasyon, kur ve CDS primi) üzerinden şekillendirdiği ima edilmektedir.

title: Türkiye Genelinde ve İllerinde Konut Birim Fiyatlarında Histeri Etkisi: Çok Kırılmalı Birim Kök Testlerinden Bulgular
summary: Bu çalışmada, 2010:Q1-2026:Q1 dönemine ait çeyreklik veriler kullanılarak Türkiye geneli ve veri sürekliliği sağlanan 59 il için reel konut birim fiyatlarındaki şokların kalıcılığı ampirik olarak araştırılmıştır. Serilerdeki yapısal rejim d
content: Bu çalışmada, 2010:Q1-2026:Q1 dönemine ait çeyreklik veriler kullanılarak Türkiye geneli ve veri sürekliliği sağlanan 59 il için reel konut birim fiyatlarındaki şokların kalıcılığı ampirik olarak araştırılmıştır. Serilerdeki yapısal rejim değişikliklerini içsel olarak dikkate alan Kapetanios (2005) çok kırılmalı birim kök testinin uygulandığı analiz neticesinde, Türkiye genelinde ve incelenen illerin büyük bir çoğunluğunda (53 ilde) güçlü bir histeri etkisinin geçerli olduğu saptanmıştır. Buna karşın yalnızca 6 ilde konut fiyatlarının şoklar sonrasında tarihsel ortalamasına geri döndüğü tespit edilmiştir. Endojen olarak belirlenen yapısal kırılmaların kronolojik dağılımı, makroekonomik istikrarsızlıkların tırmandığı 2018 yılı ve sonrasındaki dönemde yoğunlaşmaktadır. Bu durum, 2018 yılında yaşanan kur şokunun, artan inşaat maliyetlerinin ve makroekonomik belirsizliklerin yerel konut piyasalarında kalıcı yapısal hasarlar bıraktığının ampirik bir göstergesidir. Çeyreklik bazda en yüksek kırılma yoğunlaşması, 2022:Q1 döneminde 31 ilde gerçekleşmiştir. Bu sonuç, 2021 yılının son çeyreğinde “Yeni Ekonomi Programı” çerçevesinde uygulamaya konulan agresif faiz indirimlerinin yol açtığı negatif reel faiz şokunun doğrudan bir sonucudur. Çalışma, konut fiyatlarındaki kalıcı artışların dar gelirlilerin konuta erişimini engelleyerek sosyal refah kaybına yol açtığını göstermektedir. Bu yapısal katılıkları aşmak için fiyat ve kur istikrarının yanı sıra, yabancıya konut satışının sınırlandırılması, ikincil konutlara artan oranlı vergi getirilmesi ve sosyal konutların yaygınlaştırılması zorunludur.

title: Evolution of ecological indicators in the assessment of restoration of mining‐degraded riparian forests: a global bibliometric analysis (1990–2024)
summary: Abstract Introduction The restoration of mining‐degraded riparian forests faces challenges due to structural, compositional, and functional impacts on these ecosystems. The demand for effective monitoring requires an understanding of how ec
content: Abstract Introduction The restoration of mining‐degraded riparian forests faces challenges due to structural, compositional, and functional impacts on these ecosystems. The demand for effective monitoring requires an understanding of how ecological indicators have been applied to assess post‐mining restoration success. Objectives To evaluate the restoration of riparian forests in mined areas based on scientific articles published in recent decades (1990–2024), seeking to identify temporal trends, geographic distribution, restoration methods, and patterns of integration among compositional, structural, and functional indicators. Methods A total of 101 articles selected from international databases were analyzed. Data were extracted to evaluate temporal and geographic distribution, journals, mineral types, restoration methods, and categories of ecological indicators. Results Publications increased markedly from 2020 onward, with China, the United States, Brazil, and Australia as leading contributors. Functional indicators predominated (87.3% in recent studies), with a progressive increase in the integration of composition, structure, and function. Seedling planting was the most frequent restoration method (48.3%). Indicator selection varied according to restoration method and mineral type, with integrated approaches more common in metallic mining, particularly gold. Conclusions The field has evolved from the use of isolated indicators to multidimensional assessments. Methodological variation persists across restoration methods and mineral types, highlighting the need for standardization to enable robust comparisons.

title: Organic Amendment Quality Regulates Greenhouse Gas Trade-Offs and Short-Term Carbon Retention During Reductive Soil Disinfestation
summary: Background/Objectives: Reductive soil disinfestation (RSD) is increasingly viewed as a viable alternative to chemical fumigation, yet the role of organic amendment quality in regulating greenhouse gas (GHG) fluxes, soil organic carbon (SOC)
content: Background/Objectives: Reductive soil disinfestation (RSD) is increasingly viewed as a viable alternative to chemical fumigation, yet the role of organic amendment quality in regulating greenhouse gas (GHG) fluxes, soil organic carbon (SOC) dynamics, and net climate forcing remains poorly understood. Methodology: In a 30-day anaerobic incubation experiment, we set up three treatments—a flooded control (CK), soil amended with wheat straw (WS, C/N = 55.5), and soil amended with kiwifruit branches (KB, C/N = 110.8)—each replicated three times under identical conditions. Results: Both WS and KB additions strongly stimulated CO2 and CH4 production, while suppressing N2O emissions by over 85% relative to CK. The WS treatment exhibited a substantially higher global warming potential (GWP, 823.52 t ha−1) than KB (636.23 t ha−1), with CH4 accounting for more than 99% of total GWP. Although WS surpassed KB in short-term carbon sequestration efficiency (25.79% vs. 20.11%) and showed greater hydrolytic enzyme activities (βG, CBH, and XYL), the two organic amendments diverged clearly in carbon fraction distribution: Cmic was 17.9% higher under WS, whereas Cmin was 16.2% higher under KB. When factoring in the CO2 equivalent benefit derived from carbon sequestration, the net GWP (NGWP) indicated that both RSD treatments remained net GHG sources. Notably, KB yielded a markedly lower NGWP (611.60 t CO2-eq ha−1) than WS (798.19 t CO2-eq ha−1), highlighting a fundamental trade-off: WS favored rapid SOC accumulation at the expense of elevated methane emissions, whereas KB achieved a smaller climatic footprint despite more moderate carbon retention. Conclusions: These findings underscore that selecting organic amendments for field RSD requires balancing the competing goals of carbon sequestration and GHG mitigation.

title: Should We Put Solar Panels in Rural Landscapes? Discrete Choice Modeling Reveals Preferences for Local Biodiversity and Community Benefits
summary: ABSTRACT Landscapes provide a range of ecosystem services including food production, biodiversity conservation and recreational value. Increasingly, landscapes are also used to generate energy. While this is essential for achieving climate
content: ABSTRACT Landscapes provide a range of ecosystem services including food production, biodiversity conservation and recreational value. Increasingly, landscapes are also used to generate energy. While this is essential for achieving climate mitigation targets, it affects biodiversity and the appearance of rural landscapes, potentially leading to public opposition. Previous research has addressed public opposition against wind turbines and regulatory solutions. However, despite holding the potential for similar conflicts, the ongoing large‐scale expansion of ground‐mounted photovoltaic (PV) installations has so far received less attention. We conduct a choice experiment in Germany to identify preferences regarding the expansion of ground‐mounted PV and its regulation. Three findings stand out: (1) A large majority of respondents support a regulated expansion. (2) There is no significant support for spatial planning regulation in terms of maximum size and density of PV installations, or minimum distance of PV installations from settlements. In contrast, respondents support the provision of local benefits. These include biodiversity benefits, an enhanced appearance of the landscape through flower strips and hedgerows, but also financial benefits like support for renewable energy communities, farmers in low‐yield areas, and the provision of local public goods such as kindergartens. (3) The policies advocated by different parties often do not match the preferences of respondents who identify with general political orientations typically associated with these parties. This may be a sign that currently, public preferences for ground‐mounted PV installations are still poorly understood. Policy makers must act quickly and ensure local benefits to prevent opposition.

title: Decoupling additive manufacturing from virgin resource consumption through recyclable bio-composites
summary: Additive manufacturing could support decentralised, on-demand production, but it remains largely reliant on linear polymer systems that consume virgin resources and generate persistent waste. Here, we report a fully bio-derived composite pl
content: Additive manufacturing could support decentralised, on-demand production, but it remains largely reliant on linear polymer systems that consume virgin resources and generate persistent waste. Here, we report a fully bio-derived composite platform for closed-loop additive manufacturing based on dynamic lipoic acid networks and renewable fillers. Printable inks containing hydroxyapatite or thiol-functionalized silica were processed by direct ink writing to produce robust three-dimensional structures. Unlike most sustainable 3D-printing strategies, which depend on biodegradation or downcycling through mechanical reprocessing, our lipoate matrix enables printed objects to be thermally recycled directly back into their original printable ink. This allows repeated cycles of fabrication, use, recovery and re-fabrication with minimal losses in printability, material recovery and mechanical performance. Life-cycle assessment shows that this circular materials design reduces impacts on human health, ecosystem quality and resource use, establishing a pathway to circular additive manufacturing that retains material value across multiple life cycles.

title: Carbon fetishism: towards a libidinal economy of net-zero capitalism
summary: This article argues that political-economic analyses of climate change in terms of economically rational incentives, governance mechanisms, and the structural contradictions of capitalism overlook the constitutive irrationalities of economi
content: This article argues that political-economic analyses of climate change in terms of economically rational incentives, governance mechanisms, and the structural contradictions of capitalism overlook the constitutive irrationalities of economic behaviours. Drawing on the Global Libidinal Economy perspective, the paper outlines and develops the concept of ‘carbon fetishism’ to account for these dynamics. Our approach to fetishism is informed by Lacanian psychoanalysis, which complements the structural grammar of critical IPE with a subjective grammar that maps libidinal investments to economic investments. This develops the concept of fetishism beyond a Marxist account of commodity fetishism, emphasising commodification and production, to consider the libidinal aspects of fetishism and fantasy that animate debates over carbon, and its absence as ‘net-zero’. Combining these analyses, we argue that classically Marxist strategies of defetishisation are inadequate to addressing the lived realities of climate change, proposing a qualitative form of re-fetishisation instead: returning to anthropological and animist fetishisms of the natural world as a way to reimagine human/ecology relationships that might resist the dominant, quantitative fetishisms of CO2 equivalents that dominate political economic climate change imaginaries.

title: Advancing urban solar integration: Performance and policy analysis of BIPV systems in India
summary: : Sustainable urban energy generation is an attractive goal with a growing solution: building integrated photovoltaic system. By combining the functions of a building envelope with those of a photovoltaic system in a single construction, bu
content: : Sustainable urban energy generation is an attractive goal with a growing solution: building integrated photovoltaic system. By combining the functions of a building envelope with those of a photovoltaic system in a single construction, building integrated photovoltaic systems simultaneously serve as a building component and an energy generation system. India has a high potential for building integrated photovoltaic applications in massive scales due to the extensive urbanization and ambitious targets set by the Indian government for renewable energy. This analysis offers a thorough evaluation of building integrated photovoltaic performance, architectural integration, and policy aspects in India through a systematic review approach, drawing on the PRISMA framework. The studies and projects related to the scope of the research were found by searching through databases such as Scopus, Web of Science, Science Direct, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, and technical reports through predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. The novelty of this study is that it has an analytical framework is India-specific, and merges the aspects of architectural design, technical performance, operational challenges, policy analysis, and comparative evaluation of real-world case studies of building integrated photovoltaic systems. The study clearly differentiates building integrated photovoltaic systems from building applied photovoltaic systems to avoid conceptual ambiguity, unlike previous studies. The case studies analyzed in this study showed that annual energy production of over 89,000 kWh/year and average annual energy yields of nearly 1460 kWh/kWp could be achieved. Semitransparent glazing solutions, bifacial modules, roof mounted photovoltaic tiles and façade mounted solutions were proposed as the solutions for urban application. The study also addresses some challenges such as partial shading, thermal degradation, complexity, maintenance requirements, and lack of policies for building integrated photovoltaic in India.

title: Overcoming gelling agent-derived inhibitory factors enables the cultivation of fastidious nitrifiers on solid media
summary: Abstract Nitrification is a key process in the global nitrogen cycle, yet the physiological characterization of nitrifiers remains limited due to their low culturability. Although culture-independent approaches have provided important ecolo
content: Abstract Nitrification is a key process in the global nitrogen cycle, yet the physiological characterization of nitrifiers remains limited due to their low culturability. Although culture-independent approaches have provided important ecological insights, they do not fully resolve the physiological properties of nitrifying microorganisms. Here, we show that common gelling agents (agar, agarose, and gellan gum) contain toxic substances that inhibit the growth of diverse nitrifying microorganisms as well as some heterotrophic bacteria. These inhibitory substances appear to be generated during autoclaving and act via mechanisms distinct from previously reported hydrogen peroxide. Removal of these inhibitory factors using a simple washing strategy enables colony formation in recalcitrant nitrifiers, including Nitrososphaera (ammonia-oxidizing archaea) and Nitrospira (nitrite-oxidizing bacteria). Application of this approach to environmental samples enabled the isolation of multiple difficult-to-culture nitrifying strains, including ammonia-oxidizing and nitrite-oxidizing microorganisms. Together, these findings demonstrate that the limited culturability of nitrifiers on solid medium is largely driven by gelling agent-derived inhibitory substances and can be overcome by a simple and broadly applicable strategy.

title: How Do FDI and Population Affect Carbon Emissions in Indonesia: An ARDL Approach
summary: Indonesia is challenged to balance as income rises, population expands, and foreign direct investments grow, there is a tension between economic progress and reducing carbon emissions. This study examines both the immediate and extended con
content: Indonesia is challenged to balance as income rises, population expands, and foreign direct investments grow, there is a tension between economic progress and reducing carbon emissions. This study examines both the immediate and extended connections between GDP per capita and carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions, population, and foreign direct investments (FDI) in Indonesia using annual data spanning 1989 to 2023, resulting in 34 observations. The study uses the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) approach in estimating the dynamic relationships between the variables. Augmented Dickey-Fuller with the bounds test confirming the establishment of long-run cointegration. The findings of the ARDL (1, 1, 0, 0) model revealed that GDP per capita and population exert substantial and beneficial effects on CO₂ emissions over both immediate and extended timeframes. On the other hand, foreign direct investment, after being transformed through inverse hyperbolic sine, has a negative and significant impact on CO₂ emissions both in the short- and long-run periods. An adjustment coefficient of -0.818 means that about 81.8 percent of the short-run imbalance is corrected in one period. Robustness analysis estimates retain the nature of the long-run coefficients.

title: Preliminary site selection for floating offshore wind farm using multi-method GIS-MCDM: A Malaysia exclusive economic zone case study
summary: Preliminary site selection for Floating Offshore Wind farm in Malaysia is favourable for renewable energy. This study includes a literature review and GIS-MCDM analysis of Malaysia's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ). The literature review foll
content: Preliminary site selection for Floating Offshore Wind farm in Malaysia is favourable for renewable energy. This study includes a literature review and GIS-MCDM analysis of Malaysia's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ). The literature review follows a PRISMA-guided methodology to examine research trends, criteria families, GIS-MCDM frameworks, and robustness approaches. Subsequently, a multi-method GIS-MCDM workflow is established from literature findings and applied to Malaysia’s EEZ using 20 years of ERA5 wind and wave data. A wind filter across the EEZ determines optimal corridors near Sabah and evaluates suitability on a harmonized grid. Seven key selection factors, such as wind power density and bathymetry, are assessed after removing critical constraints like extreme values and protected areas. Robustness is analysed through subjective and objective weighting methods (AHP and CRITIC), along with three ranking techniques (TOPSIS, VIKOR, PROMETHEE II), yielding six suitability surfaces. An aggregated suitability surface is calculated using the geometric mean of these surfaces. High-suitability zones are mainly found in the northern Sabah corridor, highlighting a robust candidate area of about 6,458 km² near Kudat. An indicative annual energy estimate from the final surface suggests substantial preliminary energy projections. These results serve as initial analyses requiring enhancement with higher-resolution, site-specific datasets in subsequent research.

title: Lanthanum-modified SBA-15 as a robust catalyst for renewable hydrocarbon production from vegetable oil
summary: The transition to renewable energy systems requires efficient catalysts for the production of drop-in hydrocarbons from triglyceride feedstocks. In this study, ordered mesoporous La-SBA-15 materials with Si/La molar ratios of 20, 40, and 10
content: The transition to renewable energy systems requires efficient catalysts for the production of drop-in hydrocarbons from triglyceride feedstocks. In this study, ordered mesoporous La-SBA-15 materials with Si/La molar ratios of 20, 40, and 100 were synthesized by a two-step pH-adjusted hydrothermal route and evaluated for crude soybean oil hydroprocessing in a fixed-bed reactor at 450 °C under H 2 flow. Physicochemical characterization by small-angle and wide-angle XRD, N 2 physisorption, FTIR, SEM, TEM, AAS, and NH 3 -TPD showed that lanthanum incorporation preserved the ordered SBA-15 mesostructure, maintained high surface area and mesoporosity, and modified the acidity of the catalysts. Among the evaluated catalysts, La 20 SBA-15 exhibited the best catalytic performance, achieving complete conversion after 30 min and maintaining high selectivity toward C 5 –C 18 hydrocarbons throughout the reaction.
