Governance quality does not significantly moderate the transition–resilience relationship. The findings suggest that climate-related transition exposure operates through country-specific structural channels rather than through a simple vulnerability mechanism.

title: National-scale PM2.5 health consequences of a proposed LNG power project in South Korea: Looking beyond localized assessment boundaries
summary: Abstract Environmental impact assessments (EIAs) in South Korea rely primarily on localized dispersion models within restricted geographical boundaries (~10 km), which may not adequately capture regional secondary PM2.5 formation and broad
content: Abstract Environmental impact assessments (EIAs) in South Korea rely primarily on localized dispersion models within restricted geographical boundaries (~10 km), which may not adequately capture regional secondary PM2.5 formation and broad population exposure. To address these limitations, this study pursues two distinct objectives: (1) evaluating potential limitations in the current EIA framework, and (2) quantifying the nationwide health impacts and monetized mortality damages under cumulative emissions scenarios including a proposed 3 GW LNG power cluster at the Yongin Semiconductor Industrial Complex. We employed Global InMAP—selected to examine regional atmospheric transport and secondary PM2.5 formation beyond the spatial scope typically addressed by local dispersion models—under 35%, 55%, and 75% capacity factor (CF) scenarios. Health outcomes were modeled nationwide and monetized using domestic and international Values of a Statistical Life (VSL). The modeled development scenarios were associated with 21.5–31.1 additional annual premature deaths nationwide, with secondary PM2.5 driving 63–71% of the cumulative burden. These estimates reflect the combined emissions of the proposed plants and surrounding sources and are not attributable to the plants alone. Under the central 55% CF scenario, annual monetized mortality damages range from 40.6 billion KRW (~USD 23 million; domestic benchmark) to 231.6–247.9 billion KRW (~USD 157–168 million; international benchmarks). Spatial disaggregation revealed potential regulatory blind spots: only 14–16% of attributable premature deaths occur within the typical 10 km EIA assessment radius, while 67–69% fall outside Yongin City and 46–47% outside host Gyeonggi Province. Geographically bounded EIAs may overlook these broader health externalities; the findings highlight the need to account for regional secondary PM2.5 formation and population exposure in environmental assessment and to transparently monetize health damages in energy planning decisions.

title: An Ecolinguistic Analysis of Ideological Framing of Forest City in Indonesian Digital Media: Media Discourse Dynamics and Public Perception
source: Theory and Practice in Language Studies
summary: Sustainable development is the central paradigm in modern urban planning, exemplified by the Nusantara Capital City in Indonesia, which incorporates the forest city concept that combines green technology and ecological sustainability. Howev
content: Sustainable development is the central paradigm in modern urban planning, exemplified by the Nusantara Capital City in Indonesia, which incorporates the forest city concept that combines green technology and ecological sustainability. However, the ideological representation of this concept in digital media remains a relatively understudied area. This study examines how Indonesia’s digital media portrays forest cities in the context of IKN's development. It employs an ecolinguistic approach that combines mixed-methods analysis, including critical discourse analysis of news from five national media outlets and public surveys using the Likert scale. The results of this study show that media supporting government policies use positive word choices, such as "sustainable forest cities," "conservation," "smart forest cities," and "green energy." In contrast, media opposing government policies use specific terms to describe ecological impacts, including "deforestation," "climate change," and "social conflicts." The choice of the lexicon in news writing reflects the ideology of each media outlet. The results of the public survey indicated that the development of the IKN will positively impact economic development and social welfare; however, environmental concerns remain. This research contributes to the expansion of ecolinguistic studies and the development of government communication strategies.

title: Perspectives on scaling up clean energy technologies in the energy transition
summary: Carbon neutrality requires massive, rapid scaling up of clean energy technologies, with economic factors playing a central role in market uptake. We investigate how economic drivers and investment behaviors affect technology growth using a
content: Carbon neutrality requires massive, rapid scaling up of clean energy technologies, with economic factors playing a central role in market uptake. We investigate how economic drivers and investment behaviors affect technology growth using a novel, multi-model analytical framework. By combining macro-level cost-driven technology diffusion with micro-level business profitability modeling, this framework captures realistic, investment-centric decision-making. Cost-competitiveness-dependent, varying technology adoption rates realistically reflect market growth and saturation, indicating a declining adoption rate as market share increases. Growth is initially influenced by technical and technoeconomic factors, but shifts toward complex systemic, social, and socioeconomic factors around the inflection point (halfway to saturation). This transition triggers, for instance, when solar PV share reaches around 20% of global electricity. At higher market shares, cost-competitiveness encompasses both basic technology costs and system-level limitations, better captured by the value-adjusted levelized cost of electricity than pure cost. Furthermore, micro-level profitability analysis underlines that sustained scaling up requires adequate business margins and profits. Growth can be accelerated through higher sales margins, reinvesting more profits into investments, reducing the time cash is tied up in sales, etc. Public support speeds up market entry but risks creating unhealthy competition and oversupply if sustained too long. Future technologies benefit from policies supporting a shorter development phase followed by rapid adoption. Finally, insights for future scaling up emphasize low costs, profitability, granularity, modularity, system flexibility, learning and scale effects, and technology-push versus market-pull trade-off. This multitude of factors stresses an integrated, multidisciplinary systems view to accelerate scaling up of clean energy.

title: Security evaluation and coupling coordination of the water–energy–food–carbon system in Northeast China
summary: Summary In China’s push towards peak carbon and carbon neutrality targets, the coordinated, secure and sustainable development of water resources, energy, food and carbon is of vital importance. To analyse the current security status and de
content: Summary In China’s push towards peak carbon and carbon neutrality targets, the coordinated, secure and sustainable development of water resources, energy, food and carbon is of vital importance. To analyse the current security status and degree of coupling coordination in the water–energy–food–carbon (WEFC) coupling system in Northeast China, this paper constructs an indicator system to evaluate the security level and changes over 2013–2022 of the system by integrating an entropy approach, a coupling coordination mechanism and a comprehensive safety evaluation model. The coupling coordination degree of the WEFC system is also predicted for the period 2023–2030 using a long short-term memory model. The analysis demonstrates that the comprehensive security status of the WEFC system in Northeast China remained relatively low from 2013 to 2022, with the subsystem of water resources exerting the most pronounced influence. The security evaluation indices of the energy and carbon subsystems showed steady growth, while those of the water resources and food subsystems experienced fluctuating growth. The coupling coordination degree underwent minor fluctuations due to policy interventions and climatic impacts but revealed a gradually improving trajectory. Influenced by resource endowments, the northern and southern regions of Northeast China displayed more disharmony than the central region (Jilin > Liaoning > Heilongjiang) in terms of coordination levels. The coupling coordination degree is expected to continue to increase and progress towards a high-level coordination state by 2030.

title: ElectriQ: LLM dialogue benchmark for electric power marketing in renewable-integrated power systems
summary: As power systems decarbonise and digitalise, electric power marketing (EPM) is becoming a key interface between regulation, system operation and sustainable-energy deployment. However, many utilities still rely on human agents and rule-base
content: As power systems decarbonise and digitalise, electric power marketing (EPM) is becoming a key interface between regulation, system operation and sustainable-energy deployment. However, many utilities still rely on human agents and rule-based chatbots with fragmented knowledge bases, which struggle with long, cross-scenario dialogues and often fail to provide compliant and verifiable responses. Although large language models (LLMs) show strong conversational ability, existing benchmarks underrepresent the sector-specific terminology, regulatory reasoning and multi-turn stability required in EPM. To address this gap, we present ElectriQ, a large-scale benchmark for LLM evaluation in EPM. ElectriQ contains over 550k multi-turn dialogues across six service domains and 24 sub-scenarios, and defines a unified evaluation protocol combining human ratings, automatic metrics, and two dedicated stress tests: Statutory Citation Correctness (SCC) and Long-Dialogue Consistency (LDC). For reproducible comparison, we further implement SEEK-RAG as a reference baseline to support evidence-grounded responses on ElectriQ. Experiments on 13 LLMs show that domain-aligned 7B models can match or surpass much larger models at lower computational cost, providing an auditable basis for deploying LLM-based EPM assistants in demand-side management, renewable integration and resilient grid operation.

title: A Strategic Governance Perspective on Carbon Accounting Enablers: An In‐Depth Qualitative Examination of Business Strategies
summary: ABSTRACT This study advances a governance perspective on how firms implement, adopt, and routinize carbon accounting. Although prior research has identified several carbon accounting drivers and enablers, less is known about how these eleme
content: ABSTRACT This study advances a governance perspective on how firms implement, adopt, and routinize carbon accounting. Although prior research has identified several carbon accounting drivers and enablers, less is known about how these elements interact at the firm level to support the organizational embedding of carbon accounting. Drawing on a qualitative analysis of essay‐based responses from 44 industry experts, this study identifies four interconnected dimensions of carbon accounting enablement, specifically carbon governance, structural sustenance, technological and operational transformation, and external persuasion. This study argues that external institutional pressures are important but insufficient to explain the organizational uptake of carbon accounting. Rather, these pressures become consequential when governance arrangements translate them into capabilities, routines, data infrastructures, and accountability mechanisms. The findings reveal that carbon accounting should not be treated just as a measurement or reporting practice but should be understood as a socio‐technical accountability infrastructure connecting emissions measurement, governance oversight, operational decision‐making, and stakeholder‐oriented legitimacy. The originality of this study lies in shifting attention from isolated enablers to the relational and iterative mechanisms through which carbon accounting is perceived to become embedded at the firm level under conditions of technological friction, supplier dependence, Scope 3 data uncertainty, and assurance pressure. This study contributes to theory by developing an interpretive framework of carbon accounting enablement, to practice by clarifying the governance and capability conditions required for routinization, and to policy by highlighting why regulatory pressure needs to be supported by organizational and assurance infrastructures.

title: The green dividend of the digital economy: how information consumption reduces urban carbon emission intensity
summary: This paper investigates the environmental impact of the National Information Consumption Pilot Policy (NICPP), a key Chinese initiative promoting digital economic activities. Using the policy as a quasi-natural experiment, we examine its ef
content: This paper investigates the environmental impact of the National Information Consumption Pilot Policy (NICPP), a key Chinese initiative promoting digital economic activities. Using the policy as a quasi-natural experiment, we examine its effect on urban carbon emission intensity (CEI) with a difference-in-differences (DID) model based on a panel dataset of 268 prefecture-level cities in China from 2008 to 2023. The empirical findings indicate that the NICPP significantly lowers urban CEI, and this conclusion is supported by a series of robustness checks. Mechanism analysis suggests that service sector upgrading and green technological innovation are two channels through which information consumption reduces urban CEI, while logistics efficiency strengthens the policy effect by reducing the additional distribution-related emissions generated by the expansion of online consumption. Heterogeneity analysis further shows that the CEI-reducing effect is more pronounced in cities with more advanced digital infrastructure, higher levels of financial development, and cleaner energy consumption structures. This study provides quasi-experimental evidence on the green dividend of information consumption policies and offers policy implications for aligning digital development with urban low-carbon transition.

title: Long-term climatic and management drivers of cropland gross primary production (GPP) from eddy covariance explained by interpretable machine learning
summary: Abstract. Understanding the long-term response of cropland gross primary production (GPP) to climate variability remains limited, despite the key role of agricultural carbon fluxes in climate change mitigation. Here, we analyze two decades
content: Abstract. Understanding the long-term response of cropland gross primary production (GPP) to climate variability remains limited, despite the key role of agricultural carbon fluxes in climate change mitigation. Here, we analyze two decades of eddy covariance measurements from a Swiss cropland site to assess how climate and management influence GPP dynamics of three winter crops: wheat, barley, and rapeseed. Crop-specific growing seasons were characterized by fitting logistic functions to cumulative GPP as a function of growing degree days, allowing the extraction of phenological metrics and growth rates. In parallel, an eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model combined with SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) was used to identify the dominant climatic and management drivers of daily GPP and their temporal patterns. Air temperature and vapor pressure deficit exhibited significant increasing trends over the study period, consistent with ongoing climate change. However, no corresponding trends were detected during either actual or fixed winter growing season (October–July). Instead, significant warming and atmospheric drying were determined to occur during the post-harvest off-season (August–September). This shows that a crop rotation dominated by winter crops acts as a climate-smart strategy for the Oensingen site, enabling crops to escape intensifying peak summer heat and atmospheric dryness. Across crops, cumulative GPP trajectories and growth rates were largely similar. Winter wheat was the only crop showing a significant increase in maximum cumulative GPP over time, yet this increase was not reflected in grain yield, confirming that GPP is a poor predictor of harvested production. Machine-learning results identified incoming radiation, air temperature, and nitrogen fertilization as the dominant drivers of GPP, highlighting the importance of explicitly accounting for management variables in cropland carbon flux studies. Overall, the absence of strong crop-specific divergence and limiting responses suggests that the studied crops have not yet experienced climatically constraining conditions for carbon uptake. These findings emphasize the need for long-term, multi-site cropland observations that integrate management data to better assess crop-climate interactions under future climate change.

title: A Universal and Robust Protocol for Accurate Urea Quantification in Electrochemical C─N Coupling Systems
summary: ABSTRACT Electrochemical conversion of CO 2 and nitrate into urea offers a sustainable route for nitrogen fixation, yet the reliability of catalytic performance evaluation is frequently compromised by inaccurate product quantification. Curr
content: ABSTRACT Electrochemical conversion of CO 2 and nitrate into urea offers a sustainable route for nitrogen fixation, yet the reliability of catalytic performance evaluation is frequently compromised by inaccurate product quantification. Current detection methodologies are susceptible to severe interferences from electrolyte pH fluctuations, byproduct accumulation (e.g., NO 2 − , NH 3 ), and complex electrolyte factors. In this study, we systematically decouple the interference mechanisms affecting these mainstream detection methods, revealing that extreme pH conditions lead to significant quantitative deviations in urease‐based assays due to enzymatic denaturation. To overcome these limitations, we establish a comprehensive calibration strategy and a multi‐method synergistic detection protocol. This approach integrates targeted pH optimization with a logic‐guided selection of analytical techniques based on specific concentration ranges and impurity profiles. Validated using a BiOCl‐catalyzed urea synthesis system, this integrated protocol demonstrates exceptional accuracy, stability, and cross‐method consistency. By offering a standardized, high‐throughput‐compatible workflow for eliminating false positives and measurement errors, this work provides critical methodological support for the objective assessment of electrocatalytic urea synthesis.

title: Hourly Ozone Fields and Province-Level Crop Production Losses Under Sector-Specific Mitigation Scenarios Toward China's Clean Air and Carbon Neutrality Goals by 2060
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This dataset supports the study “Distributional and Equity Impacts of Sector-Specific Ozone Mitigation on Farmers’ Incomes Under China’s Clean Air and Carbon Neutrality Goals.” It includes hourly surface ozone fields at 0.25° × 0.25° resolu
content: This dataset supports the study “Distributional and Equity Impacts of Sector-Specific Ozone Mitigation on Farmers’ Incomes Under China’s Clean Air and Carbon Neutrality Goals.” It includes hourly surface ozone fields at 0.25° × 0.25° resolution (μg m⁻³) for the 2020 control scenario, five sector-specific 2060 mitigation scenarios, and a coordinated mitigation scenario. The 2020 control field was bias-corrected and downscaled using machine learning. For each mitigation scenario, the GCHP-simulated ozone concentration change relative to the control simulation was added to the machine-learning-corrected 2020 control field using a delta approach. The dataset also includes province- and crop-specific production losses for wheat, maize, and rice under each scenario, reported in Mt.

title: Key Features of Decarbonization in Russia’s Oil and Gas Companies in the Context of Northern and Arctic Resource Development
summary: The current economic and environmental agenda presents complex challenges for enterprises in the energy sector. In the context of simultaneous growth in global energy consumption, the continued dominance of fossil fuels in the energy mix, a
content: The current economic and environmental agenda presents complex challenges for enterprises in the energy sector. In the context of simultaneous growth in global energy consumption, the continued dominance of fossil fuels in the energy mix, and increasingly demanding international climate policy requirements, oil and gas companies are compelled to transition toward more sustainable operational models. One of the key directions of such transformation is decarbonization. This study aims to conceptualize decarbonization in relation to the specific characteristics of the Russian oil and gas sector. Four dominant approaches to interpreting this phenomenon are identified, and a refined definition is proposed, adapted to the operational conditions of oil and gas companies. Particular attention is paid to the specific features of the Russian oil and gas industry, including the concentration of production capacity in the Arctic region, which is highly sensitive to the consequences of climate changes. Based on empirical data from major Russian companies, current trends in greenhouse gas emissions reduction are analyzed, including instances of decreased decarbonization efficiency and, conversely, emission growth. The study systematizes the key internal and external factors influencing the choice of decarbonization strategies: the political and legal conditions, the structure and quality of the resource base, the degree of state participation, the geographical distribution of assets, and emission dynamics. It is revealed that there is a lack of unified targets or regulatory guidelines for emission reductions in the oil and gas industry, which leads to fragmentation in the strategies and variability in the selection of instruments for achieving carbon neutrality. As a result of the study, a conceptual vision of decarbonization for Russian oil and gas companies is developed, encompassing promising development directions and the specific nature of industry transformation under the conditions of Northern and Arctic resource development.

title: Future-proofing the plantation sector for wellbeing and welfare: Insights from PLACROSYM XXVI
summary: Although plantation crops occupy less than 5% of India’s cultivated area, they contribute approximately 10% to the agricultural GDP and 14% to agricultural exports, underscoring their strategic role in the national economy and rural livelih
content: Although plantation crops occupy less than 5% of India’s cultivated area, they contribute approximately 10% to the agricultural GDP and 14% to agricultural exports, underscoring their strategic role in the national economy and rural livelihoods. However, the sector faces escalating risks from climate change, biotic stresses, market volatility, and labor shortages. The 26th Plantation Crops Symposium (PLACROSYM XXVI) was organized at ICAR–CPCRI, Kasaragod, from 5–7 January 2026. The symposium convened scientists, policymakers, and industry stakeholders across seven technical sessions, four keynote addresses, and a high-level panel discussion titled “Plantation Crops Strategy for Viksit Bharat.” Deliberations identified critical research priorities, including the development of climate-resilient genotypes through marker-assisted selection, the scaling of tissue culture protocols, and the integration of AI and geospatial tools for precision agriculture. Keynote sessions highlighted the urgent need for government-backed regulatory mechanisms for biocontrol products and the potential of carbon trading within plantation ecosystems. A major policy recommendation emerged for establishing a unified institutional mechanism, such as a single Plantation Board, to foster inter-crop synergy and strategic branding. The symposium concluded that achieving the “Viksit Bharat @ 2047” vision requires a transition toward technology-driven, market-oriented, and carbon-smart production systems. Strategic focus must remain on mechanization to reduce drudgery, enhancement of farmer income through integrated multi-crop systems, and the exploration of high-value nutraceuticals. This roadmap serves as a blueprint for ensuring the long-term resilience and global competitiveness of India’s plantation sector.

title: Computing at Sea: Floating and Offshore Data Centres as a Pathway to Sustainable AI Infrastructure
summary: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence is transforming data centres into one of the world's fastest-growing sources of electricity demand. As AI systems scale in size and capability, the physical infrastructure supporting computatio
content: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence is transforming data centres into one of the world's fastest-growing sources of electricity demand. As AI systems scale in size and capability, the physical infrastructure supporting computation is approaching critical limits in energy availability, cooling capacity, land use, freshwater consumption, and carbon management. Conventional land-based data centres are increasingly constrained by urban land competition, grid congestion, environmental pressures, and lengthy permitting processes, raising fundamental questions about where future computing infrastructure can sustainably exist. This article examines floating and offshore data centres as an emerging alternative model for digital infrastructure. By relocating computation to marine environments, offshore systems can exploit the ocean's natural cooling capacity, reduce freshwater dependence, and enable direct integration with offshore renewable energy resources such as wind, wave, and tidal power. Early deployments have demonstrated the potential for significantly improved energy efficiency and operational reliability compared with conventional facilities, while also opening new possibilities for distributed and resilient computing architectures. The article explores how offshore computing may reshape the future relationship between electrification, renewable energy, and large-scale AI infrastructure. It analyses the opportunities and trade-offs associated with marine deployment, including environmental impacts, engineering design challenges, economic feasibility, and regulatory governance. Rather than treating offshore data centres as experimental novelties, the article presents them as part of a broader systems-level transition in how society may power, cool, and sustain the next generation of computational growth.

title: Optimization of oilfield produced water treatment parameters using Agro-based adsorbents: A comprehensive review
source: International Journal of Chemical and Process Engineering Research
summary: Produced water from oil and gas extraction constitutes a major, complex waste stream demanding efficient, sustainable treatment solutions. Agro-based adsorbents derived from agricultural residues offer cost-effective, environmentally compat
content: Produced water from oil and gas extraction constitutes a major, complex waste stream demanding efficient, sustainable treatment solutions. Agro-based adsorbents derived from agricultural residues offer cost-effective, environmentally compatible alternatives due to their high porosity and functional surface chemistry. This review systematically synthesizes recent peer-reviewed studies to critically evaluate key optimization parameters affecting adsorption efficacy, including adsorbent dosage, contact time, pH, temperature, particle size, carbonization, chemical activation, and the use of single versus blended biomass systems. Findings reveal that chemically activated agro-based adsorbents achieve hydrocarbon removal efficiencies of up to 96%, markedly outperforming raw biomass, which typically attains 61–70%. Carbonization enhances adsorption capacity to approximately 90–93% by improving pore architecture and hydrophobicity. Optimal adsorption consistently occurs at near-neutral pH (6–8), with equilibrium reached within 60–120 minutes. Particle size reduction yields a 20–25% increase in removal efficiency, while elevated temperatures negatively impact adsorption due to exothermic behaviour. Blended biomass adsorbents demonstrate synergistic performance gains of 10–25% over single-source materials, though variability persists due to the absence of standardized optimization protocols. The review identifies a critical gap in integrated multi-parameter optimization frameworks, limiting the translation of laboratory-scale successes to industrial applications. It advocates for future research emphasizing coupled parameter modelling, continuous-flow system validation, and comprehensive techno-economic analyses to enable scalable, robust agro-based produced water treatment technologies. This work advances the field by providing a holistic, optimization-driven perspective essential for developing sustainable, high-performance adsorption systems in petroleum wastewater management.

title: When nationalism meets environmentalism: an inverted U-curve linking national sentiment to carbon emission intensity through an institutional lens
summary: Against the backdrop of rising corporate carbon emissions, managerial attributes are garnering increasing scholarly scrutiny. Utilizing a panel dataset from China’s A-share market between 2010 and 2023, this paper employs an institutional t
content: Against the backdrop of rising corporate carbon emissions, managerial attributes are garnering increasing scholarly scrutiny. Utilizing a panel dataset from China’s A-share market between 2010 and 2023, this paper employs an institutional theory perspective to examine the relationship between national sentiment and carbon emission intensity. We reveal a significant inverted U-shaped relationship between national sentiment and carbon emission intensity. Meanwhile, we also find that market competition, emission reduction target constrains and environmental penalties positively moderate the relationship between national sentiment and carbon emission intensity. Moreover, corporate social responsibility and green investment act as significant mediating channels in this relationship. Furthermore, national sentiment significantly influences enterprises characterized by high pollution, low subsidies, or low R&D intensity, and its impact on green patent, encompassing both green invention and green utility models, still exhibits a significant inverted U-shaped relationship. We further analyzed the effect of macro-environmental changes on this inverted U-shaped relationship.

title: Hollow nanostructured rare-earth-containing high-entropy carbides: Facile electrochemical synthesis and effective electrocatalytic performance for hydrogen evolution
summary: Abstract High-entropy carbides (HECs) have attracted growing attention as promising noble-metal catalyst alternatives for the hydrogen evolution reaction. Nevertheless, the reported HEC nanocrystals remain confined to dense solid structures
content: Abstract High-entropy carbides (HECs) have attracted growing attention as promising noble-metal catalyst alternatives for the hydrogen evolution reaction. Nevertheless, the reported HEC nanocrystals remain confined to dense solid structures with metallic components limited to groups IVB-VIB. The first synthesis of hollow nanostructured high-entropy carbides (HfNbTaTiZr)C, (HfNbTaTiZrRE)C (RE=Gd, Ce, Y) and (HfNbTaTiZrCeY)C was achieved by a direct electroreduction process. Electrolysis was conducted at 3.1 V using a graphite anode and a cathode prepared from mixed oxides/carbon additive powders in molten CaCl2-NaCl at 800 °C. The effects of carbon sources on the microstructure of the product were systematically investigated. The results show that the microstructure of HECs can be easily tailored from solid to hollow particles by selecting different carbon sources. All as-synthesized HECs exhibit a single face-centered cubic phase and compositional homogeneity from the nanoscale to the microscale. It was found that the engineered hollow nanostructure, coupled with the incorporation of rare-earth elements, significantly enhanced electrocatalytic performance of HECs for hydrogen evolution in an alkaline electrolyte. Specifically, the HECs incorporated with dual rare-earth elements exhibited superior performance to those with a single element. Among them, (HfNbTaTiZrCeY)C demonstrates superior hydrogen evolution reaction performance with a low overpotential of 167 mV, a small Tafel slope of 58.8 mV·dec-1, and a low charge transfer resistance of 2.7 Ω. This work not only establishes a facile method for synthesizing various hollow rare-earth-containing high-entropy carbide nanoparticles, but also provides a novel strategy for the design of high-performance non-noble metal-based catalysts.

title: Adsorption and Mass Transport of Methane and Hydrogen in Nanoporous Carbon Membranes - Binary Mass Transport Experiments and Modeling
summary: Abstract This study investigates binary mass transport of methane (CH4) and hydrogen (H2) through carbon-based nanoporous membranes at elevated temperatures. Building upon previous single-component adsorption and permeation measurements, we
content: Abstract This study investigates binary mass transport of methane (CH4) and hydrogen (H2) through carbon-based nanoporous membranes at elevated temperatures. Building upon previous single-component adsorption and permeation measurements, we present new binary permeation experiments conducted up to 220 °C and develop a predictive transport model based on the Maxwell–Stefan (M–S) framework. Initial model predictions underestimated H2 flux, which were resolved by incorporating a confinement correction to account for slit pore geometry and a temperature-dependent scaling factor. These modifications significantly improved model accuracy and alignment with experimental data. The refined model was extrapolated to 500 °C and varying gas compositions to evaluate membrane selectivity under relevant process conditions, thus offering predictive capabilities for membrane-based separations applicable to hydrogen production and carbon utilization.

title: Impact of bundling and sequencing of measures in retrofit roadmaps with hybrid heat pump systems – A case study for a municipal non-residential building in Germany
summary: Achieving climate neutrality in the building sector necessitates a well-balanced mix, entailing measures that reduce the space heating demand and measures to decarbonize the heat supply system. In non-residential buildings, the space heatin
content: Achieving climate neutrality in the building sector necessitates a well-balanced mix, entailing measures that reduce the space heating demand and measures to decarbonize the heat supply system. In non-residential buildings, the space heating demand can be reduced through both renovation measures targeting the building envelope and heat recovery from the ventilation system. In order to avoid CO 2 emissions, the implementation of the entire set of retrofit measures should be aimed at, but is often not practically feasible due to financial and other constraints. This issue may be addressed with a hybrid heat pump system, wherein the existing, fossil-fueled boiler continues to be operated to cover the residual thermal load until other retrofit measures have reduced the space heating demand to a level that it can only be covered by the heat pump. The proposed approach combines a techno-economic assessment of retrofit measures with a detailed simulation of the hybrid heat pump system across different stages of implemented retrofit measures. The process of bundling and sequencing gives rise to a multitude of combinatorial permutations of possible retrofit roadmaps. To apply the methodology to a real building as a case study, realistic requirements and constraints are transferred into filters to obtain a manageable number of possible roadmaps as a basis for exemplary roadmaps as scenarios. Hence, this approach is suitable for a techno-economic assessment of adequate measure bundles that ensure the transformation to carbon-neutral buildings despite limited resources.

title: The comparison analysis of ancillary service market in new power system: policies, practices and inspirations for China
summary: In the context of the accelerated access of renewable energy to the power system, how to effectively encourage multiple flexible resources to participate in system regulation has become the core issue of building a new power system. The anc
content: In the context of the accelerated access of renewable energy to the power system, how to effectively encourage multiple flexible resources to participate in system regulation has become the core issue of building a new power system. The ancillary service market is the key mechanism to solve this problem. This paper systematically reviews the policy evolution path and current practice of China’s ancillary service market, and selects representative mature markets such as Germany, PJM, and Australia for in-depth comparison. It is found that China’s market has laid a good foundation for the systematic and forward-looking top-level design, but there is still a gap with the international advanced level in terms of product design refinement, price signal sensitivity, subject participation breadth, and cross-regional resource coordination. In the future, from the three dimensions of technical support, market mechanism, and policy standards, this paper puts forward a series of specific suggestions, such as improving market design, strengthening incentive compatibility, and promoting standard unification, to provide a reference for the construction of an efficient and stable ancillary service market system in line with China’s national conditions.

title: From houseplant exhibition to conservation platform: a replicable curatorial model using Platycerium at the Sejong National Arboretum
source: Sibbaldia The International Journal Of Botanic Garden Horticulture
summary: Companion plant culture – the keeping of plants as household companions – has expanded rapidly in the Republic of Korea, prompting botanic gardens and arboreta to reconsider how public enthusiasm for horticulture may be aligned with ex situ
content: Companion plant culture – the keeping of plants as household companions – has expanded rapidly in the Republic of Korea, prompting botanic gardens and arboreta to reconsider how public enthusiasm for horticulture may be aligned with ex situ conservation. This article presents a case study of a Platycerium initiative at the Sejong National Arboretum (SNA) that developed between 2024 and 2025 from a thematic exhibition into a conservation platform. In 2024, the special exhibition The Mysterious Flight of Bakjwi-ran (Staghorn Ferns) displayed over 100 individuals representing 70 Platycerium taxa, including all 18 recognised species, which were subsequently incorporated into SNA’s documented living collection. In 2025, SNA established a 90 m2 core Platycerium conservation zone within the 2,800 m2 Tropical Garden, complemented by installations across the conservatory to accommodate species-specific growth forms. Public programmes involving plant enthusiasts facilitated knowledge exchange, collaborative exhibition contributions and resource efficiencies. This transition demonstrates how exhibition-led initiatives can catalyse accession and collection development. The article proposes a four-stage curatorial model applicable to ornamental taxa where popularity intersects with ecological constraints.

title: FEASIBILITY AND POTENTIAL ASSESSMENT OF SOLAR ENERGY GENERATION IN RAMAIAH TECHNOLOGY CAMPUS (MSRUAS)
source: World Journal of Advanced Engineering Technology and Sciences
summary: This paper examines the feasibility of installing a solar photovoltaic (PV) system at the Ramaiah Technology Campus (RTC) to promote sustainable energy use. The study evaluates rooftop availability, energy consumption patterns, and the pote
content: This paper examines the feasibility of installing a solar photovoltaic (PV) system at the Ramaiah Technology Campus (RTC) to promote sustainable energy use. The study evaluates rooftop availability, energy consumption patterns, and the potential to reduce dependence on diesel generators and conventional electricity. M.S. Ramaiah University of Applied Sciences (MSRUAS) is a private university in Bengaluru, Karnataka, India, and the Faculty of Engineering and Technology (FET) is located within the Ramaiah Technology Campus (RTC) in Peenya, Bengaluru. Data from electricity bills, diesel usage, and power capacity were analyzed along with solar radiation data to determine the optimal system size. The FET campus includes four academic blocks and a girls’ hostel, offering a total rooftop area of 52,200 sq. ft., suitable for PV installation. With average solar irradiation of 5.3–5.6 kWh/m²/day, the system can support a capacity of 443.7 kW using 682 panels of 650 W each. The estimated annual energy generation is 8,09,752.5 kWh, resulting in savings of Rs. 36,43,886.25. The payback period is 6.0 years, reduced to 5.3 years with diesel savings, confirming technical viability and economic feasibility.

title: Rapid Adsorption−Desorption in Direct Air Capture Using 3D-Printed Amine Adsorbents with Electromagnetic Induction Heating
summary: Abstract Direct air capture (DAC) is a promising strategy to address climate change and achieve carbon neutrality goals. The development of an adsorbent material with a high capacity, low pressure drop, and short regeneration period is nece
content: Abstract Direct air capture (DAC) is a promising strategy to address climate change and achieve carbon neutrality goals. The development of an adsorbent material with a high capacity, low pressure drop, and short regeneration period is necessary for high-performance DAC. Here, we incorporated direct ink writing (DIW) for tetraethylenepentamine (TEPA)-loaded silica gel adsorbent preparation and induction heating techniques to enable a fast CO2 adsorption/desorption cycle for efficient CO2 capture. Fe3O4 and TEPA loadings and the drying methods were evaluated for adsorption/desorption performance. Under 430 ppm of CO2, the CO2 adsorption capacities reached 1.57 and 1.11 mmol/g for powdered silica gel and monolithic silica gel, respectively. The desorption process can be completed in ca. 25.5 min at 85 °C in magnetic induction swing adsorption (MISA), affording a saving of ca. 70% reduction of desorption time when compared to conventional heating. The addition of methyl cellulose was beneficial for adsorbent stability and structure strength enhancement. This work offers insights into high-throughput CO2 capture and demonstrates the feasibility of the MISA system for use with amine-loaded adsorbents for DAC.

title: Editorial: Advancing the just transition: navigating towards a sustainable future
summary: By content clustering the contributions, five categories emerge. The first concerns participatory governance and democratic engagement. Keywords such as "participation" and "decision-making" characterize this body of work. Kambo et al. [1]
content: By content clustering the contributions, five categories emerge. The first concerns participatory governance and democratic engagement. Keywords such as "participation" and "decision-making" characterize this body of work. Kambo et al. [1] demonstrate how a structured deliberative engagement process can bridge the gap between citizens, policymakers, and industry actors in shaping Australia's future energy and fuel systems. Using the "diamond of participatory decision-making" framework, their analysis reveals that while considerable alignment exists across cohorts on the broad direction of a lowcarbon future, divergences surface around the social and environmental justice dimensions of specific technology choices -including hydrogen and biogas -that require innovative governance mechanisms to navigate. Similarly, Kunlere and Shah [2] challenge the simplistic binaries that often dominate public debates on renewable energy. By introducing the PARO framework, which categorises public responses to energy injustice across a spectrum of positions that conventional "supporter versus opponent" dichotomies cannot capture, the authors provide a more granular analytical perspective for diagnosing and addressing public resistance to energy transitions. Both studies make clear that how decisions are made matters as much as what is decided -a lesson that is easy to articulate and difficult to institutionalise. They also draw attention to a persistent gap: the limited institutional capacity to convert participatory insights into actionable, binding policy commitments.A second category revolves around sustainable energy systems and socio-technical transitions, captured by the keywords "decarbonisation" and "infrastructure." Singh and Clough [3] critically interrogate the global bioenergy system, challenging the widespread assumption that bioenergy is inherently carbon-neutral or renewable. Through causal loop analysis, they demonstrate how current production regimes displace negative social and ecological impacts -including threats to food security, land use change, and biodiversity loss -from consumer to producer regions, making the globalised bioenergy economy fundamentally unjust as well as unsustainable. Complementing this critical systems perspective, Oduro and Taylor [4] draw on expert interviews from industry, academia, and policy to map the challenges facing energy networks in Great Britain during decarbonization. Their findings reveal broad agreement on electrification and decentralization, yet deep uncertainty about the future role of gaseous fuels, particularly hydrogen. The paper highlights a regulatory gap: existing structures may be too rigid and slow-moving to enable networks to drive -rather than impede -the net-zero transition. Soloviy et al. [5] further expand the debate by conceptualizing what they call the "triple transition," linking green, digital, and just transitions. Drawing on 28 real-world case examples and five distinct analytical pers

title: Knowledge-guided machine learning for predicting the carbon sequestration potential of natural forests in Heilongjiang Province
summary: Abstract Key message Integrating ecological process knowledge into machine learning substantially improves the robustness and extrapolation of forest carbon stock predictions. The knowledge-guided model maintained strong predictive performa
content: Abstract Key message Integrating ecological process knowledge into machine learning substantially improves the robustness and extrapolation of forest carbon stock predictions. The knowledge-guided model maintained strong predictive performance over 10–15-year horizons, when conventional machine-learning performance declined markedly, providing a promising framework for long-term forest carbon assessment under climate change. Context Accurate quantification of forest carbon stocks and their dynamics is essential for understanding ecosystem carbon sequestration potential. However, traditional machine learning models often exhibit limited extrapolation capability in long-term forest carbon predictions because they rely primarily on statistical relationships learned from historical observations and lack explicit representation of ecological processes. Aims This study aimed to develop a knowledge-guided machine learning (KGML) framework that integrates ecological process knowledge with data-driven algorithms to improve the accuracy, stability, and long-term generalization of forest carbon stock predictions. Methods The study focused on natural forests in Heilongjiang Province, China, defined as stands classified as having a natural origin in forest inventory records. Forest fixed plot observations from 1976 to 2015 were combined with historical and projected climate data and atmospheric CO 2 concentration data. The CO 2 fertilization effect was incorporated into an optimized forest carbon sequestration (FCS) process model, and its outputs and process-based constraints were subsequently integrated with machine learning algorithms to construct the KGML framework. Model performance was compared with that of standalone machine learning and process-based models across forest types and prediction horizons. Results Incorporating the CO 2 fertilization effect improved the predictive performance of the FCS model, increasing the coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) from approximately 0.85 to above 0.90. The KGML model consistently outperformed the standalone machine learning and process-based models across the evaluated forest types. Its advantage was particularly evident for prediction horizons of 10 years or longer, over which the performance of conventional machine learning models declined substantially. Scenario simulations indicated that natural forests in Heilongjiang Province had the greatest projected carbon sequestration potential under SSP126. Depending on model configuration and forest type, projected carbon stocks in 2060 ranged from 1371.37 ± 422.04 to 1442.38 ± 316.77 Tg. Conclusion Integrating ecological process knowledge with machine learning can improve the accuracy and long-term extrapolation capability of forest carbon stock predictions. The proposed KGML framework provides a potentially transferable approach for regional forest carbon assessment. Nevertheless, the projections remain subject to uncertainty arising from climate scenarios, proc

title: Carbon-Aware Offline Reinforcement Learning for Joint Inventory Replenishment and Transportation Scheduling in Multi-Echelon Supply Chains
source: Highlights in Business Economics and Management
summary: Joint replenishment and transportation decisions couple service, inventory, vehicle utilization, and carbon emissions over time. Offline reinforcement learning (RL) is attractive when operational logs exist but online exploration is unsafe;
content: Joint replenishment and transportation decisions couple service, inventory, vehicle utilization, and carbon emissions over time. Offline reinforcement learning (RL) is attractive when operational logs exist but online exploration is unsafe; however, distribution shift and cumulative carbon constraints make direct offline Q-learning unreliable. This paper proposes budget-conditioned carbon-aware conservative Q-learning (CA-CQL), a discrete-action offline method that combines a remaining-budget state, carbon-shaped conservative value learning, a learned behavior-support prior, a state-dependent carbon shadow price, and a pathwise carbon-feasibility screen. A reproducible supplier–distribution-center–three-retailer benchmark is constructed because public sales datasets lack synchronized replenishment actions, vehicle schedules, loads, and emissions. Transport emissions are calibrated with the official UK Government 2026 vehicle-kilometer conversion factors. Across five independently generated offline datasets and 250 evaluation episodes per policy, CA-CQL achieves an operating cost of 16,865 ± 404, emissions of 14,119 ± 57 kg CO₂e, a 92.18 ± 0.88% fill rate, and zero carbon-cap violations. Relative to a support-regularized CQL baseline, it reduces emissions by 110.8 kg and the violation rate by 13.6 percentage points, with a 1.36% cost increase and a 0.63-point fill-rate decrease. Ablations show that the behavior prior prevents severe under-replenishment and that the carbon screen is necessary for hard pathwise compliance. The results establish a transparent compliance–service trade-off rather than claiming universal dominance.

title: ISA: Institutional Standards Architecture
summary: The Institutional Standards Architecture (ISA) introduces an evidence-centric structural interoperability methodology designed to identify, classify, and analyze shared evidence requirements across governance, sustainability, disclosure, as
content: The Institutional Standards Architecture (ISA) introduces an evidence-centric structural interoperability methodology designed to identify, classify, and analyze shared evidence requirements across governance, sustainability, disclosure, assurance, procurement, finance, education, supply chain, and institutional participation environments. ISA begins with Evidence Requirements and Evidence Objects rather than framework comparison, disclosure crosswalks, taxonomy alignment, or standards harmonization. It defines structural interoperability as the ability of an Evidence Object to support multiple governance environments through shared Evidence Requirements while preserving the independence, authority, purpose, and interpretive sovereignty of each environment. The methodology does not create, harmonize, reinterpret, or replace external standards and does not determine materiality, compliance, assurance, certification, regulatory obligations, or legal outcomes. It provides a repeatable methodology through which shared evidence foundations may be identified and evidence compatibility may be analyzed across independent governance environments. Two representative Golden Mapping Examples, A01-1 Green Ticket and B01-1 Supplier Commitment Proof, illustrate the structural consistency of the Native Mapping Architecture across distinct activity domains. These examples are conceptual demonstrations rather than empirical validation.

title: Tracking Evolution of Reactive Species in Pellets During HyDR through combined X-ray and Neutron Imaging
summary: Steel production emits 3.6 Gtyr −1 of CO 2 , and the majority of these emissions come from a single step: ironmaking. Hydrogen-based direct reduction (HyDR) offers a lowemission alternative, producing H 2 O instead of CO 2 when operated wit
content: Steel production emits 3.6 Gtyr −1 of CO 2 , and the majority of these emissions come from a single step: ironmaking. Hydrogen-based direct reduction (HyDR) offers a lowemission alternative, producing H 2 O instead of CO 2 when operated with green H 2 . Though conceptualized in the 1930s, market adoption of HyDR remains limited due to reactor failures from sticking of iron-ore pellets. The sticking phenomenon is rooted in rate-limiting kinetics, where transport of reactive species competes with surface reaction to become the dominant process. We combine X-ray and neutron imaging to simultaneously resolve microscale pore network evolution and the spatial distribution of reactive species in two iron ore pellets, one non-fractured and one fractured, across three stages of reduction. We detect a consistent accumulation of hydrogenous species on the surface and interior of both pellets across all timepoints. Pellet pores > 10 2 µm, do not contribute to this accumulation, marking regions of efficient mass transport. Within the pellet interior, hydrogenous species are spotted in the pellet matrix and at pore boundaries. Isolated pore boundaries have up to 3× higher enrichment of hydrogenous species than the largest connected pore cluster, marking them as regions of poor mass transport. By quantifying permeability, diffusivity, and tortuosity, we show that improved bulk transport with reduction progress does not mitigate local trapping. Our findings connect hydrogenous species retention to pore network evolution and mass transport behavior. Insights from this study provide a basis for microstructural design strategies that could boost transport of reactive species and improve HyDR reactor performance.

title: Phosphoinositides protonation states dictate AKT1 binding with membrane
summary: Abstract Phosphoinositides are key regulators of membrane-associated signaling, yet their electrostatic properties are commonly represented by a single nominal charge in molecular simulations and structural models. Using the essential prote
content: Abstract Phosphoinositides are key regulators of membrane-associated signaling, yet their electrostatic properties are commonly represented by a single nominal charge in molecular simulations and structural models. Using the essential protein kinase AKT1 as a model system, we show that phosphoinositide protonation microstates, both the degree and positional placement of protons, govern peripheral membrane-protein recognition. By integrating quantum-mechanics-derived headgroup parameters, microsecond-scale all-atom molecular dynamics, and umbrella-sampling free-energy calculations with the available solid-state NMR-derived lipid populations via Bayesian/Maximum Entropy reweighting, we account explicitly for the thermodynamic ensemble of phosphoinositide protonation states. This population-weighted free-energy framework provides a quantitative mechanistic rationale for the strict specificity of wild-type AKT1 toward PI(3, 4, 5)P 3 and elucidates how the oncogenic sentry mutation (E17K) alters this specificity to enable high-affinity PIP 2 binding. Furthermore, Proximity-based Labeling of Membrane-Associated Proteins (PLiMAP) assays experimentally confirm that AKT1 pleckstrin homology domain binding to distinct phosphoinositide species is differentially sensitive to pH. Together, our findings establish a direct connection between phosphoinositide protonation equilibria, binding energetics, and AKT1 lipid specificity. Beyond AKT1, these results demonstrate that the dynamic protonation microstates of anionic phospholipids act as a functional regulatory layer governing peripheral membrane-protein recruitment across diverse cellular microenvironments. Significance Statement In physiological conditions, AKT1 protein is highly specific to PI(3,4,5)P 3 lipids and completely excludes PI(4,5)P 2 lipids. However, a single charge reversal (oncogenic) mutation of sentry glutamate (E17K) on the membrane adaptor Pleckstrin Homology domain of AKT1 enhances its PIP 2 binding remarkably. Our simulation data reveal that AKT1-PHD dissociation free-energies have remarkable variations with changes in lipid protonation state. By integrating our atomic simulation readouts with available ensemble-averaged low-resolution information from experiments using machine learning methods, we could explain the highly enhanced PIP 2 specificity for the pathological mutant. The work highlights the degenerate roles of secondary messenger lipids as a function of membrane environments.

title: Exploring slow-release plasma nitrogen nano-fertilizer for improved maize production and nutrient use efficiency
summary: The use of nitrogen (N) fertilizer in maize production is constrained by scarcity, low use efficiency, and high costs. Plasma technology presents a more environmentally friendly nitrogen source (PN). When incorporated into nanocellulose com
content: The use of nitrogen (N) fertilizer in maize production is constrained by scarcity, low use efficiency, and high costs. Plasma technology presents a more environmentally friendly nitrogen source (PN). When incorporated into nanocellulose composites to control fertilizer release (NPN), they improve N supply and mitigate environmental risks, thereby optimizing benefits. However, the productivity of NPN relative to urea and its nanoform (NU) remains unexplored. Screenhouse and field experiments were conducted twice on maize using five fertilizer treatments: control, urea, PN, NU, and NPN. All treatments were applied once at 66 kg N ha -1 and replicated four times. Maize cultivated in plots treated with nano-fertilizers showed increased plant height, chlorophyll content, and stem and leaf area. Similarly, maize yield components, including kernel row number, grains per row, and 100-seed weight, were enhanced by the application of nano-fertilizers. Compared to urea, NU and NPN increased the grain yield by 46-49% and 34-85%. Compared to PN, the increases were 8-53% and 36-37%, respectively. Nano-fertilizers boosted yield by 81-235% relative to the control. Furthermore, the Nitrogen Recovery Efficiency increased to 84% and 83% for NU and NPN, respectively, from 16-57% for urea and 10-50% for PN. The uptake affected plant utilization, causing higher Agronomical Efficiency in maize with nano-fertilizer application. The high performance of nano-fertilizers, once validated through economic and on-farm evaluations, suggests that urea and PN nanoencapsulation could enable a single application to meet all N requirements for maize production. These findings indicate that the use of nano-fertilizers can reduce nutrient loss, fertilizer requirements, and the associated environmental risks.

title: GRAPHENE-DERIVED BROADBAND PHOTODETECTORS FOR Si-COMPATIBLE OPTICAL SENSING APPLICATIONS
source: Suranaree Journal of Science and Technology
summary: Graphene and its derivatives, particularly reduced graphene oxide (rGO), have attracted significant attention for broadband photodetection owing to their unique optoelectronic properties, solution processability, and compatibility with sili
content: Graphene and its derivatives, particularly reduced graphene oxide (rGO), have attracted significant attention for broadband photodetection owing to their unique optoelectronic properties, solution processability, and compatibility with silicon (Si) platforms. The current paper reports the fabrication and characterization of rGO-based photodetectors designed for Si-compatible optical sensing applications. rGO was synthesized using a modified Hummers’ method and characterized via Raman spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) to confirm its structural integrity, reduction level, surface morphology, and thermal stability. The photodetectors exhibited a broad spectral response from the visible to near-infrared (NIR) region, with responsivity strongly dependent on the rGO layer thickness and applied bias voltage. The optimized devices demonstrated a peak responsivity of 0.5 A/W at 650 nm under a 5 V bias for a 3 μL rGO layer, with fast switching characteristics and reasonable stability. Lower concentrations (1-2 μL) exhibited reduced dark current and enhanced reliability, thus achieving a responsivity of up to 0.2 A/W. These devices function efficiently at low optical power levels (~30 μW) and low voltages, making them suitable for integration into energy-constrained environments and CMOS-based systems. The proposed rGO-based photodetectors offer a cost-effective and scalable solution for broadband low-power optical sensing, highlighting their potential in biomedical diagnostics, environmental monitoring, and silicon photonic circuits.

title: Applications and Innovations in Bioenergy From Waste Biomass
summary: The increasing demand for sustainable and low carbon energy sources has greatly led to the development and research on bioenergy derived from waste biomass. This paper explores recent advancements in biofuel production technologies and thei
content: The increasing demand for sustainable and low carbon energy sources has greatly led to the development and research on bioenergy derived from waste biomass. This paper explores recent advancements in biofuel production technologies and their integration into a circular bioeconomy framework. The study also discusses the role of integrated biorefineries as multifunctional systems for converting diverse biomass resources into fuels, chemicals, and value-added products. Furthermore, the integration of digitalization and artificial intelligence in bioenergy systems has enabled predictive modelling, process optimization, and smart monitoring for enhanced yield and reduced operational costs. The paper highlights the synergy between waste valorization, advanced technologies, and data-driven systems as the basis for resilient and circular bioenergy sector. All innovations collectively contribute to achieving global energy security, carbon neutrality, and sustainable waste management objectives.

title: A case study: Enhancing the efficiency of a resistive-based engine preheating system with heat pumps and photovoltaic generation in a powership
summary: To supplement renewable energy sources and ensure energy security for consumer centers, the Brazilian power system relies on thermal power plants that remain on standby until the National System Operator (ONS) issues a dispatch request. Thi
content: To supplement renewable energy sources and ensure energy security for consumer centers, the Brazilian power system relies on thermal power plants that remain on standby until the National System Operator (ONS) issues a dispatch request. This study considers a floating gas-fired thermal plant (powership) equipped with twelve 2 0 . 6 5 M W generator units. To meet the 30-minute dispatch tolerance, generator-driving engines must be maintained under pre-operational conditions, which is currently provided by a 1 . 6 2 M W resistive engine preheating system consuming up to 2 0 M W h / d a y . To improve energy efficiency, enhance the transient thermal response, and reduce the operating costs of the preheating system, this work proposes and evaluates three heat pump (HP)-based retrofit scenarios considering practical installation constraints of the powership, while assessing the photovoltaic (PV) generation potential of the available deck area as a complementary strategy. The application of HPs for this purpose has received little attention in the literature. The proposed configurations were evaluated through numerical simulations in MATLAB/Simulink and compared with the existing resistive system. The results show that the daily energy consumption of the engine preheating system was reduced by 7 0 . 4 - 8 0 . 0 % , and the time required to reach the engine standby temperature decreased from 2 ⁢ h ⁢ 5 1 ⁢ m i n to less than 1 ⁢ h ⁢ 0 3 ⁢ m i n , while energy balance and economic analyses indicated payback periods ranging from 3.2 to 8.1 years. The proposed retrofit scenarios demonstrate the feasibility of replacing M W -scale resistive engine preheating systems in thermal power plants with more energy-efficient HP-based systems, particularly when integrated with renewable energy sources.

title: A framework for evaluating the traceability of primary data elements for textile digital product passports
summary: Digital Product Passports (DPPs) require high-quality traceable product data across complex supply chains. However, existing approaches to traceability assessment predominantly emphasise data availability and enabling technologies but offer
content: Digital Product Passports (DPPs) require high-quality traceable product data across complex supply chains. However, existing approaches to traceability assessment predominantly emphasise data availability and enabling technologies but offer no methodology for systematically evaluating whether individual primary data elements (PDEs) can be reliably linked to the physical product characteristics they are intended to represent. This limitation constrains the ability of DPP systems to support downstream applications such as material sorting and recycling. For the first time, this study develops a set of indicators for product-level traceability by applying maturity model theory and information quality frameworks to develop a Traceability Degree Score (TDS). This framework conceptualises traceability as a graduated, multidimensional construct rooted in data standardisation, process automation, measurement reliability and blockchain readiness, each assessed on a five-point maturity scale. The framework was tested with a case study of a man-made cellulosic fibre (MMCF) textile composed of 80% renewable wood and 20% recycled textiles by evaluating 336 PDEs across 10 supply chain nodes. The results reveal that only 20% of the PDEs have high traceability (TDS = 5) with no or poor traceability (TDS 1--2), constituting 5% of PDEs concentrated in consumer-use and end-of-life stages. The framework also enables the comparison of nodes in the value chain on each of the four indicators and as single effective indicators of node level traceability. The study contributes a replicable diagnostic framework for assessing the effectiveness of product data systems in sustainability governance and resource management.

title: Cultivating future green chefs: students’ needs and competency levels in sustainable culinary creativity
summary: Introduction As the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals deadline approaches, food system transformation has become a global priority. Chefs play a key role in promoting sustainable consumption, yet culinary education should move beyond techn
content: Introduction As the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals deadline approaches, food system transformation has become a global priority. Chefs play a key role in promoting sustainable consumption, yet culinary education should move beyond technical training to strengthen students’ creative competencies for addressing sustainability challenges. Methods This study adopted a questionnaire survey method and targeted university students majoring in hospitality-related fields in Taiwan. A total of 650 questionnaires were distributed, and 619 valid questionnaires were collected, yielding a response rate of 95%. Importance–Performance Analysis (IPA) was employed to examine students’ self-perceived training needs and self-reported current competency levels across sustainable culinary creativity competency dimensions. Results This study identified nine professional competency dimensions: product, culture, sustainable resources and food management (SRFM), business and marketing techniques (BMT), service, aesthetics, creativity, sustainable culinary technology (SCT), and culinary technology application (CTA). The results showed that SRFM and BMT were the dimensions most in need of priority improvement, while product, culture, service, and aesthetics were identified as secondary improvement dimensions. Discussion By analyzing students’ sustainable culinary professional competencies, this study provides a reference for planning future hospitality training curricula, helps reduce the gap between education and industry practice, and supports the cultivation of sustainable culinary professionals with sustainability literacy, innovative capabilities, and social responsibility.

title: Economic integration and carbon rebalancing in China’s grain functional zones
summary: Achieving regionally coordinated and sustainable development has become an urgent global priority amid accelerating globalization and intensifying environmental challenges. In China, balancing agricultural carbon emission equity with region
content: Achieving regionally coordinated and sustainable development has become an urgent global priority amid accelerating globalization and intensifying environmental challenges. In China, balancing agricultural carbon emission equity with regional economic integration is essential for addressing environmental justice and promoting low-carbon transformation. This study employs the coupling coordination degree (CCD), space–time geographically weighted regression model (GTWR), and partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to reveal the multi-stage interactive response mechanisms between agricultural carbon emission equity and regional economic integration across China’s three major grain functional zones, from the perspectives of spatial heterogeneity and temporal non-stationarity. The results indicate that the major grain-producing zones (MGPZs) exhibit high ecological support but low production efficiency, while the major grain-consuming zones (MGCZs) maintain strong economic performance under ecological constraints, and the production-consumption balanced zones (PCBZs) have been fluctuating. There are significant differences in economic integration, with higher integration in MGPZs and MGCZs compared to lagging PCBZs. The coordination between equity and integration shows significant spatial and temporal variations, with only Jiangsu Province achieving high coordination. Moreover, key factors, including agricultural industrial structure, investment intensity, and pesticide application intensity, exert heterogeneous and sometimes conflicting effects on the carbon-economy coordination at different dimensions. These findings suggest that one-size-fits-all policies are inadequate. Instead, region-specific strategies that focus on ecological compensation, efficient input management, and interregional cooperation are essential. The study provides a theoretical basis for environmental impact assessments and the formulation of targeted policies that harmonize agricultural carbon mitigation with sustainable regional economic development.

title: Laboratory-scale development of hybrid micro-PEC–biovoltaic emergency power systems from organic waste
summary: The increasing demand for reliable and sustainable emergency power systems has driven interest in decentralised energy technologies capable of operating under variable and resource-limited conditions. In this study, a laboratory-scale hybri
content: The increasing demand for reliable and sustainable emergency power systems has driven interest in decentralised energy technologies capable of operating under variable and resource-limited conditions. In this study, a laboratory-scale hybrid Micro-photoelectrochemical (Micro-PEC)–Biovoltaic system powered by organic waste was developed and systematically evaluated for emergency energy applications. The hybrid system integrates a visible-light-responsive Fe₂O₃/BiVO₄ photoelectrode with a biovoltaic unit employing electrogenic bacteria and a proton exchange membrane. Electrical performance was assessed through repeated testing under varying organic waste concentrations, dynamic illumination, and load conditions. The hybrid configuration achieved an average voltage of approximately 0.41 V, an average current of 1.25 mA, and an average power output of 0.51 μW, outperforming standalone Micro-PEC and biovoltaic systems while exhibiting improved operational stability. Load variation tests revealed a well-defined maximum power point at ∼200 Ω, and the system showed rapid, reversible voltage and current responses to light interruption. Progressive improvements in emergency performance indicators, including availability, reliability, resilience, and cumulative energy delivery, were also observed. These results demonstrate that coupling photoelectrochemical and bioelectrochemical processes yields an operationally stable and adaptable energy platform. Overall, the proposed hybrid Micro-PEC–Biovoltaic system offers a low-complexity, environmentally sustainable approach for decentralised emergency power generation from organic waste, with promising potential for future scale-up and further practical feasibility investigation.

title: Carbon-aluminum price tango: Dynamic multi-paths amid climate-energy dual constraints
summary: This study investigates the dynamic connection between Chinese carbon prices (CAP) and electrolytic aluminum prices (EAP) from 2013: M08 to 2025: M09, using a rolling window causality test. CAP primarily impacts EAP through cost transmissio
content: This study investigates the dynamic connection between Chinese carbon prices (CAP) and electrolytic aluminum prices (EAP) from 2013: M08 to 2025: M09, using a rolling window causality test. CAP primarily impacts EAP through cost transmission and influencing market expectations, and EAP primarily influences CAP through production scale adjustments and substitution effects. These influences have positive and negative impacts in various time periods that reflect changing market operation circumstances. This study moves research attention from the macro metal market to the aluminum industry, providing a unique industry-related angle to understand the CAP–EAP connection that enriches the theoretical consideration of cross-market mutual actions with empirical evidence. By exposing the dual-direction features of diverse phases, the findings provide a practical reference for policymakers to coordinate steady industry growth and low-carbon transition.

title: Modeling demand flexibility in electrified supply chains: optimizing manufacturing and transport under carbon pricing
summary: Introduction This study presents a novel framework for leveraging temporal slack in end-to-end electrified logistics systems to enable medium- to long-duration load flexibility. Methods We formulate a coordinated optimization of energy-inte
content: Introduction This study presents a novel framework for leveraging temporal slack in end-to-end electrified logistics systems to enable medium- to long-duration load flexibility. Methods We formulate a coordinated optimization of energy-intensive manufacturing and freight transport within an electricity-dominant logistics network and evaluate it using a regional case study of clinker-based material distribution in the Eastern United States. Results The synchronized electrification of transport and production processes can facilitate multi-gigawatt-hour temporal load shifting aligned with stochastic wind power availability over timescales exceeding one week. This capability arises under relatively low marginal carbon pricing (below $50 per metric ton CO 2 ), while stationary energy storage remains economically unattractive. Discussion Parametric analyses show that the magnitude and nature of achievable flexibility are highly sensitive to system configuration. Under low-capital-cost truck scenarios, flexibility is predominantly transport-driven, whereas constrained vehicle investment shifts the flexibility locus toward manufacturing-buffer capacity. These findings highlight the pivotal role of electric freight vehicle cost structures in shaping the dynamic flexibility potential of electrified logistics systems.

title: Effect of support properties on product selectivity in aqueous-phase Fischer–Tropsch synthesis over Ru catalysts
summary: The effect of support properties on 5 wt% Ru catalysts was investigated during aqueous-phase Fischer–Tropsch synthesis (FTS) over H-ZSM-5, SiO 2 -Al 2 O 3 , ZrPO x , TiO 2 , ZrO 2 , and γ-Al 2 O 3 at 150 °C using a H 2 /CO ratio of 2 and an
content: The effect of support properties on 5 wt% Ru catalysts was investigated during aqueous-phase Fischer–Tropsch synthesis (FTS) over H-ZSM-5, SiO 2 -Al 2 O 3 , ZrPO x , TiO 2 , ZrO 2 , and γ-Al 2 O 3 at 150 °C using a H 2 /CO ratio of 2 and an initial pressure of 3.0 MPa. Ru/SiO 2 -Al 2 O 3 showed high activity (7.5 mol CO mol Ru −1 h −1 ) and the highest chain growth probabilities (α = 0.93) for both hydrocarbons and oxygenates. Product selectivity varied strongly with acid strength, with stronger acid sites suppressing oxygenate formation and shifting the product distribution toward hydrocarbons. Ru/H-ZSM-5 completely suppressed oxygenate formation in both aqueous and cyclohexane media and exhibited comparable normalized hydrocarbon formation rates, yielding 46.0% selectivity to jet-fuel-range paraffins (C 8 –C 16 ). Ru/H-ZSM-5 also showed the highest normalized CO consumption rate.
