These results demonstrate that support acid strength influences product selectivity in aqueous-phase FTS and enables selective synthesis of jet-fuel-range hydrocarbons over Ru catalysts.

title: Large constructed treatment wetlands for decentralized wastewater treatment: an integrated decision-support framework for design, operation, and governance
summary: Introduction Large treatment wetlands (TWs) can provide decentralized wastewater treatment at infrastructure scale, but successful implementation requires the integration of site conditions, wastewater characteristics, treatment-train desig
content: Introduction Large treatment wetlands (TWs) can provide decentralized wastewater treatment at infrastructure scale, but successful implementation requires the integration of site conditions, wastewater characteristics, treatment-train design, operation, financing, and governance across the project lifecycle. Methods We developed an integrated decision-support framework based on a structured qualitative evidence synthesis and a comparative assessment of 64 large-scale TW projects. Project-level data were extracted on location, wastewater source, inflow, population equivalent, wetland area and type, treatment train, vegetation, pretreatment, post-treatment, conventional pollutant removal, data limitations, and special design or operational features. Projects were grouped into 18 configuration categories. Evidence on emerging contaminants was synthesized separately at the compound-group level. Results Staged vertical-flow/horizontal-flow systems and pretreated vertical-flow systems showed strong removal performance for BOD 5 , COD, TSS/SS, nitrogen indicators, and total phosphorus when supported by adequate pretreatment, hydraulic distribution, monitoring, and operation and maintenance. Performance varied with influent strength, treatment objective, system configuration, pollutant-specific data availability, and evidence quality. Micropollutant attenuation was promising but compound-specific and depended on media selection, redox zoning, hydraulic retention time, vegetation, sorption capacity, and multi-barrier design. The resulting matrix links six framework dimensions to key decisions, indicators, red flags, planning outputs, readiness levels, and no-go risks. Discussion Large TWs should be planned as governable, adaptive, and multifunctional public infrastructure. The framework provides implementation-oriented support for early project screening, treatment-train selection, governance design, and long-term decentralized water management.

title: Using Visual Communication to Meet Legal Obligations: Municipal Public Websites in Lesser Poland and Air Pollution Information
source: International Journal for the Semiotics of Law - Revue internationale de Sémiotique juridique
summary: This article centers on how a set of informational obligations arising under EU ambient air quality protection law are implemented, putatively, via visual tools at the municipal level in one of Poland’s regions, namely Lesser Poland ( Małop
content: This article centers on how a set of informational obligations arising under EU ambient air quality protection law are implemented, putatively, via visual tools at the municipal level in one of Poland’s regions, namely Lesser Poland ( Małopolska ). Poland, a Member State of the EU since 2004, is a unitary state characterized by a well-developed three-tier self-government system. The country is divided into sixteen regions (precisely referred to as voivodeships), including Lesser Poland, which are further subdivided into counties and, at the lowest level, municipalities–public authorities with which residents interact most frequently.

title: Rooted Currents: Research-through-design for regenerative urbanism in Changzhou Island
source: Journal of Chinese Architecture and Urbanism
summary: Changzhou Island in Guangzhou’s Pearl River Delta represents a site of both cultural significance and environmental vulnerability, facing increasing pressures from flooding, rapid urbanization, and the erosion of Lingnan architectural herit
content: Changzhou Island in Guangzhou’s Pearl River Delta represents a site of both cultural significance and environmental vulnerability, facing increasing pressures from flooding, rapid urbanization, and the erosion of Lingnan architectural heritage. This article reframes the award-winning design proposal of the student competition Rooted Currents as a research-through-design (RTD) inquiry into regenerative urbanism in deltaic environments. The study develops a multi-scalar framework integrating landform modification, transit-oriented development, and distributed water–energy–nutrient systems, informed by heritage-based spatial strategies. Scenario-based modeling and literature-benchmarked estimations indicate that land elevation, ecological water management, and decentralized infrastructure can significantly reduce flood exposure and enhance resource self-sufficiency. At the architectural scale, reinterpreting Lingnan typologies, such as cold alleys and courtyard systems, demonstrates their continued relevance as performative climatic and social infrastructures. The findings are synthesized into three transferable principles: landform as infrastructure, heritage as anchor, and distributed systems of resilience. The article contributes by demonstrating how RTD can generate transferable knowledge for urban resilience in heritage-rich delta regions. While the results remain scenario-based, the study provides a framework applicable to rapidly transforming waterfront cities in China and beyond.

title: Editorial: Global responses of marine ecosystems to extreme environmental changes: marine and coastal environments under extreme stress, volume II
summary: Marine and coastal environments are shaped by processes operating across a wide range of spatial and temporal scales. Local pollution and coastal development interact with seasonal environmental variability, while regional climate modes and
content: Marine and coastal environments are shaped by processes operating across a wide range of spatial and temporal scales. Local pollution and coastal development interact with seasonal environmental variability, while regional climate modes and remote atmospheric forcing can influence conditions thousands of kilometers from their origin. As climate change intensifies environmental extremes and human pressures continue to expand along coastlines, understanding ecosystem change increasingly depends on our ability to observe and interpret these interacting processes, distinguish long-term trends from natural variability, and connect physical forcing with ecosystem responses.The first volume of this Research Topic highlighted the diversity of pressures affecting marine and coastal environments, including extreme precipitation, altered coastal hydrology, hurricanes, marine heatwaves, coral bleaching, and contamination associated with urban development (Cavalcante et al., 2023). It also emphasized the importance of multidisciplinary approaches and technological advances for understanding ecosystem responses to extreme stress. Volume II extends this perspective through four studies spanning the China Seas (South China Sea, East China Sea, and Yellow Sea), the Persian/Arabian Gulf, and the eastern South Pacific. These regions are among the most dynamic and sensitive to global change; particularly the China Seas, which harbor substantial biological carbon pump potential and play a critical role in achieving national "carbon peaking and carbon neutrality" goals. Although these studies address different processes and use distinct methodological approaches, they share a common challenge: detecting and analyzing environmental change at the appropriate spatial and temporal scales.One of the fundamental challenges in assessing environmental change is establishing reliable historical baselines. This is particularly important for sea-level change, where long-term observations remain spatially uneven and different reconstruction approaches may represent regional variability differently. Zhang et al. compared Ocean Data Assimilations and Tide Gauge Reconstructions with tide-gauge records and satellite altimetry across the China Seas. Their results show that no single product class performs best across all aspects of sea-level variability. Ocean Data Assimilations generally show stronger correlations with observations in nearshore areas and with satellite altimetry, whereas Tide Gauge Reconstructions better represented some aspects of open-ocean variability. Both approaches, however, show limitations, including underestimation of variability and differences in estimated rates of sea-level rise.The implications extend beyond the choice of a particular sea-level product. Environmental assessments and adaptation strategies depend on the quality of the underlying data, but the performance of global datasets can vary substantially among regions. title: The challenge of supplying critical raw materials
summary: Guaranteeing a secure, steady, and diversified supply of critical raw materials (CRM) has become a global policy priority. CRM supply is subject to different risks, which endanger the continuity of industrial activities. Understanding and a
content: Guaranteeing a secure, steady, and diversified supply of critical raw materials (CRM) has become a global policy priority. CRM supply is subject to different risks, which endanger the continuity of industrial activities. Understanding and anticipating CRM supply chain disruptions and risks may minimise their effects. To reduce the impacts of CRM supply risks, adopting different types of strategies is necessary. These strategies can be classified into seven groups: (i) innovation; (ii) advanced manufacturing; (iii) reuse and recycling; (iv) domestic mining and metallurgy; (v) purchasing and other company actions; (vi) national strategies and planning; and (vii) cooperation. Each strategy has advantages and disadvantages, and some must also overcome a number of challenges. No single CRM supply chain risk mitigation strategy can eliminate all CRM risks on its own. The strategies should be tailored to each specific situation mainly because each territory/company differs in its strategic foci. There is not, therefore, a one-size-fits-all solution. Strategies are interconnected, and sometimes, the disadvantages of one strategy are countered by the benefits of other additional strategies. Additionally, governments may collaborate with companies, which play a key role in mitigating CRM risks. The analysis in this chapter leads to six policy implications on which companies and governments must work: (i) guaranteeing a steady flow of capital to investment in CRM projects; (ii) developing new knowledge and skills; (iii) increasing transparency for the social acceptance of CRM projects; (iv) spurring targeted innovation programs; (v) cooperating across value chains and sectors, and partner countries and regions; and (vi) ensuring coherence with industrial and environmental policies.

title: Enhancement mechanism of corporate green investment efficiency from the perspective of group decision making
summary: Introduction Corporate green investment is a crucial initiative for promoting high-quality economic development. However, vague decision-making scenarios imply that large-scale green investment entails significant economic risks such as res
content: Introduction Corporate green investment is a crucial initiative for promoting high-quality economic development. However, vague decision-making scenarios imply that large-scale green investment entails significant economic risks such as resource misallocation and homogenized development. Methods This paper develops a theoretical framework grounded in collective intelligence and organizational information processing theories. Using a research sample comprising Chinese listed companies from 2010 to 2020, we conduct an empirical analysis employing fixed-effects models and system GMM estimators, and measure green investment efficiency using the Richardson model. Results We find that the impact of peer effects on green investment efficiency is conditional. Under conditions of effective information-processing capabilities, peer effects significantly reduce the degree of green investment inefficiency. Peer effects may influence investment efficiency through two pathways: "blind imitation" and “rational information learning”. Only the latter effectively improves resource allocation, and this enhancing effect primarily depends on the support of enterprises' internal information transparency, information acquisition capability, and information analysis capability. Heterogeneity analysis further reveals that followers' imitation of leading enterprises does not necessarily enhance efficiency: simple replication of green-investment-scale leaders yields no significant benefits, whereas learning from corporate social responsibility (CSR) leaders significantly optimizes investment efficiency. Discussion Moderation analysis indicates that enhancing information transparency, information acquisition capability, and information analysis capability significantly strengthens the positive impact of peer effects on green investment efficiency. From the dual perspectives of government regulation and corporate governance, we propose targeted policy recommendations for optimizing group decision-making regarding green investments and improving investment efficiency.

title: Eugenol-based derivatives as potential acetylcholinesterase-targeting biopesticides: an integrated in silico and in vitro study
source: Journal of the Saudi Society of Agricultural Sciences
summary: The extensive use of synthetic insecticides has raised concerns regarding environmental persistence, resistance development, and toxicity toward non-target organisms, necessitating the development of sustainable alternatives. Eugenol, a pla
content: The extensive use of synthetic insecticides has raised concerns regarding environmental persistence, resistance development, and toxicity toward non-target organisms, necessitating the development of sustainable alternatives. Eugenol, a plant-derived phenylpropanoid, is recognized for its insecticidal properties; however, its efficacy can be further improved through structural modification. In this study, a prediction-driven approach was employed to evaluate eugenol derivatives as acetylcholinesterase (AChE)-targeting biopesticides. Molecular docking revealed strong binding affinities within the AChE catalytic gorge, with eugenol valerate (–7.4 kcal·mol⁻¹) and eugenol isovalerate (–7.0 kcal·mol⁻¹) outperforming the reference insecticide malathion (–6.7 kcal·mol⁻¹). Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed the structural stability of the ligand–enzyme complexes. In vitro leaf exposure studies against Planococcus citri demonstrated rapid insecticidal activity, with eugenol achieving approximately threefold higher mortality than malathion within 24 h and complete mortality by 48 h. Despite exhibiting weaker AChE inhibitory potency than malathion in vitro, the rapid mortality induced by eugenol may be associated with favourable toxicokinetic properties, including efficient cuticular penetration, moderate lipophilicity, rapid membrane diffusion, and possible secondary neurophysiological effects beyond direct AChE inhibition. Additionally, AChE inhibition assays showed concentration-dependent inhibition, with eugenol exhibiting moderate inhibitory activity (IC₅₀ = 12.18 mM) compared to malathion (IC₅₀ = 2.25 mM). In silico ADME analysis indicated favourable physicochemical and environmental behaviour, including optimal lipophilicity, good aqueous solubility, high absorption potential, and compliance with pesticide-relevant property criteria without PAINS alerts, supporting their suitability as biopesticide candidates. Docking analysis indicated that eugenol derivatives interact with AChE mainly through non-covalent interactions within the catalytic gorge, which may differ from the irreversible inhibition mechanism associated with organophosphate insecticides. Structural modification through esterification may also contribute to improved physicochemical stability and residual activity relative to native eugenol. These findings highlight the potential of eugenol-based derivatives as environmentally compatible, AChE-targeting biopesticides for sustainable pest management. Graphical abstract

title: Sustainable and low-carbon removal of emerging contaminants by selective adsorption and phase-transferred electrocatalytic regeneration
summary: The sustainable management of trace emerging contaminants (ECs) is essential for safeguarding water resources and achieving global carbon-neutrality targets. To address the bottleneck of high energy-consumption and carbon emission caused by
content: The sustainable management of trace emerging contaminants (ECs) is essential for safeguarding water resources and achieving global carbon-neutrality targets. To address the bottleneck of high energy-consumption and carbon emission caused by the non-selective oxidation of complex organics in conventional advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), we report a sustainable and low-carbon process for ECs removal through a two-step strategy combining selective adsorption and phase-transferred electrocatalytic regeneration using a defect-engineered Fe-N-doped hierarchical porous carbon. Carboxylate-assisted defect modulation constructed hierarchical porosity and enriched pyridinic-N-Fe sites, which not only selectively captured high ionization potentials (IP) contaminants through charge-transfer-driven interactions, but also activated the cathodically generated H2O2 on Fe-N sites to produce •OH to fulfill electro-Fenton (EF) regeneration, restoring over 90% of adsorption capacity without any oxidant addition or pH adjustment. Taking sulfamethoxazole (SMX) as sample EC, the continuous run of the process majority removed SMX with an ultra-low energy consumption (0.034 kWh log−1 m−3) that was only 4.6% and 2.1% of homogeneous EF and electro-oxidation, respectively, while the CO2 emissions reduced by 96.9-99.4% compared with conventional AOPs. Our approach achieves trace ECs purification through a reagent-minimized, cyclic adsorption-regeneration pathway, offering a more energy-efficient and cleaner alternative to conventional oxidation systems and opening new opportunities for sustainable and low-carbon water treatment. This study presents a sustainable, low-carbon strategy that removes emerging contaminants from water through selective adsorption and phase-transferred electrocatalytic regeneration, reducing energy use and carbon emissions.

title: Optimisation of fermentation conditions for cell growth of recombinant Lactococcus lactis ATCC11454-ldhΔnisRKOE using response surface methodology
summary: Food safety and shelf-life preservation remain major challenges in agroindustry due to the increasing prevalence of foodborne pathogens and the growing demand for natural alternatives to synthetic preservatives. Recombinant lactic acid bact
content: Food safety and shelf-life preservation remain major challenges in agroindustry due to the increasing prevalence of foodborne pathogens and the growing demand for natural alternatives to synthetic preservatives. Recombinant lactic acid bacteria capable of producing antimicrobial peptides have emerged as promising candidates for sustainable biopreservative development. In this study, a sequential Design of Experiment (DoE) approach was applied to optimise cell growth of recombinant Lactococcus lactis ATCC11454-ldhΔnisRKOE, a metabolically engineered strain developed for enhanced nisin biosynthesis and antimicrobial activity. A 12-run Plackett–Burman Design (PBD) was first employed to screen six fermentation variables, followed by a 20-run Central Composite Design (CCD) based on Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to optimise the significant factors. The PBD identified fermentation time, temperature, and initial cell density as influential factors for subsequent optimisation. The quadratic CCD model was statistically significant (p = 0.010), with an R² value of 81.45% and a non-significant lack-of-fit (p = 0.073), indicating an adequate fit to the experimental data. In the final reduced model, fermentation time and the quadratic effect of temperature significantly influenced cell growth (p < 0.05), whereas initial cell density showed a positive trend but did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.058). The optimum conditions predicted by the model were 2% inoculum density, 30°C fermentation temperature, and 24 h fermentation time, producing an experimental OD600 value of 1.650 that remained within the 95% confidence and prediction intervals. The findings demonstrated that metabolic engineering significantly altered the growth characteristics and fermentation behaviour of the recombinant strain compared with the wild-type. The optimised conditions obtained in this study provide an important foundation for future scale-up fermentation and sustainable production of recombinant L. lactis-based natural biopreservatives for food and agroindustrial applications.

title: Connectivity as an economic idea: A critical conceptual review of neoliberalism, Chinese Statecraft and ASEAN hedging in Southeast Asia
source: Journal of Economic Epistemology and Philosophy
summary: "Connectivity" has become the organising objective of economic policy in Southeast Asia, invoked alike by China's Belt and Road Initiative, ASEAN's Master Plans on Connectivity, the European Union's Global Gateway and the Indo-Pacific strat
content: "Connectivity" has become the organising objective of economic policy in Southeast Asia, invoked alike by China's Belt and Road Initiative, ASEAN's Master Plans on Connectivity, the European Union's Global Gateway and the Indo-Pacific strategies of the United States and its partners. This article asks what conception of the economy the idea presupposes, how its rival programmes embody rival economic philosophies, and what its epistemic and moral consequences are. A critical conceptual review is conducted on a documented corpus of 86 Scopus-indexed publications retrieved on 9 September 2026, spanning international political economy, development studies, regionalism, urban studies and the digital economy, read through the philosophy of economics, political discourse theory, infrastructure studies and moral economy. Connectivity performs three philosophical operations: an ontological one, which pictures the economy as flows across a friction-laden space in which every "gap" is a deficit; an epistemic one, which converts political choices into technical problems and renders the concept an empty signifier that any programme may fill; and a normative one, which presupposes that integration is good while lacking a theory of how its gains and harms are distributed. The Chinese state-led and the Western rule-based models are read as consequentialist statism and proceduralist liberalism respectively, both variegated in practice by developmental-state legacies and zoning technologies. ASEAN hedging is reconstructed as a pragmatist epistemology of economic statecraft under Knightian uncertainty. The knowledge of infrastructural risk is shown to be co-produced by social forces rather than measured, and the harms of connectivity to fall on those least connected to its decisions. The article brings infrastructure into the philosophy of economics, offers the first systematic philosophical reading of the Southeast Asian connectivity literature, and proposes a research agenda for a normative and epistemological theory of economic integration. Keywords: connectivity; philosophy of economics; neoliberalism; Belt and Road Initiative; hedging; ASEAN; infrastructure; moral economy; political economy

title: From Grid to Chip: Power Architecture, Stability, and Flexibility of AI Data Centers
summary: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) computing is transforming data centers into large, dynamic electrical loads. Their deployment is primarily constrained by energy availability and grid-connection capacity, which is further ag
content: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) computing is transforming data centers into large, dynamic electrical loads. Their deployment is primarily constrained by energy availability and grid-connection capacity, which is further aggravated by the ability of power-delivery architectures, control systems, and computing workloads to operate reliably during fast grid disturbances. This article presents a technological perspective on AI data centers as grid-interactive computing systems. First, it reviews grid-integration bottlenecks, evolving connection policies, grid-code requirements, which has fostered new technological trends via spatio-temporal flexibility available through workload orchestration, cooling systems, on-site resources, and energy storage. Second, it maps the evolution of power-delivery architectures from medium-voltage grid interfaces to chip-level, discussing higher-voltage DC distribution, solid-state transformers, wide-bandgap devices, advanced chip-level power delivery, and liquid cooling. Third, it establishes a three-level stability framework spanning rack-level DC-bus dynamics, facility-level converter interactions, and system-level grid-coupled behavior. The framework connects dominant instability mechanisms, including constant power load effects, impedance interactions, forced oscillations, and operating-mode transitions, with suitable modeling, assessment, and mitigation approaches. Synthesizing these topics, this article highlights grid-to-chip co-design as a central requirement for scalable AI infrastructure, linking computing workloads, power-delivery systems, energy buffers, and grid operation.

title: Life Cycle Cost Assesment Pemanfaatan Biogas POME Untuk Energi Alternatif Menuju Dekarbonisasi Dan Keberlanjutan
summary: Limbah cair kelapa sawit atau dikenal dengan palm oil mill effluent (POME) menjadi sumber emisi yang berdampak terhadap lingkungan terutama pada gas rumah kaca, eutrofikasi asidifikasi. Namun, POME potensial dimanfaatkan sebagai energi baru
content: Limbah cair kelapa sawit atau dikenal dengan palm oil mill effluent (POME) menjadi sumber emisi yang berdampak terhadap lingkungan terutama pada gas rumah kaca, eutrofikasi asidifikasi. Namun, POME potensial dimanfaatkan sebagai energi baru terbarukan sekaligus menurunkan dampak lingkungan dengan memanfaatkan biogas dengan teknologi methane capture. Penelitian bertujuan menganalisis dampak ekonomi dan finansial dari pemanfaatan POME dalam 4 skema yaitu co-firing (skema 1), listrik (skema 2), bio CNG substitusi bensin (skema 3) dan bio CNG substitusi LPG (skema 4). Penelitian dilakukan pada 3 PKS di Riau berkapasitas 45-60 ton TBS/jam yang telah menerapkan teknologi pemanfaatan POME yang berbeda. Metode penelitian yang digunakan yaitu Life Cycle Cost Analysis (LCCA), Levelized cost (LC) dan analisis kelayakan finansial. Hasil menunjukan bahwa nilai LCCA yaitu Rp26,55 milyar (skema 1), Rp 81,84 milyar (skema 2), 253,10 milyar (skema 3), 165,25 milyar (Skema 4). LC untuk masing masing skema Rp. 42,06 /Mj, Rp 1.143,57/kWh, Rp 8.500,27/LSP, Rp 6.526,41 /kg. Sedangkan harga jual masing masing skema Rp 34,49/MJ,LC, Rp 1.444,70 per kWh, Rp 8.500,27/LSP ,Rp.4.500/LSP, Rp 6.526,41 /kg Berdasarkan nilai tersebut skema 2 dan 4 Layak secara LCCA namun untuk skema 1 dan 3 tidak layak secara LCCA. Analisis kelayakan finansial mengindikasikan bahwa hanya skema 3 yang tidak layak. Analisis sensitivitas menunjukkan kelayakan finansial dipengaruhi oleh kapasitas olah PKS, kandungan COD, konsentrasi POME, kandungan metana dan harga jual energi yang dihasilkan . Skema 1 merupakan opsi rendah karbon dan biaya untuk dekarbonisasi internal PKS, hal ini terkait tidak diperlukan infrastruktur baru untuk distribusi gas terkompresi. Pengembangan Bio-CNG lebih sesuai untuk substitusi bahan bakar eksternal dan strategi jangka panjang menuju carbon neutrality di sektor transportasi maupun industri untuk pengembangan energy baru terbarukan.

title: Atom–Cluster Synergy in Scalable Fe–Ru Dual‐Site Architectures Accelerates Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
summary: ABSTRACT Sluggish initial water dissociation (the Volmer step) severely limits alkaline water electrolysis. We report a highly scalable mechanochemical strategy to construct a dual‐site electrocatalyst, Ru NC @Fe 1 NC, that spatially decoup
content: ABSTRACT Sluggish initial water dissociation (the Volmer step) severely limits alkaline water electrolysis. We report a highly scalable mechanochemical strategy to construct a dual‐site electrocatalyst, Ru NC @Fe 1 NC, that spatially decouples water activation and hydrogen recombination. Harnessing the high‐energy impact of iron media and graphite, a solvent‐free mechanochemical process generates a defective carbon matrix anchoring isolated, oxophilic Fe single atoms (Fe 1 ), followed by the targeted deposition of ruthenium nanoclusters (Ru NC ). This atomic‐level division of catalytic labor fundamentally accelerates the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction. Ru NC @Fe 1 NC requires an overpotential of only 13.8 mV at 10 mA cm −2 with an ultralow Ru loading (∼2 wt%). In a practical anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE), this catalyst drives a current density of 1.0 A cm −2 at merely 1.66 V and sustains over 1100 h of continuous operation with negligible decay. Mechanistic studies—combining isotopic substitution, in situ Raman spectroscopy, time‐resolved hydrogen accumulation–stripping analysis, and density functional theory—reveal that the Fe 1 sites readily adsorb water and selectively lower the O–H cleavage barrier, rapidly feeding hydrogen intermediates to the adjacent Ru NC for efficient hydrogen desorption. This work establishes a robust blueprint for designing synergistic dual‐site architectures to circumvent kinetic bottlenecks in green hydrogen production.

title: Teleparallel torsion and white dwarf structure in f(T)=T+ΞT2 gravity
summary: We investigate how quadratic torsion modifies the equilibrium structure of white dwarfs in covariant f ( T ) = T + Ξ T 2 gravity. Static spherical configurations are calculated with a fixed equation of state for cold carbon matter, includin
content: We investigate how quadratic torsion modifies the equilibrium structure of white dwarfs in covariant f ( T ) = T + Ξ T 2 gravity. Static spherical configurations are calculated with a fixed equation of state for cold carbon matter, including relativistic electron degeneracy and Coulomb lattice corrections. The stellar interior is matched to a vacuum exterior, and the mass is determined from the asymptotic geometry. At fixed central density, negative couplings produce more massive and more compact configurations than general relativity, whereas positive couplings give smaller masses and larger radii. The deviations increase with central density and are more pronounced in mass than in radius. The first limiting feature of each sequence depends on the coupling. For Ξ = − 10 18 cm 2 , the sequence remains monotonic up to the electron capture density and reaches 1.508 M ⊙ . General relativity and Ξ = + 10 18 cm 2 instead reach mass turning points at 1.385 M ⊙ and 1.366 M ⊙ , respectively. The positive extreme can be continued as an equilibrium solution to the capture density, where its mass decreases to 1.24 M ⊙ , but this configuration lies beyond the turning point and is not the maximum mass along that sequence. These results identify a density dependent structural response to torsion that changes the stellar mass scale without modifying the matter equation of state.

title: Steric Tuning Enables Room‐Temperature Coordination Ionic Liquids for Zn‐Metal Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT The pursuit of high‐energy‐density batteries requires molten‐salt‐like electrolytes, but conventional systems often suffer from high viscosity or elevated operating temperature. Herein, we report a class of room‐temperature coordin
content: ABSTRACT The pursuit of high‐energy‐density batteries requires molten‐salt‐like electrolytes, but conventional systems often suffer from high viscosity or elevated operating temperature. Herein, we report a class of room‐temperature coordination ionic liquids (CILs) constructed through well‐defined coordination between Zn 2+ and pyridyl ligands. X‐ray single‐crystal diffraction demonstrates the stoichiometric formation of discrete [Zn(ligand) 4 ] 2+ in the solid state, while complementary spectroscopic analyses and theoretical simulations confirm similar coordination environments in the liquid state. Precise steric modification of pyridyl ligands, exemplified by 2,6‐dimethoxypyridine (DMOP), balances cation‐ligand coordination and cation‐anion electrostatic interactions to enable room‐temperature fluidity. The unique solvation structure facilitates charge‐transfer kinetics, promotes the formation of a stable solid‐electrolyte interphase, and suppresses side reactions. Consequently, the DMOP‐based CIL enables Zn/V 2 O 5 and Zn/NaV 3 O 8 ·1.5H 2 O full cells to cycle reversibly with excellent stability under harsh operating conditions. This work establishes steric control of coordination chemistry as an effective strategy for designing advanced liquid‐state complex electrolytes and extends the concept of solvate ionic liquids to divalent Zn‐based systems.

title: A large‐scale open‐source σ‐profile database for COSMO ‐ SAC
summary: Abstract We present an open‐source σ‐profile database encompassing 361,583 neutral organic molecules. The σ‐profiles were computed using density‐functional theory in the conductor‐screening limit with the open‐source PySCF package, using PM
content: Abstract We present an open‐source σ‐profile database encompassing 361,583 neutral organic molecules. The σ‐profiles were computed using density‐functional theory in the conductor‐screening limit with the open‐source PySCF package, using PM6‐optimized geometries from PubChemQC. This database is 162 times larger than the reference of Bell et al. (2261 molecules) and 6.8 times larger than CHAOS (53,091 molecules). To recalibrate COSMO‐SAC for PySCF‐derived σ‐profiles, we performed a sequential three‐stage reparametrization of the five exchange‐energy parameters using 24,522 infinite‐dilution activity coefficient data from the NIST/TRC ThermoData Engine. Validation across three independent benchmarks demonstrated accuracy comparable to the established DMol3‐based reference. The infinite‐dilution activity coefficient yielded an RMSE of 0.898 versus 0.961 on 9748 data points. Vapor–liquid equilibria showed a mean pressure deviation of 3.12% versus 3.92% on 12 binary systems. Solid–liquid equilibria produced an RMSE of 0.412 versus 0.458 on 22 solute–solvent pairs. The database, parameters, and code are openly available.

title: Carbon‐Based Electrodes for Sodium‐Ion Batteries: Material Design, Electrochemical Performance, and Challenges
summary: ABSTRACT Substantial energy storage systems are among the contemporary demands to fulfil the rising production of clean energy resources. Constant research is being done focusing on the advancement in energy storage technology to make it ef
content: ABSTRACT Substantial energy storage systems are among the contemporary demands to fulfil the rising production of clean energy resources. Constant research is being done focusing on the advancement in energy storage technology to make it efficient, economically feasible, and environmentally friendly. LIBs were the most often employed energy storage systems, but they suffer from hazardous environmental impact and costly, insufficient precursor material. SIBs have proven to be the finest substitute due to their cost‐effectiveness and vast material sources. But still widespread application of SIBs is hindered by the limitations of the electrode materials. The poor electrochemical performance, because of the wide ionic radius, has put a limit on the selection of efficient electrode materials. Among various electrode materials, carbon‐based electrodes are of strong interest due to their chemical stability, larger active area, and higher electrical conductivity. Therefore, this review focuses on graphite, graphene, CNTs, and their composites as carbon‐based electrode materials for SIBs. Hard carbon, an important practical carbon anode for SIBs, is briefly discussed for comparison. The influence of different material design strategies on the electrochemical performance of these electrodes is critically discussed in tabular comparison of their performance. A detailed analysis of the shortcomings of these materials alongside current research progress and their eco‐economic feasibility is described. Finally, future strategies are suggested to further enhance the large‐scale practical application of carbon‐based electrodes.

title: Transition to Sustainable Mobility Through the Lens of Policy Mixes:
source: Campos Neutrais - Revista Latino-Americana de Relações Internacionais
summary: The transition to sustainable mobility poses a major challenge for developing countries, as it requires the articulation of industrial, environmental, and innovation policies capable of promoting transport decarbonization and enhancing the
content: The transition to sustainable mobility poses a major challenge for developing countries, as it requires the articulation of industrial, environmental, and innovation policies capable of promoting transport decarbonization and enhancing the competitiveness of the automotive industry. This article analyzes the policy instruments adopted to promote the transition to sustainable mobility in the automotive industries of emerging economies through the experiences of Brazil and China. The study adopts a qualitative approach grounded in the policy mix framework, which conceptualizes public policy as a combination of multiple policy instruments designed to achieve governmental objectives. The central research question is: How do interactions among policy instruments shape the technological trajectories of decarbonization in the automotive industry? Drawing on the experiences, the paper examines the phenomenon of policy layering, characterized by incremental institutional change in which new elements are added to pre-existing arrangements. Based on a content analysis of primary and secondary sources, the findings indicate that the Brazilian automotive policy adopts a technology-neutral policy mix, in which decarbonization may be achieved through multiple solutions that contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions, with electromobility representing one of the possible technological pathways. In China, the most recent configuration of automotive policy is built around a mission-oriented policy mix aimed at achieving global leadership in electromobility, in which vehicle electrification constitutes the dominant technological pathway for transport decarbonization.

title: Tri‐Functional Electrocatalysis for Zinc–Air Battery Coupled Water Splitting: A Catalyst‐Electrode‐Device‐System Perspective
summary: Tri‑functional electrocatalysis is crucial for coupling rechargeable zinc‑air batteries with water splitting (WS), enabling self‑powered hydrogen production and versatile energy conversion. Although numerous catalysts demonstrate excellent
content: Tri‑functional electrocatalysis is crucial for coupling rechargeable zinc‑air batteries with water splitting (WS), enabling self‑powered hydrogen production and versatile energy conversion. Although numerous catalysts demonstrate excellent half-cell activities toward the hydrogen evolution reaction, oxygen evolution reaction, and oxygen reduction reaction, their practical application in battery-driven water electrolysis remains challenging. The major bottleneck is multiscale mismatch, which involves conflicting adsorption energetics at atomic sites, unstable gas‑liquid‑solid interfaces at electrodes, device degradation under alternating charge‑discharge and electrolysis modes, and voltage‑power imbalances at the system level. This review goes beyond conventional material summaries by constructing a catalyst-electrode-device-system framework to systematically examine how electronic modulation, defect engineering, heterostructure design, single-atom site tuning, and self-supported electrode construction influence intrinsic activity, mass transport, interfacial durability, and overall cell performance. Importantly, the actual operating point of the coupled system is determined by the intersection of the battery discharge curve and the electrolyzer polarization curve, rather than by isolated half‑cell metrics alone. Finally, we highlight future opportunities including operando characterization techniques, AI‑driven catalyst screening, standardized device evaluation protocols, and system-level co‑design for practical renewable energy devices.

title: Energy-aware and Sustainable Cloud Computing: Dynamic Scheduling, Pricing-Driven Resource Management, and Renewable Intermittency
summary: Data centers are now the largest users of electricity, carbon, and water, driving rapid cloud computing growth and a global shift to renewable-powered, sustainable cloud infrastructure. The large-scale integration of solar and wind energy c
content: Data centers are now the largest users of electricity, carbon, and water, driving rapid cloud computing growth and a global shift to renewable-powered, sustainable cloud infrastructure. The large-scale integration of solar and wind energy creates fundamental operational challenges due to their intermittency, uncertainty, and non-dispatchability. This paper presents dynamic energy-aware cloud computing as a pathway toward sustainability by modeling renewable variability with service reliability assurance aligned workload scheduling with forecast green energy availability. Recent advances in energy-and carbon-aware orchestration (2023-2025) have been reviewed where critically missing gaps are unified frameworks integrating renewable forecasting with stochastic robust optimization SLA aware scheduling plus demand-and supply-side contingencies like storage backup provisioning plus adaptive load management. Based on these gaps an elawful operations model for the co-optimization of power use carbon footprints quality of service under time-varying energy conditions is described that uses elastic resource management supported by probabilistic solar/wind forecasts plus risk-sensitive scheduling. New directions for more sustainable clouds include decentralized speculative renewables infrastructures; this paper also describes some concepts in that area. This work lays out a structured foundation toward next-generation green cloud platforms moving beyond static efficiency metrics into predictive reliability-driven environmentally responsive cloud operations.

title: Long-Term Probabilistic Load Forecasting Across Temporal Resolutions and Extreme Weather Conditions
source: Libraries and Cultural Resources (University of Calgary)
summary: This thesis examines the problem of producing long-term load forecasts that adequately represent tempo-ral detail, peak-demand behaviour, and uncertainty. Such forecasts support resource adequacy assessment, infrastructure development, and
content: This thesis examines the problem of producing long-term load forecasts that adequately represent tempo-ral detail, peak-demand behaviour, and uncertainty. Such forecasts support resource adequacy assessment, infrastructure development, and other long-term power-system planning decisions. However, forecasts devel-oped independently for different planning quantities may be inconsistent, while conventional approaches may not fully use information available at other temporal resolutions or adequately represent the effects of extreme weather. These challenges motivate the development of forecasting methods that integrate complementary sources of information without requiring increasingly complex underlying models. Before presenting the proposed methods, the thesis provides a foundations chapter covering long-term forecasting horizons and temporal resolutions, deterministic and probabilistic forecasting, ex-post and ex-ante evaluation, scenario-based uncertainty representation, forecast reconciliation, daily peak forecasting, and extreme-weather characterization. The first framework develops a multi-resolution forecasting approach based on temporal hierarchies. Forecasts are generated at hourly, daily, monthly, and annual resolutions and then reconciled to satisfy the temporal aggregation structure. The second framework uses independently generated daily peak forecasts to improve year-ahead hourly load trajectories. Bayesian updating combines alternative peak estimates, while optimization-based reconciliation transfers the updated peak information to the corresponding 8,760-hour forecast without changing its underlying chronological structure. The third framework addresses year-ahead probabilistic daily peak forecasting under extreme weather. Heat and cold events are characterized through their frequency, severity, and duration, and this information is used to construct peak-relevant predictors and generate event-based weather scenarios. The proposed methodologies are evaluated using electricity-demand data from the Alberta system and selected Alberta planning areas under both ex-post and ex-ante conditions. The findings show that informa-tion from different temporal resolutions, independently developed peak forecasts, and explicit representations of extreme-weather events can each improve different aspects of long-term forecasting. No single forecast-ing representation fully captures the temporal, peak-related, and uncertainty requirements of power-system planning. Instead, the results support a modular approach in which complementary information is incor-porated through transparent updating, reconciliation, and scenario-generation procedures to produce more coherent, accurate, and decision-relevant long-term load forecasts.

title: Nuclear baseload, fuel dependence, and long-run solar–wind integration in the EU electricity mix
summary: This paper examines the long-run system conditions that shape solar–wind integration in the EU electricity mix. Using annual data for 20 EU member states over 2000–2024, we estimate a panel Vector Error-Correction Model (VECM) to analyze th
content: This paper examines the long-run system conditions that shape solar–wind integration in the EU electricity mix. Using annual data for 20 EU member states over 2000–2024, we estimate a panel Vector Error-Correction Model (VECM) to analyze the joint evolution of solar–wind generation shares with fossil and nuclear generation shares, dependence on Russian oil and gas, energy efficiency, long-term interest rates, industrial production, and environmental taxes. Three findings stand out. First, higher nuclear generation shares are associated with persistently lower solar–wind shares, suggesting that inflexible baseload can constrain renewable integration. Second, greater dependence on Russian oil and gas is associated with lower solar–wind shares and higher fossil shares, indicating that legacy fuel linkages can slow electricity-system transition. Third, energy-efficiency improvements are linked to a rebound pattern in fossil generation, while their effect on solar–wind shares is weak in annual data. Overall, the results show that renewable integration depends not only on cost signals, but also on system flexibility, fuel dependence, and inherited power-system structures.

title: Plant‐Inspired Symbiotic Atmospheric Water Sorption–Evaporation for High Efficiency Adaptive Passive Cooling
summary: ABSTRACT Atmospheric water sorption–evaporation passive cooling couples two antagonistic processes, moisture harvesting and evaporative heat dissipation, whose intrinsic trade‐off hinders integrated system‐level design and limits stable ope
content: ABSTRACT Atmospheric water sorption–evaporation passive cooling couples two antagonistic processes, moisture harvesting and evaporative heat dissipation, whose intrinsic trade‐off hinders integrated system‐level design and limits stable operation under high heat fluxes. Inspired by the heat‐moisture regulatory strategies of tropical broadleaves and xerophytic plants, we develop a symbiotic atmospheric water sorption–evaporation (SAWSES) device that integrates a co‐designed valve‐channel‐interface cascade to orchestrate sorption, evaporation, and heat–mass transport. A thermo‐responsive P(NIPAM ‐co‐ AM)–LiCl hydrogel valve releases liquid water at elevated temperature and reabsorbs atmospheric moisture upon cooling, enabling reversible, bidirectional water transport. Tree‐like micro/nanostructured wicking interfaces drive rapid droplet‐to‐film transition for highly efficient thin‐film evaporation, while vapor‐permeable channels accelerate moisture uptake and expand the effective evaporating area. Together, SAWSES boosts moisture‐harvesting capacity by 27% and sustains high evaporation rates, achieving a 68°C temperature reduction under 6.8 kW/m 2 heat flux. Benchmarking against representative sorption–evaporation cooling materials, including polyethylene–hydrogel composites, MOFs, and PAM–salt hydrogels, SAWSES demonstrates superior temperature reduction while maintaining robust adaptive cooling under high thermal loads. This work establishes a plant‐inspired, self‐regulating thermal management strategy with strong potential for reliable deployment in adaptive passive cooling.

title: Enabling climate change action in cities: A systematic assessment of conditions
summary: Abstract Progress toward low-carbon, resilient cities remains a complex and evolving challenge. Enabling conditions, which are the institutional, economic, and social factors that shape the pace and depth of climate action, are central to u
content: Abstract Progress toward low-carbon, resilient cities remains a complex and evolving challenge. Enabling conditions, which are the institutional, economic, and social factors that shape the pace and depth of climate action, are central to understanding why some cities can advance more rapidly than others towards sustainable development pathways. While abundant technical and social response options exist, increasing the pace and scale at which these solutions are deployed in cities requires a nuanced and place-based understanding of these enabling conditions. Multiple enabling conditions influence the pace and depth of that progress, including dynamics of multi-level governance, both technical and non-technical capacities, policy and legal instruments, behaviour and values, and funding and finance. Drawing from a pool of over 120,000 scientific peer-reviewed articles, we quantitatively and qualitatively analyzed a subset of 261 articles to uncover patterns in enabling conditions and their relative influence on urban climate change action. We found that effective urban climate action relies on coordination and mutual support among institutional, economic, and social factors, although the specific setup varies by urban environment, geography, and sector. Urban climate action may accelerate when multi-stakeholder governance structures, aligned economic incentives, and inclusive community engagement converge and mutually reinforce one another. Governance structures at various scales emerge as a foundational enabler across the reviewed literature, though the specific arrangements vary considerably by context. Economic factors shape both the feasibility and scale of urban climate action, with financing mechanisms and cost-effectiveness considerations playing a prominent role, but appear to be insufficient without the presence of other enablers. The enablers we examined, including institutional, economic, and social factors, do not operate in isolation but interact through nexuses, sequential dependencies, and feedback loops. Policymakers and practitioners should strategically identify and invest in enablers that serve as leverage points for inclusive, innovative, and ambitious climate action in cities.

title: The Impact of Energy‐Consuming Right Trading Policy on Green Technology Innovation in China
summary: ABSTRACT China is committed to building the energy‐consuming right trading market. In this article, the impact of energy‐consuming right trading policy (ERTP) on green technology innovation (GTI) of Chinese manufacturing industry listed com
content: ABSTRACT China is committed to building the energy‐consuming right trading market. In this article, the impact of energy‐consuming right trading policy (ERTP) on green technology innovation (GTI) of Chinese manufacturing industry listed companies is evaluated. The results show that ERTP can significantly promote corporate GTI. ERTP could stimulate GTI of industrial enterprises, eastern enterprises, state‐owned enterprises, high‐productivity enterprises, and high‐migration costs enterprises. Tax incentives and the improvements of corporate environmental responsibility levels are important channels to promote GTI. ERTP triggers a ‘resource stacking effect’ on the basis of existing innovation activities. ERTP primarily triggers enterprise source GTI. ERTP mostly triggers substantive GTI other than strategic GTI. This article provides important empirical evidence for the improvement of China's energy‐consuming right trading system.

title: New estimates show the first decline in California’s organic share of cropland
summary: Building on the historic leadership of California farmers in organic agriculture, statewide climate mitigation goals include increasing organic production to 20% of all cropland by 2045. The focus on cropland reflects the increased opportun
content: Building on the historic leadership of California farmers in organic agriculture, statewide climate mitigation goals include increasing organic production to 20% of all cropland by 2045. The focus on cropland reflects the increased opportunity to reduce synthetic additives as compared to animal production. However, existing data limitations obscure the relative contribution of crops and animal agriculture to trends in organic production in California. Using anonymized data on organic production from the State Organic Program, the USDA Census of Agriculture, and California’s top organic certifier (CCOF), we developed statewide and county-level estimates of organic cropland and animal production. These estimates show a disproportionate growth of organic animal production over time, especially since 2014, and an overall drop in organic cropland acreage share in recent years. We estimate that only 4.5% of all California cropland is organic as of 2022. To meet the statewide organic target, policy changes are needed to restart the expansion of organic cropland. Further, improving State Organic Program data is critical for evaluating progress toward this goal.

title: Conversion of sodium carboxymethyl cellulose into N-doped porous carbon as efficient CO2 adsorbent
summary: Sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC-Na) is a cellulose derivative, and has extensive applications in different areas. In the current work, we utilized CMC-Na as carbon precursor to prepare N-doped porous carbons as efficient CO 2 adsorbents
content: Sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC-Na) is a cellulose derivative, and has extensive applications in different areas. In the current work, we utilized CMC-Na as carbon precursor to prepare N-doped porous carbons as efficient CO 2 adsorbents. CMC-Na was pyrolyzed with K 2 CO 3 and urea, which acted as the activator and nitrogen source, respectively. The obtained carbons exhibited highly porous structure, were successfully doped with nitrogen element. In particular, CMC2U700 demonstrated an impressively high specific surface area of 2564 m 2 /g. Effects of pyrolysis temperature and urea addition on the carbons’ physicochemical properties were studied with details. It was found that urea addition affected the activation process of K 2 CO 3 , and significantly enhanced the carbons’ porosity. A high CO 2 uptake of 18.82 mmol/g was achieved by CMC2U700 at 25 °C and 20 bar. The sample CMC0U800 also demonstrated excellent stability during cyclic adsorption measurements. Relationships between CO 2 adsorption performances and the carbons’ properties were then investigated. It was found that CO 2 uptakes at 1 bar and 20 bar correlated best with ultramicropore volume and specific surface area, respectively. Overall, the present work offers a perfect example for the conversion of CMC-Na into functional carbon materials for the field of carbon neutrality.

title: Advancing forest management modelling for next-generation Earth system models
summary: Managed forests occupy a large area of land, with almost 30% of the world’s forests designated primarily for production. Management can alter a forest’s carbon storage to a considerable extent, via tree species selection, planting and thinn
content: Managed forests occupy a large area of land, with almost 30% of the world’s forests designated primarily for production. Management can alter a forest’s carbon storage to a considerable extent, via tree species selection, planting and thinning density, selective logging, and wood harvesting. Forest management can also impact biophysical variables like canopy roughness, evapotranspiration, and surface albedo, which can produce strong effects on local warming or cooling. In addition, forest management is increasingly seen as a key component of many countries’ climate mitigation planning and a component of Net Zero targets. However, Earth System Models (ESMs) used to produce climate projections have historically contained limited functionality to represent processes relevant to forest management, meaning that the coupled-system consequences of these interventions remain underexplored. In recent years significant advances have been made to simulate forest management in dynamic global vegetation models (DGVMs) and land surface models (LSMs), the offline land surface components of ESMs. These include adding features to represent wood harvest; options to allow users additional control over forest plantation; plant functional types (PFTs) tuned specifically to represent common tree species used in forestry; and more detailed representation of forest demography (allowing for age- or size-specific growth, harvesting and mortality). In this paper, we summarize these developments and make the case for their usage in operational ESM configurations, so that the impacts of forest management on the climate, and the importance of forest management for climate mitigation, are properly represented in next generation climate projections.

title: Biomass-derived waste materials as an efficient electrocatalyst for the hydrogen evolution reaction
summary: Hydrogen is progressively recognized as a clean, carbon-neutral energy carrier capable of supporting sustainable energy schemes. Water electrolysis offers an effective route for hydrogen production; nevertheless, its efficiency is largely g
content: Hydrogen is progressively recognized as a clean, carbon-neutral energy carrier capable of supporting sustainable energy schemes. Water electrolysis offers an effective route for hydrogen production; nevertheless, its efficiency is largely governed by the catalytic performance of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). In this context, biomass waste has emerged as an abundant, low-cost, and renewable resource for the development of high-performance electrocatalysts, while at the same time addressing demanding waste management challenges. This review provides a comprehensive overview of HER mechanisms, biomass conversion techniques, catalyst synthesis strategies, and performance evaluation methods for waste-derived electrocatalysts. The electrocatalytic performance of various biomass-derived systems is associated with establishing structure-activity relationships. Despite significant progress, challenges remain, including limited intrinsic activity, stability issues, and scalability constraints. To address these limitations, future directions such as advanced catalyst design and sustainable synthesis strategies are proposed. These advancements are expected to encourage the development of efficient, low-cost, and environmentally friendly electrocatalysts for practical hydrogen production.

title: Biogenic silver nanoparticles from Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb. extract: Characterization and antibacterial potential in vitro and in silico
summary: Antimicrobial resistance is a major global health threat that compromises the effectiveness of conventional antibiotics. This study aimed to synthesize silver nanoparticles using Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb. rhizome ethanol extract (CX-AgNPs)
content: Antimicrobial resistance is a major global health threat that compromises the effectiveness of conventional antibiotics. This study aimed to synthesize silver nanoparticles using Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb. rhizome ethanol extract (CX-AgNPs) and evaluate their antibacterial properties. CX-AgNPs exhibited a surface plasmon resonance band at 417–430 nm, a hydrodynamic diameter of 247.3 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.364, and a zeta potential of –39.0 mV, consistent with substantial electrostatic colloidal stability. FTIR analysis suggested the involvement of extract-derived phytoconstituents in nanoparticle reduction and stabilization. FESEM and TEM analyses revealed predominantly spherical nanoparticles, while EDX detected 84.7% elemental silver and XRD analyses indicated a crystalline face-centered cubic structure. Antibacterial assessment by broth microdilution showed that CX-AgNPs had MIC values of 62.5–125 µg/mL against Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa . CX-AgNPs also inhibited biofilm formation by both bacterial strains in a concentration-dependent manner. Complementary docking and DFT analyses indicated that curcumin exhibited the most favorable computational profile, characterized by the highest predicted binding affinity, consistent reproduction of key crystallographic interactions, and favorable electronic responsiveness. Xanthorrhizol displayed comparatively greater electronic stability, whereas ar-turmerone exhibited receptor-dependent binding behavior. Overall, CX-AgNPs present strong potential as effective antibacterial agents.

title: A novel generator–condenser heat exchange coupled auto-cascade absorption refrigeration cycle for low-grade heat utilization
summary: To improve the thermodynamic performance of auto-cascade absorption refrigeration (ACAR) systems driven by low-grade heat, a generator–condenser heat exchange coupled cycle (GCX-ACAR) is proposed. It utilizes condensation heat from non-azeo
content: To improve the thermodynamic performance of auto-cascade absorption refrigeration (ACAR) systems driven by low-grade heat, a generator–condenser heat exchange coupled cycle (GCX-ACAR) is proposed. It utilizes condensation heat from non-azeotropic refrigerant mixtures at higher temperatures, enabling more effective internal heat recovery over a wider operating range. A thermodynamic model of the GCX-ACAR cycle is developed and validated, and the effects of key operating parameters, including high-side pressure, generation temperature, and absorption temperature, are systematically investigated. The results show that the new cycle significantly reduces generator heat input while maintaining comparable refrigeration capacity. A minimum refrigeration temperature of −105°C is achieved and the maximum coefficient of performance (COP) reaches 0.04, representing an improvement of 45%-114% compared with the conventional ACAR cycle. The enhanced performance is mainly attributed to the efficient utilization of temperature glide during the condensation process of non-azeotropic mixtures and the cascade recovery of condensation and rectification heat. The proposed cycle provides a promising pathway for improving the efficiency of low-grade heat-driven refrigeration systems and shows potential applications in LNG precooling and hydrogen liquefaction processes.

title: Why soil matters: The missing link in achieving sustainable development (A review and integrated framework)
summary: This narrative review synthesizes published evidence and proposes a conceptual framework that positions soil health as a cross-cutting element of sustainable development and the energy, water, and food nexus. Healthy soils connect and enabl
content: This narrative review synthesizes published evidence and proposes a conceptual framework that positions soil health as a cross-cutting element of sustainable development and the energy, water, and food nexus. Healthy soils connect and enable the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), yet no standalone soil-health indicator exists among the 231 official SDG indicators, and no soil-centered monitoring framework spans the goals. Drawing on historical examples of soil mismanagement leading to societal collapse and Indigenous practices demonstrating long-term stewardship, we propose an integrated framework with three strategic pillars: building climate-adaptive soils, creating synergies between productivity and conservation through regenerative and Indigenous knowledge, and restoring marginal soils through bioremediation. This framework embeds soil health as a cross-cutting indicator that fosters synergies rather than tradeoffs between SDG implementation. Sustainable development is difficult to achieve when soils are degraded, because soil underpins planetary health. We argue that the energy, water, and food challenges at the centre of the energy-water-food nexus depend on soil stewardship, and that redirecting policy, finance, and innovation toward soil health is essential to achieving net-zero, food security, and equitable resource use.

title: Amorphous Calcium Phosphate Maintains Casein Microarchitecture while Modulating Bacterial Growth Kinetics
summary: Casein, the primary source of protein in ruminant milk, represents a family of proteins that self-assemble into globules composed of finer spherical subunits and stabilized by calcium phosphate (CP) nanoparticles. These globules act as hold
content: Casein, the primary source of protein in ruminant milk, represents a family of proteins that self-assemble into globules composed of finer spherical subunits and stabilized by calcium phosphate (CP) nanoparticles. These globules act as holdase-type chaperones for unfolded or partially folded proteins, preventing their aggregation. Simultaneously, by integrating CP nanoparticles, they enable the bioavailability of calcium and phosphate beyond their solubility limits, thereby enhancing the nutritional value of milk. Using a range of physicochemical and biological characterization techniques, including scanning and transmission electron microscopy, organic and inorganic elemental analyses, SDS-PAGE, and vibrational, UV/Vis and NMR spectroscopies, it is demonstrated that native casein globules critically depend on CP nanoparticles for structural cohesion. Upon removal of the CP phase, the casein globules shrink, compromise their sphericity, and begin to disintegrate at both supramolecular and molecular levels. Concordantly, spectroscopic analyses revealed heightened stereochemical disorder in the microenvironments around spectrally active atoms or molecular groups following CP depletion, attesting to the gradual collapse of the casein structure. This structural collapse was also evident from the increase in the packing density of β-sheets induced by the removal of CP nanoparticles. CP nanoparticles within natural casein globules were furthermore confirmed to be structurally amorphous, lacking any long-range crystalline order. Additionally, demineralized casein delayed the growth of Escherichia coli, suggesting that casein-derived fragments generated during disintegration modulate bacterial physiology and growth behavior. The findings of the study open avenues for further research into casein-derived antimicrobial peptides and biomimetic designs that build upon protein-inorganic nanoparticle synergies for applications in drug delivery and beyond.

title: Integration of domestic wastewater and native Tetradesmus obliquus for bioremediation and production of biomass rich in protein and polyunsaturated fatty acids
summary: Abstract The large-scale deployment of microalgae-based bioprocesses is often limited by high freshwater and nutrient demands. Domestic wastewater represents a sustainable alternative, enabling simultaneous pollutant removal and biomass pro
content: Abstract The large-scale deployment of microalgae-based bioprocesses is often limited by high freshwater and nutrient demands. Domestic wastewater represents a sustainable alternative, enabling simultaneous pollutant removal and biomass production. In this study, a native strain of Tetradesmus obliquus , isolated in southern Brazil, was cultivated in raw domestic wastewater (RDW) and primary-treated domestic wastewater (TDW) at three initial inoculum densities (10%, 20%, and 30% v/v) for 14 days. Tetradesmus obliquus in TDW inoculated at 10% (v/v) removed 62.46% of ammonium and 98.56% of phosphate, simultaneously exhibiting the highest specific growth rate (0.16 d⁻ 1 ) and the highest biomass productivity (42.54 mg L⁻ 1 d⁻ 1 ). Iron and manganese concentrations decreased significantly with a native strain in TDW, indicating effective removal of them under the evaluated conditions. RDW was associated with higher carbohydrate accumulation (32.68%) and pigment production, whereas TDW was associated with higher protein content (45.83%) and a lipid fraction with a high relative proportion of polyunsaturated fatty acids (72.70–78.90%), primarily represented by α -linolenic and linoleic acids. The combined assessment of wastewater condition and initial inoculum density revealed distinct effects on the cultivation system. These aspects influence the biochemical composition of biomass, initial inoculum density, nutrient removal, specific growth rate, and biomass productivity. Thus, the present study supports the potential to integrate domestic wastewater treatment with the cultivation of a native Tetradesmus obliquus strain and indicates that, under the evaluated conditions, both the wastewater treatment conditions and the initial inoculum density influenced bioremediation performance and the biochemical composition of biomass.

title: From Molecular Crystals to Electronic Devices: Investigating Structure–Property Relationships of Iron(III) and Cobalt(II) Coordination Complexes
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
summary: Abstract Metal–organic semiconductors based on earth-abundant 3d transition metals offer great potential for optoelectronic devices, yet establishing direct structure–property relationships between specific supramolecular networks, electron
content: Abstract Metal–organic semiconductors based on earth-abundant 3d transition metals offer great potential for optoelectronic devices, yet establishing direct structure–property relationships between specific supramolecular networks, electronic structure, and charge transport remains a major challenge. In this work, we address this gap through a combined experimental and theoretical investigation of two new coordination complexes, [Fe(N3L1)(HN3L1)]Cl4.4(H2O) (complex 1) and [Co(HN3L1)(H2O)2Cl]Cl2.3(H2O) (complex 2), derived from the previously unexplored 4-imidazole-2,6-di(pyrazinyl)pyridine ligand. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals extensive supramolecular architectures stabilized by π···π stacking and hydrogen bonding involving lattice water molecules and chloride counterions. Hirshfeld surface analysis and 2D fingerprint plots quantify the dominant intermolecular contacts, while molecular electrostatic potential, Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules, and NCI plot calculations confirm significant anion···π and lone-pair···π interactions in the solid state. Optical absorption studies yield band gaps of 2.02 and 2.16 eV for complexes 1 and 2, respectively, positioning them for visible-light applications. Fabricated Schottky barrier diodes (ITO/sample/Au) demonstrate rectifying behavior, with device 1 exhibiting a rectification ratio of approximately 66 and a conductivity of 9.2 × 10–5 S m–1, outperforming device 2 (rectification ratio ∼17, conductivity 1.14 × 10–5 S m–1). Periodic DFT calculations reveal that the superior electrical performance of complex 1 stems from localized intra-gap states associated with the deprotonated imidazolyl moiety, which facilitate charge transport through hopping mechanisms. These findings elucidate the crucial role of molecular packing and ligand deprotonation in tuning charge transport in functional metal–organic materials.

title: Elementos normativos para el desarrollo de un mercado de combustibles renovables
summary: La descarbonización para alcanzar la neutralidad climática en 2050 requiere diversas soluciones tecnológicas, donde los combustibles renovables constituyen una pieza necesaria, especialmente en sectores difícilmente electrificables directam
content: La descarbonización para alcanzar la neutralidad climática en 2050 requiere diversas soluciones tecnológicas, donde los combustibles renovables constituyen una pieza necesaria, especialmente en sectores difícilmente electrificables directamente. La regulación y el desarrollo tecnológico son imprescindibles para reducir costes y fomentar el mercado de combustibles renovables. Sin embargo, la regulación puede incluir elementos que supongan barreras para las inversiones en combustibles renovables. Este artículo, a partir de un proceso de investigación cualitativa que combina la revisión de diversas fuentes bibliográficas y las aportaciones de un grupo de debate, presenta el contexto regulatorio en Europa y en España. A continuación, se presentan y analizan tres cuestiones genéricas (neutralidad tecnológica, flexibilidad normativa y cooperación regulatoria) y cuatro específicas de la regulación de los combustibles renovables (criterios de sostenibilidad, sunset clause del CO2 renovable, infraestructura e incentivos públicos), claves para su desarrollo. El documento concluye con una síntesis de las principales conclusiones.

title: When Innovation Meets Nature and Governance: A Conditional Path to Sustainable Development
summary: ABSTRACT Despite expanding global innovation capacity, countries with similar green innovation trajectories exhibit sharply divergent sustainable development goal (SDG) performance. Drawing on strong sustainability theory, economic complexi
content: ABSTRACT Despite expanding global innovation capacity, countries with similar green innovation trajectories exhibit sharply divergent sustainable development goal (SDG) performance. Drawing on strong sustainability theory, economic complexity theory and new institutional economics, this study develops a conditional sustainability framework in which ecological integrity and governance quality enhance the sustainability returns to green innovation. Using a balanced panel of 45 countries from 2000 to 2021 (990 observations), we apply CS‐ARDL estimation following cross‐sectional dependence, unit root, slope heterogeneity and cointegration tests, with CCEMG and AMG robustness checks. Results show that ecological integrity and governance quality exert positive long‐run effects on SDG performance, whereas green innovation alone has a statistically fragile direct effect. Crucially, ecological integrity × innovation and innovation × governance interactions are consistently positive and significant across estimators. Green innovation therefore generates stronger sustainability returns when supported by robust ecological systems and effective institutional governance.

title: The role of epistemic and normative similarity in inter-organizational online relations: a self-categorization perspective on the bioplastics field
summary: Sustainability transitions unfold through the interactions of heterogeneous actors, yet the discursive mechanisms that structure inter-organizational affiliation remain poorly understood. This study examines whether organizations' publicly
content: Sustainability transitions unfold through the interactions of heterogeneous actors, yet the discursive mechanisms that structure inter-organizational affiliation remain poorly understood. This study examines whether organizations' publicly articulated epistemic and normative positioning is associated with the formation of inter-organizational ties and the emergence of coherent relational communities in the bioplastics field. Drawing on self-categorization theory, we advance a multilevel perspective in which organizations are treated as socially recognizable collective actors whose public positions provide categorical cues for affiliation, community formation, and differentiation. Conceptualizing epistemic and normative similarity as two dimensions of symbolic proximity, this perspective extends proximity-based accounts of inter-organizational relations by linking dyadic similarity to the emergence of internally coherent and comparatively differentiated communities. We reconstruct a hyperlink network of 4161 organizations across all world macro-regions, connected by 28,151 hyperlink ties, and derive their epistemic and normative positioning from web content using a transformer-based topic model and an automated UN SDG classifier. Dyadic logistic regression shows that epistemic and normative similarity positively predict tie formation, net of geographical, institutional, and social proximity, with a significant positive interaction between the two dimensions. At the community level, OLS regression and permutation tests show that greater relational density is associated both with higher internal epistemic and normative coherence within communities and with stronger differentiation from other communities in the field. These findings suggest that the relational architecture of sustainability transitions is partly constituted by the symbolic positioning organizations publicly display, shaping how coordination, fragmentation, and transition governance unfold across heterogeneous organizational fields.

title: Evaluating Sustainable Building Practices for Carbon Reduction in Nigerian Housing
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF GEOGRAPHY AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT
summary: Sustainable building materials play a crucial role in reducing the carbon footprint of the housing sector, which is significant in Nigeria due to rapid urbanisation and increasing housing demands. This study provides a comprehensive narrati
content: Sustainable building materials play a crucial role in reducing the carbon footprint of the housing sector, which is significant in Nigeria due to rapid urbanisation and increasing housing demands. This study provides a comprehensive narrative review of 60 published journal articles from 2010 to 2023, focusing on identifying, evaluating, and applying sustainable building materials for low-carbon housing in Nigeria. The review method critically analyses existing literature to highlight the most effective materials and techniques contributing to carbon reduction. Findings reveal that materials such as bamboo, recycled concrete, and earth-based materials show promise in achieving sustainability goals.
